concepts.name: Goldfeld’s theorem (Euler product at s = 1 ⇒ RH, analytic order)
concepts.plain: If the partial Euler product of L(E,s) at the centre behaves like C/(log x)^r, then L(E,s) satisfies RH and r is the analytic order of vanishing — with a surprising √2 in the constant.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: If ∏_{p≤x} L_p(E,1) ∼ C/(log x)^r then L(E,s) satisfies RH, r = ord_{s=1}L(E,s), C = L^{(r)}(E,1)/(r! √2 e^{rγ}) (Goldfeld 1982, cited via Conrad 2005; TAA Lemma 140).
pitfalls: It gives the analytic order, not the rank (rank = order is BSD).
a_p are not BSD generators.
Note the √2 factor (Conrad).
Finite products (±10% oscillation to 1e7) are not evidence for RH (TAA Lemma 150, correction 10).

rels.note: prime data vs the reference at s = 1

concepts.name: ℤ̂ in the dictionary: Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂; ℚ⧵𝔸 ≅ (ℝ × ℤ̂)/ℤ; C_ℚ ≅ ℝ₊* × ℤ̂*
concepts.plain: The profinite integers are where all the finite primes live in the adelic picture. They are not the analogue of Frobenius over ℚ (that is the real scaling flow); they give the totally disconnected direction and the Dirichlet-character sectors, and DH sits in no single sector.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C] Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂ (Frobenius generates the dense ℤ); ℤ̂ = ∏ℤ_p, dual ℚ/ℤ; 𝔸_ℚ ≅ ℝ × (ℤ̂⊗ℚ) (Wikipedia, opened). [T] ℚ + (ℝ × ℤ̂) = 𝔸_ℚ and ℚ ∩ (ℝ × ℤ̂) = ℤ ⇒ ℚ⧵𝔸_ℚ ≅ (ℝ × ℤ̂)/ℤ, the adelic solenoid (leaves ℝ, transversal ℤ̂; Den05's S¹_p = ℝ ×_ℤ ℤ_p is the one-prime case, opened). [T] class number 1 + ℤ^× = {±1}: C_ℚ = ℚ^×⧵𝔸^× ≅ ℝ₊* × ℤ̂*. [C] Connes 1999 (20)–(21): C_k ≅ K × N, N = ℝ₊* (number fields) vs q^ℤ (function fields); H = ⊕_χ H_χ over characters of K. Dictionary: over ℚ the Frobenius role goes to ℝ₊* (the flow), not to ℤ̂; ℤ̂ carries the finite primes (transversal), ℤ̂* the Dirichlet-character sectors. [T,N] DH = ½(1−iκ)L(s,χ) + ½(1+iκ)L(s,χ̄), χ mod 5 (residual 0): a sum of two sectors, in no single one; a(2)a(3) = −0.0807 ≠ a(6) = 1. Wikipedia's line 𝔸^×/ℚ^× ≅ (ℝ×ℤ̂)/ℤ conflates the additive quotient: not used.
pitfalls: ℤ̂ ≠ the Frobenius group over ℚ: Connes N = ℝ₊*.
Sector exclusion of DH is structural, not a sign: GRH per sector remains open.

concepts.name: Trace part = polarization (projection onto span{h,v}, ample ω = h + v, ω² = 2), positivity = definiteness of the primitive part relative to it; together = Hodge index on E×E (primitive Gram [[−2,−a],[−a,−2q]] definite ⇔ a² < 4q)
concepts.plain: Split each class into the part along the two fibre directions and the rest. The first part is the polarization. Positivity means the rest is definite, and that only makes sense relative to the polarization. The two together are the Hodge index theorem, which is Weil's proof of RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Trace part = polarization (projection onto span{h,v}, ample ω = h + v, ω² = 2), positivity = definiteness of the primitive part relative to it; together = Hodge index on E×E (primitive Gram [[−2,−a],[−a,−2q]] definite ⇔ a² < 4q)
numbers: h − v complement indefinite even for real curves
pitfalls: The trace-free part alone is not positivity. The flowed primitive form is definite iff t > Λ_p (formal).

concepts.name: Hermite form counts ghosts in a window
concepts.plain: The quadratic form sum_k q(z_k)^2 over the zeros in a window, built from contour moments, is positive definite exactly when those zeros are real; its number of negative directions is the number of off-line pairs. It flagged every ghost over its whole pre-landing era and nothing in any real-rooted window. It is a local positivity of Weil type with polynomial-square tests.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hermite form counts ghosts in a window. Sources: Hermite quadratic form (classical root counting).
concepts.formula: H_ij = (1/2 pi i) oint T_i(u) T_j(u) H_t'/H_t dz; #neg(H) = #non-real pairs
numbers: route score: 4.4 (0.6·significance + 0.4·probability of progress, 0–10); significance 4, probability 5
pitfalls: Exact because it counts off-line zeros in the window: for ζ, a zero negative count in every window at every height is RH restated; the non-circular use is as a zero-free barrier certificate (Polymath15-type), which bounds Λ from above.

concepts.name: Cole–Hopf: Ψ = H′/H obeys backward Burgers ∂_tΨ = −Ψ″ − 2ΨΨ′; at one prime the Toeplitz sequence 2T_k(x_t) is positive-definite iff t ≥ Λ_p; product cross-term −2tΨ_pΨ_q
concepts.plain: The log-derivative side of the flow is a Burgers equation. At one prime its time-t positivity switches on exactly at the local Newman time. For products the primes couple at first order through a product of their log-derivatives.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Cole–Hopf: Ψ = H′/H obeys backward Burgers ∂_tΨ = −Ψ″ − 2ΨΨ′; at one prime the Toeplitz sequence 2T_k(x_t) is positive-definite iff t ≥ Λ_p; product cross-term −2tΨ_pΨ_q

concepts.name: Hasse bound as a positive degree form
aliases: Q_p = x² + a_p xy + p y²
concepts.plain: For an elliptic curve the degree of an endomorphism is a positive quadratic form; Hasse’s bound is that this form is positive (Cauchy–Schwarz / Pythagoras).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: deg(m + nπ) = m² + amn + qn² is PD ⇔ a² < 4q; Hasse = Cauchy–Schwarz. Ghost a = 25, q = 101: deg(10 − π) = −49 (TAA Lemma 106).
concepts.formula: m² + a mn + q n² > 0 ⇔ a² < 4q

concepts.name: The Bochner–Kodaira–Nakano curvature of yᵏ|F|² is k/y² for every holomorphic F (θ, θ_χ₋₄, θ_DH and random coefficients agree to 1.6e−4): it is Γ-factor data (k = 2a) and is positive for Davenport–Heilbronn too
concepts.plain: The Bochner–Kodaira–Nakano curvature of yᵏ|F|² is k/y² for every holomorphic F (θ, θ_χ₋₄, θ_DH and random coefficients agree to 1.6e−4): it is Γ-factor data (k = 2a) and is positive for Davenport–Heilbronn too. [Theorem]

concepts.name: Inertia of a compressed Weil form gives 2/3 on the line
concepts.plain: A rank–trace inequality on a finite compression of the Weil hermitian form, with Sylvester inertia counting off-line pairs as negative squares, makes Montgomery's simple-zero argument unconditional: at least 2/3 of zeros are simple and on the line (preprint, Lean-formalized by its authors).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Inertia of a compressed Weil form gives 2/3 on the line. Sources: arXiv:2608.13637.
concepts.uncertain: preprint, unrefereed

concepts.name: Coupled coils: the Frobenius norm form is a two-coil energy with coupling k = |a_p|/2√p; Hasse ⇔ k ≤ 1; one-factor Laguerre margin 4 log²p (1 − k)
concepts.plain: The quadratic form m² − a mn + p n² is the energy of two coupled inductors. It is never negative exactly when the coupling coefficient is at most one, which is the Hasse bound. A perfect transformer (k = 1) is the cusp; k > 1 would need an active element.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Coupled coils: the Frobenius norm form is a two-coil energy with coupling k = |a_p|/2√p; Hasse ⇔ k ≤ 1; one-factor Laguerre margin 4 log²p (1 − k)
concepts.formula: k_p = |a_p|/(2√p) = |cos θ_p|; Λ_p = log k_p / log²p; min_u (f′² − f f″) = 4 log²p (1 − k_p) for f = 2cos(u log p) − a/√p

concepts.name: Epstein zeta no-go
concepts.plain: Epstein zeta functions of binary quadratic forms have a functional equation but no Euler product, and they have zeros off the line — the classic counterexample class next to DH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 83: Epstein x² + 5y² = ζL(χ₋₂₀) + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅); N(200) = 253 zeros, 183 on the line (70 off-line); first off-line 0.93297 + 15.66825i. TAA Lemma 135: 46 zeros with ½ < σ < 1 for t ≤ 250; control x² + y² (= 4ζL(χ₋₄), has Euler product): 0. TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion and FE hold, unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 153 (G, CM points): Σ′(m²+n²)^{−s} = 4ζ(s)L(s,χ₋₄) (NUM s = 3: 4.6589136156); Σ′(m²+mn+n²)^{−s} = 6ζ(s)L(s,χ₋₃) (6.3758815528); x²+5y²: ζ_K + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), 2x²+2xy+3y²: ζ_K − L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), sum over the class group = 2ζ_K (Euler product restored, Hecke; NUM to 1e−12). Off-line zero refined: 0.9329696975 + 15.6682495313i (|Z| = 3e−21; ζ_K there 0.933). CM points are where one restricts (toric periods), not a quotient (TAA Lemma 153, correction 22). TAA Lemma 164 (merged here; the delta proposed a separate positive-ghost entry): Z_Q = ζL(χ₋₂₀) + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅) (genus theory, checked n ≤ 300) has non-negative integer multiplicities (a Gibbs/KMS system with H = log Q(m,n)), the functional equation and Bochner positivity, yet zeros with ½ < Re ρ < 1, so KMS/thermal/partition-function positivity does not force RH; r_Q(2)r_Q(3) = 0 ≠ r_Q(6) = 4 (a sum of two Euler products, like DH). Davenport–Heilbronn 1936: infinitely many zeros in σ > 1 (cited). TAA Lemma 164 Krawczyk-certified 52 zeros with Re ρ ≥ 0.52, t < 400 (max Re 0.9549; mpmath |Z_Q(ρ₁)| = 2.8e−15). Correction (Missing Piece v5, I16): the 52 is a lower bound, not a census, because TAA Lemma 164's scan grid starts at σ = 0.52 (TAA Lemma 135 already found 46 zeros with ½ < σ < 1 for t ≤ 250, against 38 in TAA Lemma 164's list there); and the ghost is not new: it is this entry (TAA Lemma 83, TAA Lemma 135, TAA Lemma 138, TAA Lemma 153, TAA Lemma 159). TAA Lemma 164 adds the KMS/Bochner reading and the certification.

TAA Lemma 169: truncated Weil test h = 0.025: onset 3.0 (kerP 3.175, no pole 1.05); index 32 at W = 7.9; ζ_K control passes to W = 8
TAA Lemma 174: counting θ̂ ≈ 0.32; composite share of |c(n)| 0.921; ψ slope 0.92 (max Re 0.955)

concepts.name: de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ
concepts.plain: Heat flow on ξ; Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao), RH ⇔ Λ = 0.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable (TAA Lemma 111). Healing times TAA Lemma 124/TAA Lemma 136 conflict. TAA Lemma 150 (opened): Rodgers–Tao Λ ≥ 0 (Forum Math Pi 2020), Polymath 15 Λ ≤ 0.22; H_0(z) = Ξ(z/2)/8, so t_RT = 4·t_Ξ (TAA Lemma 150, correction 8). DH heuristic (truncated list): pair at 85.70 closes at t_RT ≈ 0.177 (isolated 2δ² = 0.190); does not separate DH from ζ's known range. TAA Lemma 158: H_t = ∫e^{tu²}Φ(u)cos(zu)du solves the BACKWARD heat equation ∂_tH = −∂_zzH (Rodgers–Tao, Polymath, opened); increasing t (= exp(−tD²), anti-dissipative) makes zeros real (Pólya); the dissipative (forward-heat) direction t ↓ creates collisions and complex pairs. RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0; Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao, Forum Math Pi 2020); Λ ≤ ½ (de Bruijn 1950); −∞ < Λ (Newman 1976); Λ ≤ 0.22 (Polymath). Toy exp(−tD²)(z²−1)(z²−1.6²): Λ_toy = −0.0463. F/V merge = 𝔽_q picture of the collision (Analogy, fv_merge_trichotomy). TAA Lemma 159: Newman–Wu 2019 (opened): the 1976 theorem's motivation came 'more by statistical physics and Euclidean field theory … than by analytic number theory'; Lee–Yang property of Φ is the precise Lee–Yang form of RH (lee_yang_fisher_rh). TAA Lemma 160: direction stated explicitly (RT convention ∂_t H = −∂_zz H; increasing t makes zeros real; collisions come from lowering t); RH ⇔ Λ = 0; under RH with simple zeros the forced collisions escape every compact set as t → 0⁻ (dbn_parabolic_threshold). Newman 1976 is Proc. AMS 61, 245–251 (AMS DOI record; TAA Lemma 158 had 246). L180: local flow = F/V sweep; Λ_p = ACM Lemma 3.18 (t_ACM = t log²p, t_RT = 4t); product cross-term explicit; Λ_global = 0 for incommensurable Hasse products (Heuristic/Numerical).
pitfalls: t* = 2δ² vs δ²/2.

Correction (v1.15): Newman 1976 (Proc. AMS 61) classifies the class 𝒫 and shows Φ ∉ 𝒫; it does not state RH ⇔ Lee–Yang for Φ, and no theorem states it for all ferromagnetic J ≥ 0. The single-spin Lee–Yang property of Φ (all zeros of ∫Φ(u)e^{hu}du = ¼ξ(½+h/2) on iℝ) is a Restatement of RH; by continuity at J → 0 the many-spin ferromagnetic version fails exactly when the single-spin one does, so it adds no information (see multispin_adds_nothing).

concepts.name: Two walls: the parabolic (signature) wall and the Routh (Krein-collision) wall; RH = ζ never reaches the first
concepts.plain: Every positivity failure in the dictionary is a collision, of one of two kinds. The parabolic (signature) wall is a one-mode collision of a conjugate pair on the real axis: a² = 4q over 𝔽_q (Hasse), Kepler’s E = 0, a Levinson step with |k| = 1, a Hodge–Riemann signature change, and along the support filtration the Weil radius L*. RH ⇔ ζ never reaches it (L* = ∞; Weil) [Restatement]. The Routh wall is a collision of two different modes of opposite Krein sign off the real axis (Hamiltonian–Hopf; at L4 μ_R = ½(1 − √(23/27)) = 0.0385209, ω = 1/√2). It needs a Krein-negative mode, so it lies downstream: RH ⇒ ζ never reaches any Routh wall (Krein’s theorem plus Weil’s criterion) [Theorem]. The converse fails at finite L: Davenport–Heilbronn crosses the parabolic wall at L* ≈ 3.6–3.9 (depending on the resolution), then sits in an L4-like window (energy indefinite, every pencil mode still elliptic, one Krein-negative pair), and shows Hamiltonian–Hopf quartets from L_H ≈ 4.3–4.8 on (4.263 at h = 0.0125, 4.775 at h = 0.025; quartets at 18 of 27 grid points up to L = 8). ζ shows none of this for L ≤ 8 [Numerical]. Over 𝔽_q in genus 1 the two walls coincide.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Two walls: the parabolic (signature) wall and the Routh (Krein-collision) wall; RH = ζ never reaches the first.
numbers: Weil-pencil census, L ∈ [3, 8]: ζ 0 Krein-negative modes, 0 real pairs, 0 quartets (41 cutoffs); Davenport–Heilbronn real pair at L = 3.875 (h = 0.025), Krein-negative pair present at 3.763 (h = 0.0125), first quartet 4.775 / 4.263

dense-band conjecture: any Krein-negative mode collides with a Krein-positive neighbour within about one level spacing as L → ∞ (collision distance / spacing 0.09–1.29 at 23 grid points) [Conjecture 2.6]; if true for the whole class, “never a Routh wall at any L” ⇔ RH

v1.11: the Routh wall is unreachable under a Rosati-type (Krein-definite) polarization by Krein–Gelfand–Lidskii; Davenport–Heilbronn’s parabolic crossing L* = 3.875 is the birth of a cap of the forbidden set and the neck opens at 4.025 (Hamiltonian–Krein index, 212/212) [Theorem + Numerical]

L_H moves with the resolution (4.78 → 4.26 as h halves); the h → 0 limit is open.

Correction (v1.14): Davenport–Heilbronn’s first Weil-window crossings move to L ≈ 3.63 (even) / 3.65 (odd) on fine bases (fine grid M = 320; h = 0.0083), and the second pair to ≈ 4.19/4.21 (h = 0.0083); the values 3.80–3.925 (and 6.3–7.4 for the second pair) quoted here are basis values at h = 0.025 or coarser, where the hat factor s(γh)⁴ attenuates the ghost ordinate. The qualitative statements are unchanged; see dh_crossing_basis_dependence.

v1.20. This parabolic wall and the Routh wall stay distinct from each other, from the Beurling-pencil Hasse wall, and from the primary and secondary sheets of Sigma. The model null conic in the v1.20 polarity figure is a discriminant boundary of that model. It is not captioned as either of these walls.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian–Krein index for the Weil pencil: n₋ = N_real + 2N_quart + 2N_Krein−, so positivity is stability plus Krein-definiteness (grading Γ = 1)
concepts.plain: For the scaling pencil D v̇ = Z_L v, with D the invertible skew scaling generator, the Hamiltonian–Krein index theorem (Kapitula–Kevrekidis–Sandstede 2004; Pelinovsky 2005) equates the signature of the Weil form with the spectral data: n₋(Z_L) = N_real + 2N_quart + 2N_Krein− (real pairs, Hamiltonian–Hopf quartets, Krein-negative elliptic pairs). The identity holds at 212/212 pencils (ζ, Davenport–Heilbronn, L(11a) and a hybrid, 53 support lengths each, h = 0.025). Hence Z_L ≥ 0 exactly when there is no real pair, no quartet and no Krein-negative pair: positivity is Krein-definiteness, the trivial grading Γ = 1, and not merely the existence of some grading (a non-trivial one exists for Davenport–Heilbronn on L ∈ [4.025, 4.625], where it is elliptic). This corrects the v1.10 statement “P = ZΓ positive for some Γ”. As an RH criterion it is circular (it is Z_L ≥ 0); its content is the exact accounting between the potential (Jacobi) half and the symplectic (Legendre) half.

concepts.name: Lee–Yang vs Fisher zeros; single-spin Lee–Yang property of Φ ⇔ RH (Restatement) ⇔ Λ ≤ 0
concepts.plain: Lee and Yang proved that ferromagnets have their partition-function zeros on a circle. ζ's zeros are zeros in temperature (Fisher zeros), not in field; the exact Lee–Yang-type statement for ζ is the de Bruijn–Newman one, which is RH itself.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: [C] Lee–Yang (1952): ferromagnetic Ising, zeros in the fugacity z = e^{−2βh} on |z| = 1; Newman 1974 extension (Newman–Wu 2019 Thm 11, opened); Lee–Yang zeros (field) vs Fisher zeros (temperature) (Wikipedia 'Lee–Yang theory', opened). [N] 3-spin toy: ferromagnet J = 0.4 zeros |z| = 1, 1, 1; antiferromagnet J = −0.4: 13.79, 1.00, 0.0725. [T] Truncated Euler products have no zeros in any prime fugacity: ζ zeros are Fisher zeros of the Bost–Connes continuation, not Lee–Yang zeros (TAA Lemma 124). [C/R] Precise Lee–Yang form: Newman–Wu Thm 9 (de Bruijn 1950, Newman 1976): H_λ has only real zeros iff λ ≥ Λ; RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0; Rodgers–Tao Λ ≥ 0; Polymath Λ ≤ 0.22. NW19: the 1976 result's 'original motivation was provided more by statistical physics and Euclidean field theory … than by analytic number theory'. e^{λt²} weighting = Gaussian (ferromagnetic-type) tilt; increasing λ = backward heat (TAA Lemma 158, correction 16). L180: Newman 1976 (opened) proves the classification of the class 𝒫 and Φ ∉ 𝒫 unconditionally (so b₀ < ∞), and states RH as b₀ ≥ 0. It does not state 'RH ⇔ Φ Lee–Yang'. The single-spin form is a direct Restatement; the many-spin ferromagnetic form adds no information (v1.15 correction). ζ zeros are Fisher-type (temperature) zeros of the Bost–Connes continuation at Re β = ½, beyond the transition at β = 1; finite truncations have zeros off the line.
pitfalls: ζ zeros are Fisher, not Lee–Yang, zeros (TAA Lemma 159, correction 5).
Lee–Yang 1952 originals not opened (via Newman–Wu, Wikipedia).

Correction (v1.15): Newman 1976 (Proc. AMS 61) classifies the class 𝒫 and shows Φ ∉ 𝒫; it does not state RH ⇔ Lee–Yang for Φ, and no theorem states it for all ferromagnetic J ≥ 0. The single-spin Lee–Yang property of Φ (all zeros of ∫Φ(u)e^{hu}du = ¼ξ(½+h/2) on iℝ) is a Restatement of RH; by continuity at J → 0 the many-spin ferromagnetic version fails exactly when the single-spin one does, so it adds no information (see multispin_adds_nothing).

concepts.name: Arithmetic unitarity ("RH = unitarity")
concepts.plain: TAA’s founding claim made precise: the scaling flow is always an isometry of the Weil form; RH is the statement that this form is positive, so the flow is genuinely unitary.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1: (ii) T_t is a 𝒬-isometry unconditionally; (iii) growth exponent = Θ − ½; (iv) RH ⇔ 𝒬 ≥ 0 ⇔ unitary Hilbert realization ⇔ bounded matrix coefficients.
pitfalls: Isometry is free (Ax3-like); positivity of the form is the content (Ax2).

concepts.name: Λ = 0 (⇔ RH, given Rodgers–Tao) puts ζ at the parabolic threshold of the de Bruijn–Newman family — at infinity: with simple zeros, forced collisions for t < 0 escape every compact set
concepts.plain: Under RH the heat-flow family sits exactly at the point where lowering the time would push zeros off the line. Since ζ's known zeros are all simple, the first collisions would happen farther and farther up, so ζ is at the edge only at infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C] Newman 1976: −∞ < Λ ≤ ½, zeros of H_t all real ⇔ t ≥ Λ; de Bruijn 1950: real for t ≥ ½; Rodgers–Tao (Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6) Thm 1: Λ ≥ 0; Polymath 15 Thm 1.1: Λ ≤ 0.22; CSV 1994 Cor. 1: for t > Λ zeros real and simple. [R] RH ⇔ Λ = 0. Direction: ∂_t H_t = −∂_zz H_t (RT: backwards heat); increasing t makes zeros real; collisions come from LOWERING t (TAA Lemma 158, correction 16, TAA Lemma 160, correction 6). [T] Prop: under RH, if H_0 has simple zeros near a compact K, then for −δ < t ≤ 0 all zeros of H_t in K are real; since H_t has non-real zeros for every t < 0, these leave every compact set as t → 0⁻: the threshold is at infinity. Simplicity verified for the first 1,500,000,001 zeros (γ < 545,439,823.215; van de Lune–te Riele–Winter 1986). Newman's 'barely true' (RT §1; CSV 'quantitative version of the dictum'); Lehmer pairs are finite-height witnesses (CSV Thm 1). [N] first low collision at t ≈ −3.95 (zeros 4, 5), far from 0.
pitfalls: ζ does not have a double zero at any computed height; the family, not ζ, is at threshold (TAA Lemma 160, correction 5).
H_t has no Euler product for t ≠ 0 (TAA Lemma 160, correction 9).

concepts.name: Γ is the dual−adjoint gap: ⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v,v⟩ = 1 − 2β
concepts.plain: The width Γ of a zero equals how far the pairing-dual and the positive adjoint disagree on that zero.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] For any eigenvector v (|v| = 1) of Θ with eigenvalue ρ = β+iγ: Θ^∨v = (1−ρ)v and ⟨Θ†v,v⟩ = ρ̄, so ⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v,v⟩ = 1 − 2β and Γ_ρ = |1−2β| = |(1−ρ) − ρ̄| ≤ ‖Θ^∨ − Θ†‖ = 2‖S‖ (no normality needed). 𝔽_q: |q/α − ᾱ| = |q − |α|²|/|α|; in exponents (α = q^s) |(1−s) − s̄| = |1−2β|. [N, certified inputs TAA Lemma 156] DH: ρ₁ gap 0.617034364913274771106, ρ₂ 0.301660161219474164808, ρ₃ 0.14871210090161198144, ρ₄ 0.448515389253619560422 (mirrors equal); ζ (52 zeros, t < 150) and DH on-line (122, t < 200): gap 0.
pitfalls: Γ ≤ ‖Θ^∨ − Θ†‖ is an inequality per eigenline; equality of operators needs normality.

concepts.name: KMS/modular positivity is coefficient positivity: a KMS system with partition function F = Σ a_n n^{−β} exists ⇔ a_n ∈ ℤ≥0; then t ↦ F(β+it) is positive definite (|F(β+it)| ≤ F(β)). Compact pieces of the modular route: Tomita J (ℤ/2) and the imaginary-time circle; the BC modular group n^{it} is unitary but not periodic and acts on the prime side (log n)
concepts.plain: The thermal (KMS) route makes imaginary time a circle and gives a positivity, but that positivity is only about the coefficients being counts. It rules out DH for the wrong reason and lets other bad functions through.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Bochner; Tomita–Takesaki S = JΔ^{1/2} (checked 2e−16); thermal time = Hamiltonian time (Connes–Rovelli); BW: wedge boost, e^{2πiK} = 1. [N] BC: Tr e^{−βH} = ζ(β); Galois-averaged KMS value (p^{1−β}−1)/(p−1) (2e−31); symmetry breaking φ(e(1/5)) =.04+.606i. Toeplitz test β = 1.6: ζ, Z_Q PSD, DH min −3.96 (relative). DH excluded by coefficients (not a sign on zeros); Z_Q passes ⇒ B2 negative (TAA Lemma 164 Cor. 4.3).

concepts.name: Levinson/Verblunsky causal coordinates for the window Weil form: ghost = first super-luminal step
concepts.plain: In the box model the window Weil form is exactly Toeplitz, pole included, so the Szegő/Levinson recursion writes it as an exact sum of squares of causal innovations with no curvature remainder: W = Σ_m E_m ε_m², E_m = r₀ Π_{j≤m}(1 − k_j²). Hence W ≻ 0 if and only if every Verblunsky (reflection) coefficient satisfies |k_m| < 1. Each step is an SU(1,1) transfer matrix, a Lorentz boost of rapidity artanh|k_m|; |k| = 1 is the light cone, and a ghost is the first super-luminal step. The first Levinson failure equals the first negative eigenvalue box for box in every failing case checked. This is a Restatement of positivity in coordinates where the margin is O(1): for ζ, E/r₀ ≈ 0.18 at window length 7 and is stable in the grid step, while λ_min/r₀ is about 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁷ and shrinks with the grid step.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Levinson/Verblunsky causal coordinates for the window Weil form: ghost = first super-luminal step. Sources: Verblunsky (1935); B. Simon, Orthogonal Polynomials on the Unit Circle, Part 1, AMS 2005; Levinson (1947); Durbin (1960).
concepts.formula: fᵀW_ℓ f = Σ_{m<N} E_m ε_m(f)²;  W_ℓ ≻ 0 ⇔ |k_m| < 1 for all m < ℓ/h
numbers: sup k genuine l7: ζ 0.260, L(Δ) 0.251, 11a1 0.186
zeta to l16 h0.01: no failure; band sup|k| ≤ 0.076 for ℓ ≥ 9; λ_min/r₀ = 2.7e−7; E/r₀ ≈ ℓ^(−0.70)

concepts.name: Eisenstein scattering resonances at s = ρ/2: purity at Re s = ¼
concepts.plain: At the cusp the Eisenstein series scatters with a phase of modulus one; its poles sit at half the zeta zeros, all on one line exactly when RH holds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s) for SL₂(ℤ): |φ(½+it)| = 1 (NUM 2e−31), φ(s)φ(1−s) = 1 (FE, ghost-blind; NUM 8e−32). Zeros ρ of ζ give poles of φ at s = ρ/2 (simple: |φ|·ε → 0.5146 at ρ₁/2): under RH all on Re s = ¼ (one stratum); an off-line zero β + iγ would sit at Re s = β/2 (DH-type fake: 0.404, 0.0957, 0.325, 0.175 vs 0.25). Constant term a₀(y) = y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s} on s = ½+it: half-density lobes y^{½}e^{±it log y}. Where Selberg's zeta picks these up (Hejhal, Venkov): BIB, unopened.

concepts.name: Hardy/KLMN constant of the window Weil form
concepts.plain: For any exact split W = T - V of the window Weil form with T positive definite, the best constant a = sup V/T satisfies a <= 1 iff W is positive semidefinite, so a Hardy inequality for the primes is Weil positivity restated. For zeta the constant stays below 1 for windows up to 16 but the margin closes in every normalisation tried (critical, no slack); Delta and 11a1 behave alike, Davenport-Heilbronn crosses 1 near l = 4-5, sign-flip controls are far above 1.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hardy/KLMN constant of the window Weil form. Sources: Reed-Simon II (KLMN); Hardy-Littlewood-Polya, Inequalities; Weil 1952.
numbers: route score: 3.9 (0.6·significance + 0.4·probability of progress, 0–10); significance 4.5, probability 3; circular as a route
pitfalls: A Hardy-type constant for the primes is equivalent to window positivity under any exact positive-definite split; only its margin is informative, and that margin closes for every positive form tested.

concepts.name: Invariant (χ-type) vs refined (h-type) counts: Lefschetz/GRR totals, N(T), box counts are FE-determined and ghost-blind; the on-line count changes only at collisions; RH ⇔ refined = invariant
concepts.plain: Some counts can't change under deformation, like the total number of zeros or a Lefschetz number. Others can, like the number of zeros on the line. RH says the second count equals the first. Davenport–Heilbronn has the same total count as a true L-function but fewer zeros on the line, so the protected counts can't tell ghosts apart.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T/B] Lefschetz number homotopy-invariant (fixed points collide/annihilate in pairs); in flat proper families χ = Σ(−1)^i h^i is constant while h^i are upper semicontinuous (Hartshorne III.12.8, not opened); TAA Lemma 140: #C(F_{qⁿ}) − (1 + qⁿ) = −Tr(Fⁿ|H¹): H⁰/H² terms rigid, H¹ frames movable. [N] all 10,100 smooth y² = x³ + Ax + B over F_101: invariant part 102, a_p in [−20, 20] (41 values), all elliptic. [T] H_t: box count (argument principle) conserved across a collision (2.000000), real count 2 → 0. [R] N₀(T) = N(T) ∀T ⇔ RH. [H/N] DH: Riemann–von Mangoldt main term (T/2π)log(5T/2πe) by the FE argument (no source opened for DH): N(135) = 79 vs 79.0002, N(200) = 130 vs 129.548 (TAA Lemma 156 certified); on-line 75 and 122 (ghost deficits 4, 8 at 85.70, 114.16, 166.48, 176.70). ζ: N(150) = 52 vs 52.75. No-go: invariance of counts cannot exclude ghosts.
numbers: F_101 family: 1 + p = 102 fixed, 41 values of a_p
pitfalls: For ζ there is no family and no h¹ (Deninger’s conjectured cohomology, MP0–MP4): Analogy.
DH main term is Heuristic (no source opened) + Numerical (TAA Lemma 160, correction 14).

concepts.name: Li criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the Li coefficients are non-negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Li 1997 / Bombieri–Lagarias 1999: RH ⇔ λ_n ≥ 0 for all n — the Weil positivity in another basis. TAA Lemma 112 reads the Weil form as a Toeplitz–Carathéodory problem; TAA Lemma 131: no route supplies the positivity.

concepts.name: Lossy Weil pencil: with any loss, the number of growing modes equals n₋(Z_L) (Ostrowski–Schneider), so robustness to dissipation is Krein-definiteness
concepts.plain: For the scaling pencil with a loss term, v̇ = (J − εR)Z_L v with J = D⁻¹ skew and R > 0, one has AX + XAᵀ = −2εR < 0 for X = Z_L⁻¹, so by the Ostrowski–Schneider inertia theorem the number of eigenvalues with positive real part is exactly n₋(Z_L), with none on the imaginary axis. Checked on 18 pencils (ζ and Davenport–Heilbronn, L = 2–6.5, two loss matrices, two loss strengths): 72/72. Where Davenport–Heilbronn is elliptic but Krein-indefinite (n₋ = 2), any loss produces two growing modes with rate ∝ ε (log–log slopes 1.000, 0.997, 0.993); ζ (n₋ = 0) decays. This is the L4 libration mechanism: the pencil survives every dissipation iff Z_L ≥ 0 iff the grading is trivial (Γ = 1). Circular as a criterion; no physical loss term is known on the ζ side.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Lossy Weil pencil: with any loss, the number of growing modes equals n₋(Z_L) (Ostrowski–Schneider), so robustness to dissipation is Krein-definiteness. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: A positive-tensor representation of the Weil form is equivalent to positivity
concepts.plain: A Hermitian form on window test functions is the integrated time component of a pointwise positive tensor built quadratically from the test function if and only if it is positive semidefinite. For the Weil form over all windows this is Weil positivity, so seeking such a tensor is RH-strength and its existence carries no information beyond positivity. The canonical complex-spacetime construction, with zeros as modes, reproduces the Weil form only when every zero ordinate is real, which is the Hilbert-Polya input; a ghost quartet pairs each zero with its conjugate rather than itself.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: A positive-tensor representation of the Weil form is equivalent to positivity. Sources: Weil (1952) explicit-formula criterion.
concepts.formula: Q(g) = int T00[g],  T[g] = sum_k psi_k[g] psi_k[g]*  <=>  Q >= 0

concepts.name: de Branges spaces
concepts.plain: Hilbert spaces of entire functions built from a Hermite–Biehler function E; RH becomes "E_h is Hermite–Biehler", but de Branges’ stronger positivity conditions are known to fail for ζ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36 Thm 3.1: for h ∈ (0,½], all β ≤ ½ + h ⇔ PR on σ > ½ + h ⇔ E_{h′} HB ∀h′ > h; h = ½ free, h → 0 = RH. Conrey–Li 2000 (opened, TAA Lemma 78): de Branges positivity fails for ζ and χ₄. TAA Lemma 118: Ψ_c passive ⇔ E_c = ξ(·+c) Hermite–Biehler. TAA Lemma 34: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side.
pitfalls: Conrey–Li: de Branges’ stronger conditions fail — beware "positivity ⇒ RH" shortcuts.

concepts.name: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side
concepts.plain: A de Branges / transmission-line object built from prime data whose passivity along the whole line is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Su21 (Suzuki JFA 281 (2021) 109116): E^{ω,ν} = ξ(½ + ω − iz)^ν, νω > 1, Hankel kernel from prime-side data (TAA Lemma 34). TAA Lemma 37: headline exponential line Θ_c = exp(−2c ξ′/ξ); ‖𝒦[t]‖ < 1 ∀t ⇔ sup ≤ 1; weak form sup_t ≤ 1 ⇔ RH; "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; strict pointwise bound open (M11).
pitfalls: "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; the correct form is sup ≤ 1 (TAA Lemma 37).

concepts.name: Bagchi recurrence
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ ζ approximates itself in the strip (strong recurrence).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Bagchi (via Nakamura Thm B): RH ⇔ strong recurrence of ζ for all K, ε ("infinite prime bath still recurs", TAA Lemma 118). TAA Lemma 123 local form [T given Voronin + Carlson]: ζ strongly recurrent on a disc K ⇔ no zero on K; ghosts show up as a local Rouché defect. Finite prime baths recur but are ghost-blind.

concepts.name: Linear positivity equals Weil positivity on exponential type
concepts.plain: By the Akhiezer/Krein factorization, a nonnegative entire function of exponential type is |F|^2. So positivity of the zero sum on nonnegative test functions is the same cone as Weil quadratic positivity: not a weaker route. Fejer kernels make ghost pairs negative while real pairs stay positive.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Linear positivity equals Weil positivity on exponential type. Sources: Akhiezer theorem; Weil explicit formula.

concepts.name: Lorentzian index for pole-free L-functions: n+ = N+
concepts.plain: For an L-function without pole the pole plane is absent, so the Lorentzian form P - Z is -Z and its positive index equals the number of zeros with Re > 1/2; the zeta-type statement (1, infinity) becomes (0, infinity). Like-for-like controls: zeta*L(chi5) (Dedekind zeta of Q(sqrt5)) vs zeta*DH, built additively.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Lorentzian index for pole-free L-functions: n+ = N+. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026; TAA Lemma 15 Thm 15.2.

concepts.name: Morse counting of log|Ξ| on the critical line: extra saddles exactly at the off-line zeros
concepts.plain: log|Ξ(t + iy)| is harmonic off its zeros, so every critical point is a saddle. On the line, a Laguerre–Pólya-type function has one critical point between consecutive real zeros. ζ: 43 real zeros and 42 critical points in (1, 130), excess 0. Davenport–Heilbronn: 71 and 74, excess 4 = 2 per off-line pair, in the gaps 83.1–87.6 and 112.4–116.7; the forced saddles sit on the line at 85.747, 86.629, 114.170. Classical (circular as a criterion).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Morse counting of log|Ξ| on the critical line: extra saddles exactly at the off-line zeros. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: Below the genuine surface case the rescaled Maass–Selberg form has no underlying L² space; its positivity restates zero locations
concepts.plain: Only A = 2 is a truncated L² norm. For A < 2 the kernel is not the norm of anything on the modular surface, and its positivity is equivalent to the zeros lying left of Re = A/2, a restatement (circular).

concepts.name: Gain lines (active media)
concepts.plain: A ghost acts like a gain line: negative absorption.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §2: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²) — each zero is an absorption line to its right; an off-line zero gives a gain line. Grid σ ∈ [.505,1.1], t ∈ [80,92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; TAA Lemma 144 ghost −66.97 (1.94%). Lorentz model: dRe χ/dω −6 (absorber) / +6 (gain). TAA Lemma 154: measured widths — the near line of a DH ghost on σ = ½+d has FWHM 2|d − (β−½)| (match ≤ 3e−6, 13 d), inverted for d < β−½; as d → 0 its FWHM → Γ = 2(β−½) from below; the visible feature (near − mirror) keeps width ≈ ½(β−½) while its depth fades as 2d/(β−½)². KK sign invariant κ = Re F·∂_tIm F = −1/a³ flips at a gain line. [N] TAA Lemma 155: DH's gain lines reconstructed from ≈ 10 nonzero coefficients via the theta AFE (N = 13), and detected as ghost-map bumps from damped Dirichlet sums with X ≈ 55.

concepts.name: Maxwell–Cremona on the discretized mix wall Σ is too thin to lift
concepts.plain: The discriminant wall on S₂(Γ₀(23)) mixes, drawn as a graph, is a union of paths. A path that is not straight has only the zero equilibrium stress, so there is no Maxwell–Cremona reciprocal and no convex polyhedral lift. A mix simplex of dimension at least 2 would be needed before convex liftability of chambers is a real question. This does not supply (P).
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The wall Σ on S₂(Γ₀(23)) mixes, once discretized, is a union of polygonal paths (primary low: v = 48, e = 47; primary high: v = 14, e = 13; and secondary sheets the same way). The Maxwell excess e − (2v − 3) equals −46 and −12 on the two primary branches (down to −118 on the union); there are 56 non-collinear corners. A non-straight path admits only the zero equilibrium stress, so there is no Maxwell–Cremona reciprocal and no convex polyhedral lift. Treating L*(t) as a graph over the t-axis yields a tautological one-dimensional roof (the low branch is a unimodal U, not slope-convex) that already uses W. The eigenlines t = 0, 0.02, π/2 have no vertex on Σ. The graph is too thin: a mix simplex of dimension ≥ 2 (a cusp-form space of dimension ≥ 3) would be needed before convex liftability of chambers is well-posed. This does not supply (P) over ℚ. Open ~1.8 is unchanged. RH is not proved. Sources: TAA research notes, 5–6 Nov 2026.
numbers: 56 non-collinear corners; a nontrivial self-stress does not exist
pitfalls: A thin graph has no convex lift to mine for a sign. Over ℚ the zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L is still missing (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved.

concepts.name: Adding primes in order to ∞ + pole first increases the negative count and positivity appears only once every prime up to e^L is present

Positivity is collective, not built prime by prime.

concepts.name: ζ sits on the boundary of the Weil cone in every prime direction
concepts.plain: Removing any prime from ζ’s prime side (Euler product cut at P) makes the window Weil form indefinite as soon as the first missing prime p enters the window: L* − log p between 0.01 and 0.18 for P = 2 … 401, with quartets within 0.25. Changing a single weight Λ(101) by as little as 0.3%, or inserting a fake prime at 100, is detected the same way. Heuristic reason (conditional on RH): ζ’s spectral measure is pure point, and any finite prime-side change adds an almost-periodic symbol that is negative on a zero-free interval. Elementary, but it is the exact sense in which each Euler factor is pinned at weight log p.
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: Gluing curvature sees a ghost only through positivity
concepts.plain: A single ghost injected on the zero side of the explicit formula (quartet off the line at height 14.13 or 79.34) leaves the gluing curvature K(p,q) of the window form essentially unchanged (relative change of its sum ≤ 1e-3) until the window form itself loses positivity. The first negative K appears at the same grid step as the first negative eigenvalue, or one step later; afterwards the most negative K equals the lowest eigenvalue of the form and grows smoothly past the threshold. A ghost at height 1001 is invisible at windows up to 7. Gluing curvature is therefore not a more sensitive detector than positivity.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Gluing curvature sees a ghost only through positivity. Sources: TAA Lemma 103 ghost convention; TAA Lemma 184 rev 2 gluing curvature.
concepts.formula: min K(p,q) ≈ λ_min(W_ℓ) after onset;  −min K ∝ (δ − δ*)^p
numbers: onset agreement: 7/7 visible cases within one grid step
pre onset relative change of sum: ≤ 1.0e-3

concepts.name: The Kac gap at the c = 1 edge closes like N^{−1.04}, the ζ window gap like e^{−1.67L}: not alike
concepts.plain: Near c = 1 the smallest Shapovalov eigenvalue decays like N^{−1.04}, while ζ’s κ-window gap closes like e^{−1.67L}. Decay of λ_min is generic, so the "ζ ↔ c = 1 edge" reading is not supported quantitatively.

concepts.name: The pole-orthogonal margin of ζ_K shows no stable relation to h(−d) or L(1, χ) on windows L ≤ 8
concepts.plain: On the pole-orthogonal (primitive) part of the ζ_K Weil form the weakest eigenvalue has no stable correlation with the class number h(−d) or with L(1, χ_{−d}) across the 33 discriminants and windows L ≤ 8.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The pole-orthogonal margin of ζ_K shows no stable relation to h(−d) or L(1, χ) on windows L ≤ 8. Sources: TAA research notes, 2–3 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: ζ’s Weil form with the pole removed is exactly (n−1, 1) for L ≤ 8; the full form is positive; the negative lies in span{e^{±x/2}}
concepts.plain: With the pole term included (sign convention Q = pole − primes + archimedean) the ζ Weil form is positive semidefinite at every tested window L ≤ 8. Removing the pole leaves exactly one negative direction, 99.9% in the pole plane span{e^{±x/2}}; the primitive (pole-orthogonal) part is positive definite. RH ⇒ the full form is positive ⇒ the pole-free form has n₋ ≤ 1, and RH ⇔ the primitive part is positive (Weil).
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: ζ’s Weil form with the pole removed is exactly (n−1, 1) for L ≤ 8; the full form is positive; the negative lies in span{e^{±x/2}}. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: The one-box axis: F(ℓ) = W(1_[0,ℓ]) has a uniform rescaled margin on [1, 10], but only by a 1-in-9400 cancellation
concepts.plain: Instead of growing the number of test functions at a fixed window, take one box of length ℓ. The resulting function F(ℓ) is an explicit prime sum minus the pole plus the archimedean term. On the zero side it is a sum of squares under RH, and an off-line zero would add a term growing like e^(βℓ) with oscillating sign, so "F(ℓ) ≥ 0 for all ℓ" is (heuristically, Landau-type) equivalent to RH. Numerically F stays between 0.060 and 0.134 on [1, 10], but the pole and the primes cancel to one part in about 9400 at ℓ = 10. The obstruction is moved, not removed.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The one-box axis: F(ℓ) = W(1_[0,ℓ]) has a uniform rescaled margin on [1, 10], but only by a 1-in-9400 cancellation. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: F(ℓ) = ℓ·W(1_[0,ℓ]/√ℓ) = W(1_[0,ℓ]) = Σ_{γ>0} 8 sin²(γℓ/2)/γ² (under RH)
numbers: prime side = zero side (5000 zeros plus tail) to 2.1e−4 relative on ℓ ∈ [0.1, 10]
concepts.uncertain: The equivalence with RH is a Heuristic, Landau-type sketch; criteria of this shape are probably classical (not checked against the literature); no novelty is claimed.
pitfalls: As a route this is RH again (circular).
If the ordinates γ are linearly independent over ℚ, Kronecker’s theorem makes inf F = 0 over all ℓ, so the margin is uniform only on finite ranges [Heuristic].

concepts.name: Hodge index theorem
concepts.plain: On a surface the intersection form has exactly one positive direction (the ample class); everything orthogonal to it is negative. This sign is what proves RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: NS(C×C) ⊗ ℝ has signature (1, ρ−1); U = ⟨f₁,f₂⟩ is the (1,1) part and its complement is negative definite. Over ℚ, Hodge-index form on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91, restatement). Surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (D8). TAA Lemma 162: E×E Gram of {pt×E, E×pt, Δ, Γ_F}: det = a² − 4p; one positive eigenvalue ⇔ |a| ≤ 2√p; compact-group analogue: Haar positivity (Peter–Weyl).
concepts.formula: sig NS = (1, ρ − 1); D·D ≤ 0 on h^⊥
pitfalls: Effectivity and Hodge index are independent on both sides (TAA Lemma 94).
Hodge index needs S2, S3, S5 too (TAA Lemma 145).

rels.note: D·D ≤ 0 on V₀ over ℚ (TAA Lemma 91)
U^⊥ = physical quotient (TAA Lemma 115, TAA Lemma 146)

concepts.name: L4 linearization, Krein signatures and the Routh wall
concepts.plain: lambda^4+lambda^2+(27/4)mu(1-mu)=0; short mode Krein +, long mode Krein -; Hamiltonian Hopf (Jordan) at mu_R=0.0385209; stability at a potential maximum of index 2 via Coriolis.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: L4 linearization, Krein signatures and the Routh wall. Sources: Gascheau 1843; Routh 1875; van der Meer 1985; Meyer-Hall-Offin 2009.

concepts.name: Legendre strata: support function / Fenchel–Moreau as a definiteness detector
concepts.plain: All the information about a convex curve sits in the intercepts of its tangent lines; the Legendre transform returns the curve exactly when it is convex, so it is a definiteness test.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Tangent lines carry a convex curve: the support function h(θ) = sup_{x∈K}⟨x,u_θ⟩ determines a closed convex K (Minkowski; BIB). For f = ½xᵀAx the Legendre transform is ½pᵀA⁻¹p, finite everywhere iff A ≻ 0; if A has a negative eigenvalue f* ≡ +∞ (on a box |x| ≤ R it grows with R: TAA Lemma 153 NUM). Fenchel–Moreau: f** = f iff f is convex lsc (BIB). Support-function window of a conic region: 2π for an ellipse; for one convex hyperbola branch exactly 2·atan√(|λ₋|/λ₊) < π (NUM 64.8° vs 64.62° predicted for λ = 1, −0.4); for both branches (or the region xᵀAx ≤ 1 with A indefinite) empty; jump 2π → 0 at det = 0. J. W. McGreevy's 'Legendre type concept' is this. TAA Lemma 159: thermodynamic potentials U, F, H, G are Legendre transforms of one generating function on one Legendrian surface; stability (convexity) is what makes the dictionary invertible.

concepts.name: Pole plane / Tate poles at s = 0, 1
concepts.plain: The two poles of ξ(s) at s = 0 and 1 give the reference plane; subtracting them is what makes a form "relative".
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: the relative Gram on translates uses the pole terms f̂(0), f̂(1) (zero-free entries). Pole of ζ at s = 1 is the 𝕃-ray; the functional equation pairs it with s = 0.

concepts.name: Weil operator C = i^{p−q} = Wick rotation
concepts.plain: Turning an indefinite pairing into a positive one by inserting a quarter turn — the same move as Wick rotation in physics.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 139: Q indefinite → Q(C·, ·̄) PD (Rosati); Abel–Jacobi = principalization. A complex structure is a μ₄ action (J² = −1). Obstruction: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has no complex structure.
numbers: y² = x³ − x: π/√p primitive 4th root of unity for p ≡ 3 mod 4 (TAA Lemma 140)
pitfalls: The Fourier transform is the swap, not the Weil operator (TAA Lemma 140).
Over F_q the sign is algebraic (Castelnuovo); the Hodge model is only an analogy there (TAA Lemma 139 caveat).

rels.note: no complex structure on Pic^ ≅ ℝ

concepts.name: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations
concepts.plain: Pairing a holomorphic form with its own complex conjugate gives a positive number: a genuine |amplitude|².
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: HR holds on every compact Riemann surface; HR form = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Positivity = complex structure inserted (Weil operator C = i^{p−q}). Hecke self-adjointness gives a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
pitfalls: Column 2 (F_q) never fully inherited the HR sign; Castelnuovo replaces it algebraically (TAA Lemma 140).

concepts.name: Lax–Phillips scattering
concepts.plain: Scattering theory for waves on the modular surface; resonances relate to zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: LP80 (read at source, TAA Lemma 118/TAA Lemma 141): s(z) = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s), Res_{s=1} = 3/π, poles at zeros of ζ(1+2iz), RH ⇒ Im z = ¼; Pavlov–Faddeev "RH iff Z″ decays exponentially"; spectrum of B″ = {(κ−1)/2}; "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product". TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally. TAA Lemma 153: bib verified by Crossref: Lax–Phillips, Scattering Theory for Automorphic Functions, Ann. Math. Stud. 87 (Princeton 1976; De Gruyter record dated 1977), doi 10.1515/9781400881567; Bull. AMS 2 (1980) 261–295 (Crossref pages; TAA Lemma 141 cited 261–296, TAA Lemma 153, correction 31); Pavlov–Faddeev, J. Soviet Math. 3 (1975) 522–548, doi 10.1007/BF01084688 (Zap. LOMI 27 (1972)). Poles of φ at ρ/2 = eigenvalues of the generator of the contraction semigroup Z(t) (LP80, read in TAA Lemma 141); contraction ⇒ Re s ≤ ½ (Re ρ ≤ 1) only; purity Re s = ¼ ⇔ RH: Restatement of MP4 ('all that is missing is an appropriate inner product').

concepts.name: Function-field test of the MP4 headline: over F_q, point counts + functional equation + non-negative integer closed-point counts (an Euler product with positive multiplicities, which implies Ihara’s constraints) do NOT induce the Hodge sign; the sign on the Frobenius-graph Gram comes from the surface C×C (Hodge index), not from the counts
aliases: F_q test of the lead conjecture
concepts.plain: Over a finite field, you can write down fake zeta functions whose point counts look perfectly healthy (all positive, with the right symmetry) but whose zeros are off the circle. So the counts alone do not force the sign; what does is the geometry of the surface C×C.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Gram of ⟨H, V, Γ₀..Γ_M⟩ from counts only (Γ_m·Γ_n = q^min N_|m−n|, N₀ = 2−2g; Hallouin–Perret arXiv 1409.2357 Lemma 3); primitive Gram −q^min Σα^|m−n| is −Toeplitz(Σ u^k), so #positive eigenvalues = #σ-2-cycles (real pair 1, quartet 2). [N] 15 point-counted curves (q, g) = (7,2), (11,2), (13,2), (7,3), (11,3): full inertia (1, 2g+1), primitive part NSD rank 2g (max eig ≤ 1e−13). Exact census g = 2, |a| ≤ 6q, |b| ≤ 20q (no hits on the border), a_d exact for d ≤ 40: off-circle FE integer polynomials with all a_d ≥ 0: 675 (q = 7), 2935 (q = 11; = TAA Lemma 109), 4961 (q = 13); on-circle 205/401/513. DH-like pencil (1−λ)P₁ + λP₂ of two genus-3 curves over F₁₁: off-circle for λ ∈ [0.233, 0.9725] (4 roots, 2 positive primitive eigenvalues); genus-2 pencils and (7,3) stay on the circle (sign kept although a_d non-integral). Consequence for MP4: 'Euler product' read as counting data is insufficient; the conjecture can only hold in a geometric reading (an object whose square carries Hodge index).
pitfalls: a_d ≥ 0 checked for d ≤ 40 only (exact integers).
Not a refutation of the conjecture in Deninger’s conjectured cohomology: it rules out the reading “numerical Euler-product data ⇒ sign”.
Framework (Gram of Frobenius graphs, geometric vs arithmetic facet) is Hallouin–Perret’s; TAA Lemma 109/TAA Lemma 137/TAA Lemma 141/TAA Lemma 152 had the count-positive ghosts.

concepts.name: Over F_q the Weil form is the Gram matrix of the Frobenius orbit in H¹ for the Rosati / Hodge-index form
concepts.plain: For a curve over F_q, −D′·D′ on C×C equals the Toeplitz Weil form T exactly: rank 2g, signature (1, ρ−1) on the Néron–Severi side, and positive on the primitive part by the Hodge index theorem. Ghost (non-Weil) polynomials break the Hodge index pattern and give (2,2). This is the realized version of "the Weil form as a Gram matrix".
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Over F_q the Weil form is the Gram matrix of the Frobenius orbit in H¹ for the Rosati / Hodge-index form. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: The pole kernel is the symmetrised product of the forward and backward translation-cogenerator defects at rate ½
concepts.plain: The cogenerator of right translation on L²(0, ∞) at a = ½ is an isometry with cokernel span{e^{−x/2}} (a one-vacancy "Hilbert hotel"); on a window the backward one has defect e^{x/2}. The pole kernel cosh((x−y)/2) equals the symmetrised product of the two defects (difference 2.6·10⁻¹⁸), signature (1,1); one defect alone gives (0,1). The choice a = ½ is the pole’s offset and is put in by hand (score 2.00).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The pole kernel is the symmetrised product of the forward and backward translation-cogenerator defects at rate ½. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: Arakelov geometry
concepts.plain: Compactified arithmetic surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 74: Ô(1)² = ½ for FS metrics; pole-plane Gram [[½,1],[1,0]] signature (1,1); Hodge index vacuous in genus 0. TAA Lemma 139: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has rank 1 and no complex structure. TAA Lemma 65/TAA Lemma 145: Faltings–Hriljac = Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K), relative part = Néron–Tate, not ζ. TAA Lemma 138 R5: Néron–Tate PD (37a1 ĥ = 0.051114). TAA Lemma 152: Faltings 1984 (Ann. Math. 119, 387–424), Hriljac 1985 (Amer. J. Math. 107, 23–38), bibliographic data verified: Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces ⇒ Néron–Tate positive definite; not RH for any L-function (TAA Lemma 152, correction 12).
numbers: TAA Lemma 158: Moriwaki (opened) Thm B, d = 1 case = Faltings–Hriljac: deg(x·ĉ₁(H)^{d−1})-form ≤ 0 on classes with z(x)·H^{d−1} = 0, equality iff nx = f*(y); hypothesis d = dim f ≥ 1 excludes Spec ℤ itself (d = 0, CĤ¹ ≅ ℝ)
pitfalls: Faltings–Hriljac gives height positivity, not RH (TAA Lemma 152, correction 12).

concepts.name: Laguerre's formula: angle = (1/2i) log cross-ratio with the circular points
concepts.plain: The angle between two lines is read off at infinity, from how the lines sit relative to two imaginary points; the metric lives at infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(ℓ₁,ℓ₂) = (1/2i) log CR(ℓ₁,ℓ₂; I, J), I, J = (1 : ±i : 0), isotropic lines y = ±ix; CR = (m₁−i)(m₂+i)/((m₁+i)(m₂−i)) = e^{2i(θ₁−θ₂)} (TAA Lemma 152 NUM 7.1e−16, 2000 pairs). The ½: θ is defined mod π (ℝP¹). The Euclidean metric is the pair {I, J} at infinity (the absolute). Resolves J. W. McGreevy's paradox: lines through 0 are not parallel at infinity (Riemann sphere: they meet again at ∞ with the same angle, opposite orientation; ℝP²: distinct points at infinity); the angle at 0 becomes a separation at infinity.
pitfalls: Sign/orientation conventions: with CR as written Laguerre gives θ₁ − θ₂ mod π; only |θ| mod π is canonical (TAA Lemma 152, correction 9).
Laguerre 1853 (Nouv. Ann. 12, 57–66): Numdam record and first page opened; the formula’s place in the paper not seen.

concepts.name: The archimedean side of the Weil form has a one-sided cone; odd Γ = even Γ + π sech(πr)
concepts.plain: Raising the archimedean multiplier pointwise adds a positive semidefinite form, so Weil positivity survives every such change at every cutoff: a larger conductor, or switching the even Gamma factor to the odd one, since Re ψ(3/4 + ir/2) − Re ψ(1/4 + ir/2) = π sech(πr) > 0 exactly (from the reflection formula). Numerically ζ’s primes with the odd Gamma factor stay positive to L = 8, as do χ₅’s; every other shift of the Gamma argument fails at L < 1.1.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The archimedean side of the Weil form has a one-sided cone; odd Γ = even Γ + π sech(πr). Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: Cartan involution / compact unitary group
concepts.plain: A positive involution is the same thing as a compact (rotation-type) symmetry group; Albert lists the possible kinds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Positive involution ⇔ compact unitary group (TAA Lemma 99, Milne Prop 1.20); Rosati = Cartan θ_J on commutant of J; Weil numbers generate CM or totally real fields (TAA Lemma 136); Albert types I–IV.
pitfalls: Abelian scaling has only an outer Cartan U(1); zeros-as-angles = RH (circular, TAA Lemma 99).

rels.note: no compact Hodge circle for ℚ (TAA Lemma 100)

concepts.name: On a compact manifold a flow conformal on TF with factor e^{αt} has α = 0 (Jacobian e^{αt}, volume conserved); ζ needs α = 1, so the phase space must be solenoidal, with leaf expansion balanced by contraction of a totally disconnected transversal (product formula as volume balance, in Deninger’s elliptic-curve example)
concepts.plain: A flow on a closed, finite manifold cannot stretch everything sideways forever, because the total volume has to stay the same. The Riemann zeta function needs exactly such stretching. So Deninger's space has to be a solenoid, in which the stretching along the leaves is paid for by shrinking in a dust-like p-adic direction.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] one-line proof (TAA Lemma 174 Thm V). [C] Deninger 2005 Cor. 5.5 Rem. 2 and arXiv 0709.2801 state that the conditions force α = 0; Rem. 3: finitely generated orbit-length group, infinitely generated needs fixed points; §7: solenoid (C ×_Γ T_πΓ) ×_{p^Z} R*_+ with metric e^t Re ξη̄ has α = 1. [H] multiplication by π scales leaf area by q and has index q on T_πΓ.
pitfalls: Volume balance on solenoids is shown only for Deninger’s elliptic-curve example (Heuristic in general).

concepts.name: Deligne's route: Lefschetz pencils, monodromy and Rankin's tensor-power trick
concepts.plain: Deligne proved the Weil conjectures without the Hodge index theorem, but still with a positivity: Rankin’s positivity of coefficients of tensor powers.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Deligne, Weil I (Publ. IHÉS 43, 1974, 273–307): RH over F_q without a Hodge index theorem — Lefschetz pencils and monodromy (SGA 7) reduce to a local system on a curve; Rankin's trick (Rankin 1939) bounds weights through L-functions of tensor powers. It still uses positivity: of the coefficients of those L-functions (TAA Lemma 152, correction 4). For ζ no tensor-power analogue is known to give more than zero-free regions (Heuristic, BR-4).
concepts.uncertain: Numdam record and reference list opened; the argument itself is standard knowledge (BIB), not re-read.
pitfalls: 'No positivity' is wrong: Rankin's coefficient positivity is used; what is avoided is a Hodge index theorem (TAA Lemma 152, correction 4).

concepts.name: Selberg eigenvalue conjecture ↔ mass shell λ = ¼ + r²
concepts.plain: The Laplacian on the modular surface is positive, which forces its eigenvalues onto a line; whether the first eigenvalue is at least ¼ for all congruence groups is still open.

concepts.name: Maxwell construction / convex effective potential
aliases: convex hull of a double well
concepts.plain: Doing the Legendre transform twice fills in a double well with a flat floor; this convexity comes for free only from a positive measure.
concepts.label: Theorem

As a Kepler analogue of "trace-free cross terms carry positivity" this scores 1.80.

concepts.name: Measure versus metric: the product formula gives an invariant measure, not an invariant metric
concepts.plain: By the product formula, multiplication by nonzero rationals preserves Haar measure on the idele classes, and the closed orbits have lengths log p. What it does not give is an invariant metric, i.e. a Hermitian structure: Spec ℤ comes with a density, and that is exactly why it is not yet Kähler. The lift the shape list asks for would turn that Haar measure into a Hermitian metric for which the pole line is self-dual and the graphs of multiplication by n are anti-self-dual. A positive Hodge star commuting with the flow would give RH (Deninger, ICM 1998, p. 169), so such a lift stated as positivity is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Measure versus metric: the product formula gives an invariant measure, not an invariant metric. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma). Cited: Connes, Selecta Math. 5 (1999) 29–106; Deninger, Doc. Math. Extra Vol. ICM 1998 I, 163–186.

concepts.uncertain: The lift itself is Open (Conjecture-level); it would need Deninger’s conjectured cohomology, which has not been constructed.
pitfalls: Random Euler products have no pole, so they are not Haar at s = 1; Davenport–Heilbronn has no Euler product, hence no adelic density [Heuristic / Theorem].

concepts.name: log p enters the modular surface as a Hecke angle, θ_p = t log p, on the spectral side, not as a geodesic length
concepts.plain: The Hecke correspondence T_p sends a class of discriminant D to 1 + χ_D(p) classes of the same discriminant (split 2, ramified 1, inert 0) plus classes of discriminant Dp², with unit index dividing p − χ_D(p) (48/48 checks). On the Eisenstein series E(·, ½ + it) the eigenvalue is λ_p = 2cos(t log p) exactly, so log p converts the spectral parameter into the local angle; for the first Maass form the Hecke relations hold to 4·10⁻¹¹ with all angles elliptic. At the scattering resonances s = ρ/2 the Satake parameters have modulus p^{±(½ − Re ρ/2)}, and RH ⇔ every resonance has the same non-tempered depth p^{1/4}. The p-adic tree and the archimedean geodesic flow commute; only adelically (Connes’ adele class space) do both live in one flow.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: log p enters the modular surface as a Hecke angle, θ_p = t log p, on the spectral side, not as a geodesic length.

concepts.name: On E×E the intersection form splits as a hyperbolic boundary term plus a perpendicular Gram whose sign is inertia, not the determinant
concepts.plain: For a divisor on E×E, the self-intersection is twice the product of the two boundary pairings plus the perpendicular square. The perpendicular Gram is negative semidefinite exactly on the Hasse range. The determinant 4q - a^2 is positive for negative-definite examples, so the determinant does not decide the sign. The normalized Frobenius graphs sit on the same scaling hyperbola as Tate’s boundary data, as discrete samples.

concepts.core: Basis h, v, Delta, Gamma. b = (D·v, D·h). D^2 = 2 b0 b1 + D_perp^2, and the cross term vanishes. Perpendicular Gram [[-2, -a], [-a, -2q]], determinant 4q - a^2. Reproduced scan: 151 trace values, negative semidefinite if and only if a^2 <= 4q. Boundary eigenvalues of [[0,1],[1,0]] are -1 and +1. This re-checks the Gram of TAA Lemma 162 and the Hodge index already in the atlas. It is a finite-field control. It is not a sign for zeta. Mattuck-Tate (Hamburg Abh. 22 (1958) 295) and Grothendieck (J. Reine Angew. Math. 200 (1958) 208-215) are the literature for the curve case via the surface; not re-proved here.

concepts.name: Boosts close into rotations only in imaginary time: Thomas–Wigner (boost commutators are rotations), Cartan duality H³ = SO(3,1)/SO(3) ↔ S³ = SO(4)/SO(3) (p ↦ ip), and Bisognano–Wichmann/Unruh: the Rindler boost is the modular flow of the wedge algebra; its Wick rotation is a Euclidean rotation whose 2π period is the KMS condition (T = a/2π) — arithmetic counterpart: ζ(β) as the primon-gas / Bost–Connes partition function, p^{−it} the time evolution

concepts.plain: In Weil's proof a curve is one factor, the surface C×C is the product, and the ample class splits the product. Over the integers Deninger's foliation plays the factor, the Connes–Consani square the product, and the splitting is what is missing.

concepts.name: Zeros-blind input is the data package “masses + force law”, not a literal equation
concepts.plain: In Kepler and in the restricted three-body problem, the input that does not look at orbits is the package of masses and a force law, which writes the effective potential and its Hessian before any trajectory. Mapped to primes, that package is place weights together with Euler factors and a pairing rule. It is not a formula of the shape x + y, and it does not license treating a prime as a Newtonian momentum.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Identification tag, not an equation. In Kepler and the restricted three-body problem the zeros-blind input is the data package “masses + force law” (G, the masses m_i, and the rotating-frame prescription) that writes U_eff and its Hessian before any trajectory, periapsis, or spectral datum is used. “Masses + force” does not mean a literal x + y written on the page, and the right-hand side is not “= 1”: normalized walls |k| = 1 and symplectic volume scales are different objects. Mapped: masses ↔ prime and place weights (log p, conductors, residue degrees q = p^n, idèle norms); force law ↔ local Euler factors, the functional equation, and the pairing rule; amended potential ↔ a zeros-blind U_eff or Gram; orbits, periapsis and spectrum ↔ zeros, eigenvalues of W_L, and turning data, which are outputs. Newtonian dimensional analysis on the abstract labels (primes obeying p = mv) is a weak analogy, about 1.5, and is not licensed. A construction is looking at the right object when it names positivity from primes, levels, Euler factors, an intersection or Weil pairing, or an ample class — and never from a list of zeros ρ. Candidate arithmetic effective potentials stay scored as before: formal Castelnuovo–Severi log Q and the archimedean log|L| are calibrations; the Arakelov–Faltings–Zhang height is the named arithmetic amended potential; W_L itself is the definition of success. RH is not proved. Sources: TAA research notes, 5–6 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: Not a literal equation, and not a license for p = mv. Analogy only: a classical or residual twin of the chamber, not a constructor. Over ℚ the zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L is still missing (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved.

concepts.name: Γ, the width of a zero: FWHM of its Breit–Wigner line
concepts.plain: Each zero shows up as a bell-shaped line; its width at the critical line is twice its distance from the line. RH says every width is zero: every line becomes a spike.

'Stable vs decaying' is convention-dependent; invariant: unitary state vs non-unitary ±Γ pair (in u = log x the ghost grows like e^{Γu/2}; TAA Lemma 154, correction 3). concepts.name: The arithmetic equation of state: primon gas / Bost–Connes dictionary (T, U, S, C, Ω; KMS time; volume options; P_X(β))
concepts.plain: ζ is the partition function of a free gas of primes. Temperature, energy, entropy and heat capacity are exact; volume and pressure are not built in. With a cutoff at X the 'pressure' is a prime count whose smooth part comes from the pole and whose wiggles are the zeros.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] Primon gas (Julia 1990, Spector 1990; Wikipedia 'Primon gas', opened): Fock basis |n⟩, H|n⟩ = log n|n⟩, Z(β) = Tr e^{−βH} = ζ(β), β > 1; Hagedorn divergence at β = 1 (density of states e^E). Bost–Connes (BC95 Thm 5, opened): unique KMS_β for 0 < β < 1 (type III₁), for β > 1 extreme KMS_β indexed by embeddings of ℚ^cycl (type I∞), normalization 1/ζ(β), T_c = 1, Gal(ℚ^cycl/ℚ) broken for β > 1. Sums over all occupation numbers at fugacity 1 = grand canonical, μ = 0: Ω = −T log ζ(β) = Σ_p T log(1 − p^{−β}) (independent modes). U = −ζ′/ζ(β), S = ∂(T log Z)/∂T = log ζ + βU, C = β²(log ζ)″ = β² Var(log n). [N] β = 2: log Z 0.497700, U 0.569961, S 1.637622, C 3.537927 (residual of S ≤ 2e−30); C(1.01) = 10200.8. [T/N] No volume: with mode cutoff p ≤ X, log Z_X(2) → log ζ(2) = 0.49770 (per mode 7.5e−7 at X = 10⁷: not extensive); log Z_X(1) = γ + log log X + o(1) (Mertens; 3.35717 vs 3.35716 at 10⁷). So 'Ω = −PV' is a name, not an identity. Time (KMS strip, BC95 §1): σ_t(μ_n) = n^{it}μ_n, Tr(e^{−βH}e^{itH}) = ζ(β − it); critical line = β = ½, inside the Hagedorn-divergent region where ζ is a continuation, not a trace. [Def + T] Energy-cutoff 'pressure' P_X(β) := Σ_{n≤X} Λ(n)n^{−β}/log n; smooth part Li_β(X) = ∫₂^X u^{−β}du/log u comes from the pole (displaced reference, TAA Lemma 146 buoyancy); fluctuation P_X − Li_β is the explicit-formula sum over zeros; RH ⇔ fluctuation O(X^{½−β+ε}) (von Koch type, Restatement). [N] β = ½: fluctuation 0.268, 0.292, 0.290, 0.246, 0.247 at X = 10³…10⁷. Earlier material: density = Hagedorn density of states; half density = β = ½ weights n^{−½} (TAA Lemma 145); mass shell β(1−β) = ¼ at β = ½ (TAA Lemma 150); buoyancy = pole subtraction (TAA Lemma 146) [Analogy for the names].
numbers: log Z_X(1) − log log X → γ (3.35717 at 10⁷)
pitfalls: 'Pressure × volume' is only the name of −Ω: the primon gas has no volume and is not extensive (TAA Lemma 159, correction 2).
The critical line β = ½ is in the Hagedorn-divergent region; there Z is a continuation (TAA Lemma 159, correction 4).
Every T,P,V,S object is a Legendre transform of one generating function: a dictionary is a change of variables unless a positivity law does work (TAA Lemma 159, correction 8).

concepts.name: Two conditions: primitive positivity and pole channel
concepts.plain: On each finite section, Weil positivity splits into (a) positivity on the primitive part (functions whose Mellin transform vanishes at the two pole points), which is Castelnuovo-Severi / Hodge index on the primitive part and is where off-line zeros and finite-field fakes show up, and (b) positivity of the even and odd pole margins, which are exactly zero in the finite-field template, tend to zero generically, and are blind to off-line zeros. (a) and (b) on all sections is equivalent to RH. What is missing is a source for (a). In the finite-field model the pole channel is zero only once the graphs span the fibre classes; with an incomplete span a fake fails first in the pole channel, so the pole condition is not pure normalisation on finite sections.

concepts.name: Passive arithmetic response of 32a1 (Λ′/Λ as a Foster function)
concepts.plain: For the CM curve y² = x³ − x (conductor 32, root number +1) take Z = Λ′/Λ of the completed L-function, critical line Re s = 1. On the line Z is purely imaginary (lossless, phase ±90° everywhere), by the functional equation and real coefficients. Lagarias's theorem on admissible zero sets gives: GRH for this L-function holds iff Re Z > 0 on Re s > 1, i.e. the response is passive. Under GRH, Z(1+w) = Σ 2w/(w²+γ²) over zeros γ > 0, one lossless resonator per zero; off the line each has damping 2(σ−1), and an off-line zero would be a gain resonator. The absorption peaks near the line sit at the zeros, not at primes. Inert primes enter only at second order, with their own poles on Re s = 1/2. No finite Euler product is passive near the line. Kramers–Kronig and the 90° crossing hold for gain media too, so they do not supply the sign. This restates GRH; it does not prove it.
concepts.label: Restatement

concepts.name: Density × density: Weil’s form read off the diagonal and its log n translates
concepts.plain: The prime side of ζ is a density on the log-scale line, dΛ = Σ Λ(n) δ(x − log n). Weil’s form pairs two half-densities g(x), g(y) against a distribution that depends only on x − y. That distribution is not supported on the diagonal alone: it lives on the diagonal (the archimedean term and the pole, which is a smooth Haar part) and on its translates x − y = ±log n, with weights Λ(n)/√n. Those translates are the graphs of multiplication by n, the analogue of the graphs of Frobenius powers on C × C, whose Gram matrix over F_q is Toeplitz (Hallouin–Perret). The two pole functionals are pairings with the Haar half-densities x^(±½), so quotienting by the pole line (Gupta–Bleuler) is quotienting by "pure Haar". Positivity of the pairing is Weil’s criterion, i.e. RH.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Density × density: Weil’s form read off the diagonal and its log n translates. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma). Cited: Hallouin–Perret, Trans. AMS 372 (2019) 5409–5451.

concepts.name: Why the area is π: the circle in every zero count (Basel as common origin)
concepts.plain: The π in each zero’s area is the circle’s π, coming from the geometry of complex numbers; the same circle gives Euler’s π²/6, but the zeros do not explain π.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] ∫ a/(a²+x²)dx = π sgn a = angle subtended by ℝ at ia = half of ∮dz/z = 2πi; P_a = (1/π)a/(a²+x²) is harmonic measure, Cayley-equivalent to the disk Poisson kernel (mass 1, NUM 40 digits); 2π = circumference/radius. [R] Area is a dimensionless invariant of the complex structure (scale- and coordinate-free yes), as C/d is of a round metric. Direction: the circle puts π into every zero count; the zeros do not derive π (TAA Lemma 154, correction 9). [T] Euler: ζ(2) = π²/6, ζ(2k) = rational·π^{2k} (sin product / π cot πz; NUM sanity ζ(2) − π²/6 = 2e−41). [R] Basel and the ±π area share an origin (the circle); NOT (±π)²/6 from residue areas: ζ(2k) is archimedean (Γ-factor, trivial zeros; ζ(1−2k) = −B_{2k}/2k) (TAA Lemma 154, correction 10). [C/O] ζ(3) irrational (Apéry, BIB); rationality of ζ(3)/π³ OPEN (TAA Lemma 154, correction 11); even/odd ↔ ghost-blind/sensitive is Heuristic at most. The locked ratio is the complex structure J, which also defines the Weil operator C = i^{p−q} (OS/Wick reading Analogy, TAA Lemma 153, correction 10).
pitfalls: Not a derivation of π from zeros or RH (TAA Lemma 154, correction 9).
ζ(2) is not a product of resonance areas (TAA Lemma 154, correction 10).
ζ(3)/π³ irrational is unproved (TAA Lemma 154, correction 11).

concepts.name: Order compatible with a form needs a Rosati involution

concepts.name: On a symmetric window the Weil Gram splits as (A+H) ⊕ (A−H), H the reflected (Hankel) form; window positivity ⇔ reflection ratio |μ| < 1
concepts.plain: On a symmetric window the Toeplitz Weil Gram is exactly the direct sum of an even and an odd sector, (A+H) ⊕ (A−H), where H(x,y) = W(x+y) is the reflected (Osterwalder–Schrader-type) form; the negative counts add sector by sector (155/155 windows, four systems). Window positivity is equivalent to |μ| < 1 for the generalized eigenvalues H v = μ A v, which is the existing domination form of Weil positivity reproduced on the hat basis; as a criterion it is circular.

concepts.plain: Staying on the definite side is equivalent to the Sundman clock being real; the regularization turns a crossing into an imaginary clock but does not forbid it. It helps only if crossings are already excluded.

concepts.name: Saddle-chain Melnikov pairing: chaining the Euler factors as hyperbolic saddles gives the Weil form on a modulated family (circular)
concepts.plain: Each prime is a hyperbolic periodic orbit of period log p on ℝ × ℚ_p (multipliers p and 1/p by the product formula); chaining them along the explicit formula gives M_L(t₀) = W(g_L e^{it₀u}), the Weil form restricted to modulated bumps of support L. ζ: M_L ≥ 0 for L ≤ 8 (prime side = zero side to quadrature accuracy); Davenport–Heilbronn turns negative at t₀ = 84.5 (its off-line zero 85.70 + 0.31i) and the Epstein zeta of x² + 5y² on t₀ ∈ [14.5, 31.25]. Sign-definiteness for all t₀ and L is necessary for RH, not sufficient; it is a zero detector, not a mechanism.

concepts.name: Weil window form on the pole annihilator, as a Morse-index / discriminant criterion
concepts.plain: No conjugate point, every nondegenerate Levinson/Schur step with |k_M| < 1, and 1 − k_M² > 0, say the same thing as W_L ≥ 0 on strict finite sections. That restates Weil positivity. It does not produce the sign. The missing non-local polarization over ℚ stays open.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Dictionary assembling the Weil window form on the pole annihilator as a Morse-index/discriminant criterion: no conjugate point ⇔ all nondegenerate Levinson/Schur steps satisfy |k_M| < 1 ⇔ 1 − k_M² > 0 ⇔ W_L ≥ 0 (strict finite sections; semidefinite limits require boundary conventions). This is a restatement, not a sign source. Connes–Consani supplies the arena; Deninger is the factor, with compatible flow-respected J missing and positive star free; Davenport–Heilbronn and Hecke mixes are the hyperbolic-side controls. Morse supplies counting, not a curvature-based sign (the downgraded “never focuses” criterion). The missing non-local polarization identity is Open ~1.8. A candidate Hecke-mix discriminant locus is not a b²−4ac quadric: W is linear in Λ-coefficients. The bath/free-energy second variation remains an analogy (the Weil form is not a relative entropy). RH is not proved. Sources: TAA research notes, 5–6 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: This restates a criterion; it is not a sign source. Over ℚ the zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L is still missing (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved.

concepts.name: W_L is the compatible metric g = ω(·, J·), not the canonical symplectic form
concepts.plain: The Weil window form is a symmetric Gram, the metric g in a Kähler triple. The canonical symplectic form ω = dp ∧ dx is a different object; calling it a Weil analogue collides with Weil–Petersson and with phase-space area. What is missing over ℚ is a zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L. Rank 1 is unchanged.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Packaging lock for (P), restating the Kähler triple (atlas rank 1, unchanged). The Weil window form W_L is a symmetric / Hermitian positivity form (a Gram), not an alternating 2-form. Naming the canonical symplectic form ω = dp ∧ dx a “Weil analogue” is a name collision with Weil–Petersson / symplectic area (numerology, about 1.2). The structural duality stands: a Hessian, a Gram, or W_L is the symmetric twin of a skew form ω (cup product, Weil pairing, Poincaré duality, phase-space area). Compatibility is extra data J with g(u, v) = ω(u, Jv), J² = −I, and [J, flow] = 0. Over 𝔽_q this is a theorem (Hodge index, Rosati, and a compatible J). Over ℚ, zeros-blind (P) is the search for a zeros-blind pair (ω_arith, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L on ker P — not another shadow of the formal Castelnuovo–Severi form Q, and not ω itself. Symmetric-only candidates (formal Q, the archimedean log|L|) remain calibrations. RH is not proved. Sources: TAA research notes, 5–6 Nov 2026.
concepts.formula: g(u, v) = ω(u, Jv), J² = −I; W_L = g on ker P, not ω
pitfalls: Do not identify W_L with the canonical symplectic form. Over ℚ the zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L is still missing (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved.

concepts.name: GNS factorization of W on all of E0 is Weil positivity for zeta; independent positivity of H+ is missing
aliases: H+ norm identity versus construction criteria
concepts.plain: For all compactly supported test functions in E0, on every window, a map into a Hilbert space or a semidefinite quotient with squared norm exactly W is Weil positivity for zeta. An abstract GNS construction assuming that positivity can inherit covariance, window compatibility, and the zeros-blind prime and gamma data already in the explicit formula. Those compatibilities are not the missing source of the sign, and the construction is circular as a proof. What is missing is positivity of H+ identified with W without assuming W >= 0. Not every further demand follows automatically.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: The equivalence is for the whole class, not for one window. A Cholesky factor of one window matrix is circular. An abstract GNS construction assuming RH can inherit formal compatibilities of W but does not prove the sign. This does not say that no compatibility follows from RH, and it does not say that an unspecified Hecke action or a Beurling control follows automatically. Place-local squares cannot equal the signed local terms one place at a time. A global coupled construction may still use primes, Euler factors, and gamma data. A positive representation does not select W. The reference form G0 does not select W. No such independent map, and no compatible J whose metric reproduces W, is constructed.

concepts.name: One Perron mode against the pole
concepts.plain: Split Weil's form on a grid of narrow boxes as W = Z + P, where Z (archimedean plus primes) has non-positive off-diagonal entries and P is the rank-2 pole term. On every grid tested, Z has exactly one negative eigenvalue, with an entrywise-positive (Perron) eigenvector. The pole's positive eigenvalue cancels it with a margin of 1e-3 to 1e-6. Without the primes, Z has about ell*6.29/pi - 1 negative modes; the primes collapse them into one. Positivity of W implies at most one negative mode of Z (theorem); an unconditional proof that there is exactly one, together with a positive 2x2 margin on all grids, is open and would imply RH. In the finite-field template the single negative mode is the ample (timelike) class of Hodge index and the pole is 2 d1 d2; fakes have two negative modes. The entrywise-positive Perron vector is automatic from the sign pattern and also occurs for fakes.
