concepts.name: Davenport-Heilbronn window jumps
concepts.plain: The Davenport-Heilbronn function has the functional equation and archimedean factor of an odd character mod 5 but no Euler product, and has off-line zeros near 0.8085+85.699i and 0.6508+114.163i. Its window form has no negative squares for short windows and gains them in pairs, one quadruple at a time, at window length about 3.9 and 5.67. So the archimedean place and the functional equation cannot force the second mode to stay non-degenerate: any proof must use the Euler product. This matches the constant-signature mechanism of Adiprasito-Huh-Katz Prop. 7.16, where non-degeneracy is proved independently.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Davenport-Heilbronn window jumps
pitfalls: Correction (v1.14): Davenport–Heilbronn’s first Weil-window crossings move to L ≈ 3.63 (even) / 3.65 (odd) on fine bases (fine grid M = 320; h = 0.0083), and the second pair to ≈ 4.19/4.21 (h = 0.0083); the values 3.80–3.925 (and 6.3–7.4 for the second pair) quoted here are basis values at h = 0.025 or coarser, where the hat factor s(γh)⁴ attenuates the ghost ordinate. The qualitative statements are unchanged; see dh_crossing_basis_dependence.

concepts.name: A synthetic real off-line zero pair (Siegel-type) adds exactly one negative direction, at the window where the base margin collapses, with no second neck
concepts.plain: Adding a synthetic real pair β, 1−β (β = 0.9, 0.95, 0.99; clearly labelled synthetic: no Siegel zero is known) to χ_{−4} or χ_{−3} gives exactly one negative direction from L ≈ 1.3–1.6 (2.7 as β → ½), set by the collapse of the base form’s margin rather than by 1 − β, and it stays one up to L = 8: a second timelike direction, not a neck. Davenport–Heilbronn’s complex quadruple gives two (first crossings ≈ 3.63/3.65 on fine bases). ζ_K with a synthetic pair and the pole removed is (n−2, 2). Deuring–Heilbronn repulsion is Open here (the additive model cannot show it).
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: Allowed locally ≠ aligned globally: every Frobenius angle is allowed, but only the genuine assignment keeps the window form positive (Δ and 11a1)
concepts.plain: For a degree-2 L-function each prime has an angle θ_p (α_p/√p = e^(±iθ_p)). Hasse (11a1) and Deligne (Ramanujan’s Δ) make every angle real, and Sato–Tate says how they are distributed. Both are proved; GRH is open. In the window model the genuine angles keep the form positive for every window up to ℓ = 7, while the same angles permuted among the primes, i.i.d. Sato–Tate angles, aligned rearrangements, or one wrong local factor all fail quickly. Global positivity pins each angle to a fraction of a degree although 180° is allowed. So the missing piece is the joint law of the angles across all primes, together with the archimedean place and the conductor — not any single angle.

Finite-window margins go to 0 as ℓ grows, so the pinning widths are model-dependent: read the trend, not the values.
The Hecke relations (a_mn = a_m a_n, a_p² relation) hold for any assignment of angles, including the shuffled ones; what is joint is the existence of the modular form, i.e. the functional equation.

concepts.name: Certified window for one off-line pair
concepts.plain: For a synthetic off-line quadruple at the height of the first zero, Paley-Wiener interpolants at the pole pair and the four off-line points, a written-out mollification step, and a tail bound (Poisson-kernel envelope of the kernels plus the Hadamard identity sum of Poisson kernels = (1/pi) Re xi'/xi) certify three negative squares for every window length at least 5.55, 3.60, 2.90, 2.20 at displacement 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.45. The certificate is floating point, not interval arithmetic. A closed form scales like displacement^(-2/3) at low height and like (1/displacement) log(8 displacement log(height/2pi)) at large height. The explicit length needs every off-line zero to be known.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Certified window for one off-line pair

concepts.name: Krein mass ratio μ_eff(L): ζ stays at μ = 0, Davenport–Heilbronn’s secondary is born at L*
concepts.plain: Take the Krein-negative pencil pair ω₋ and its nearest Krein-positive partner ω₊ and set κ = ω₋²ω₊²/(ω₋² + ω₊²)²; at L4 κ = 27μ(1 − μ)/4 exactly and the Routh wall is κ = ¼, so μ_eff solves μ(1 − μ) = 4κ/27. ζ: μ_eff ≡ 0 at all 41 cutoffs L ∈ [3, 8] (λ_min ≥ 1.2e−12): ζ behaves like the μ = 0 restricted problem, i.e. Kepler. Davenport–Heilbronn: μ_eff = 0 up to L*, a Krein-negative pair born at L = 3.763 (h = 0.0125) with μ_eff = 0.002, reaching μ_R by L ≈ 4.0 and then alternating just below (elliptic) and just above (quartet) it. At L* Davenport–Heilbronn crosses the parabolic wall, not the Routh wall.
concepts.label: Numerical

numbers: research-note label: Numerical (with a heuristic caveat)

concepts.name: Euler product does not keep the Krein mass ratio below the Routh wall (Beurling control)
concepts.plain: Beurling systems with an Euler product, a non-negative prime measure and unique factorization cross both walls: ζ times the L174 Thm C factor (zero at .75 ± 10i) is past the parabolic wall at L ≈ 1.63 and has Hamiltonian–Hopf quartets from L ≈ 1.77 (b = .55: 3.13 / 3.27), at two resolutions; discrete Poisson g-primes (log-primes a.s. rationally independent) are indefinite from L ≈ 1. So neither the Euler product, nor unique factorization, nor non-resonance keeps μ_eff below μ_R. Extends euler_fe_conjunction to the Routh wall.

concepts.name: Gluing curvature on prime pairs
concepts.plain: The mixed second difference of the lowest eigenvalue of the window form when two primes are switched off, K_g(p,q), is invariant under adding a multiple of the identity. For ζ, L(Δ) and 11a1 it is nonnegative on almost all prime pairs, while sign-flipped and permuted variants have about half the pairs negative. It is a tendency, not a sign law: the genuine twist of Δ by the character mod 5 has a fifth of its pairs negative, the 11a1 fraction grows with the window, and first differences already separate genuine from shuffled.
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: Dilution law on the path from Davenport–Heilbronn to an Euler product: ℓ*(t) ≈ 5.1 + 2.5 log(1/(1−t))
concepts.plain: Mix the two forms: (1−t)·(Davenport–Heilbronn) + t·(½L(χ)L(χ̄)). On the zero side this carries the Davenport–Heilbronn zeros with weight 1−t, so for every t < 1 the off-line zeros are still there and some window eventually sees them. The window at which they are first seen recedes only logarithmically as t → 1. In plain words: any fixed amount of non-multiplicativity is caught by a long enough window. This calibrates "a proof must use the Euler product"; it says nothing about whether RH is true.
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: Reversing the rotation does not swap the L4 Krein signs; only the planar sense of both modes flips
concepts.plain: At L4 the slow libration is Krein − and the fast epicycle Krein + (signature (2,2)); they collide at μ_R. Reversing Ω → −Ω keeps the slow mode Krein − and the fast mode Krein +, because y → −y is symplectic and conjugates H_Ω to H_{−Ω}. The Krein sign is handedness relative to Ω.

concepts.name: The zeta pole mode is the single unpaired negative square
concepts.plain: Without its pole term the zeta window form has exactly one negative square at every window length, always in the exchange-even sector; it is the only obstruction to a compatible quaternionic star. Analogy: degree-0 (real) part versus degree-1 (quaternionic) part in Deninger's graded category.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The zeta pole mode is the single unpaired negative square. Sources: arXiv:2204.02714; arXiv:1001.1621.

concepts.name: Two failure channels: W∞–pole at r ≈ 0 and W∞–primes in the first zero-free gap; pole deformations stay parabolic
concepts.plain: When an archimedean deformation breaks ζ’s Weil form, the first negative direction either sits at spectral frequency 0, where W∞ and the pole balance and the primes are silent, or at r ≈ 5.5–8.4, inside the gap below the first zero 14.13, where W∞ and the primes balance. Deforming the pole alone never produces Hamiltonian–Hopf quartets up to L = 8 (purely parabolic), unlike W∞, conductor or Gamma deformations.

With fewer graphs, the failure appears first in the odd pole channel while the primitive part is still positive. Over the rationals no finite section spans the fibre classes, so the model does not rule out an off-line zero showing first in the pole channel.

concepts.name: Which channel an off-line zero breaks first over the rationals
concepts.plain: Diagnostic, not evidence: off-line zero quartets were planted by hand on finite sections of Weil's form (box, sine, Legendre and bump bases; supports 1 to 5). In 225 of 226 failing runs the form first goes negative through the pole channel (even or odd, about equally). The primitive part fails just after, exactly when the planted zero gives the arch-plus-primes part a second unstable mode, and the gap between the two onsets shrinks as the section is refined. The finite-field rule 'incomplete span means the pole channel fails first' carries over; its 'odd channel' refinement does not, and the L2 distance of the fibre functionals from the section does not predict the channel.

concepts.name: Near-collision law at the de Bruijn-Newman edge
concepts.plain: Through the pair law, the small-gap law of zeros is the density of backward collision times near t = 0. Zeta zeros (and GUE) show a cubic small-gap law, so collisions thin out at t = 0 (zeta sits at the edge, Lambda = 0); the on-line zeros of Davenport-Heilbronn show an exponent near 2 and an excess of tiny gaps, consistent with t = 0 lying inside its collision era (Lambda_DH > 0). A diagnostic, not a proof.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Near-collision law at the de Bruijn-Newman edge. Sources: Bogomolny-Bohigas-Leboeuf-Monastra, J. Phys. A 39 (2006) 10743.

concepts.name: Signed energy as an early warning of ghost landing
concepts.plain: The signed energy always goes negative before a ghost lands, but how early depends on how far off the line the ghost starts relative to the local gap. Low ghosts are flagged for their whole era; a ghost at half a gap only in the last 8-17%. Its sign at a single time is not a reality test: one Davenport-Heilbronn window is positive at t = 0 with a ghost inside.

concepts.plain: For a ghost of displacement δ at the first zero, the window length of first failure follows ℓ* ≈ −4.8 ln δ − 11.3 (resolution-dependent). At fixed window, |k| at the onset box stays between 0.06 and 0.18 up to 98% of the critical displacement and then jumps (to 9.6 in one case), while the linearised prediction is 0.004. A 2% change in δ moves the onset by only about 0.1 in window length. Every quantity is real-analytic in the data until det T_m = 0, so loss of positivity is the first exit from the polydisk and no statistic built from the same data can diverge earlier. This is the analytic reason behind the repeated absence of early warnings.

concepts.name: Nonnegative couplings plus a pole are not enough
concepts.plain: The Dedekind zeta of ℚ(i), ζ·L(χ₄), has nonnegative prime coefficients 1 + χ₄(p)ᵏ and a pole, and its window form stays positive. Replacing χ₄(p) by random signs keeps every coefficient nonnegative and keeps the pole and the Gamma factors, yet the window form fails for every random sign pattern tried. So a ferromagnetic sign of the couplings and a pole do not by themselves produce positivity: the genuine character (the arithmetic alignment) is needed.

concepts.name: The induction matrix on the Q-quotient (Weil form on S-unit lattices)
concepts.plain: Place one Gaussian test function at log m for each S-smooth m ≤ N and take M_mn = W(η_m, η_n), Weil's quadratic form built from primes and the archimedean place. Translation invariance makes M_mn a function of the rational m/n alone. The couplings take both signs about equally (their pattern follows cos(γ₁ log(m/n))), so the matrix is pair-dependent but not ferromagnetic. Its smallest eigenvalue is positive and collapses super-exponentially as the lattice fills (σ = 0.1: 2.4e−5 → 8.7e−26 for N = 30). Restricting the prime sum to S makes it strongly negative, because the indefinite rank-2 pole term is no longer cancelled by the prime density. Including all primes up to the window scale restores positivity. The matrix is the Weil form rewritten: positivity for all such lattices is a restatement of RH.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The induction matrix on the Q-quotient (Weil form on S-unit lattices)

concepts.name: Weil discriminant wall Σ on S₂(Γ₀(23)) mixes
concepts.plain: On mixes of the two newforms in S₂(Γ₀(23)), the wall Σ = {(t, L): λ_min(W_L(v_t)) = 0} is a U-shaped curve in the support length, empty on the eigenlines up to L = 9, with a fold and one ghost-recombination branch switch. The picture describes the wall. It does not supply the sign.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Σ = {(t, L): λ_min(W_L(v_t)) = 0} for v_t = cos t · f + sin t · g, mapped at hat width h = 0.0125. The curve L*(t) is U-shaped and empty on the eigenlines t = 0, π/2 up to L = 9. There is a fold at t ≈ 0.98, L* ≈ 3.69, and a branch switch at t ∈ [1.450, 1.458] (the low ghost recombines and the high ghost takes over). No finite-L merger of two crossings. Levinson’s 1 − |k_M|² is a local defining function of the wall (62/62 sign flips; mean L*_Lev − L*_thr = −0.064). The ghost law L* = log(γ/2π) + c has rms 0.79; with an extra log(β − 1/2) the rms drops to 0.14. This describes the wall, not the sign. The mechanism is unchanged (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved. concepts.name: Clausius as candidate positivity: Γ ≥ 0 is automatic, RH = Γ ≡ 0 (reversible / lossless); the working positivity is passivity (ghosts = gain), with Foster ⇔ Laguerre on the line
concepts.plain: Reading the width Γ as entropy production gives nothing, because widths are never negative anyway; RH says every width is zero, i.e. the system is reversible. The positivity that does work is passivity: ζ absorbs everywhere to the right of the line, while a ghost shows up as gain.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: [C] Clausius ∮δQ/T_res ≤ 0, equality iff reversible; entropy production ≥ 0 (Wikipedia 'Clausius theorem', opened). [N] Carnot T_h = 2, T_c = 1: Σ Q/T = 0, efficiency 0.5; conduction Q = 1 from 2 to 1: entropy production 0.5. [A] Γ_ρ = 2|β − ½| ↔ entropy production: Γ ≥ 0 holds by definition, so this 'second law' is empty; RH is the EQUALITY Γ ≡ 0 ('every mode reversible'), matching TAA Lemma 118 (RH = undoubled system lossless). [N] TAA Lemma 156 certified: ζ 52 zeros t < 150 all Γ = 0; DH Γ = 0.617034, 0.301660, 0.148712, 0.448515 (t < 200), sum 1.516. [R] The precise positivity law is passivity (Lagarias/Hinkkanen): RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ > 0 on Re s > ½; each zero gives a Lorentzian of sign sgn(σ − β), so a ghost is GAIN (negative absorption) for ½ < σ < β — the opposite sign to 'ghost = dissipation'. [N] t ∈ [80,120], σ ∈ {.55}: ζ min 0.0467 > 0; DH min −15.08 at (0.75, 85.7), negative on [85.5,85.9] and [114.1,114.3] at σ =. [T] On the line ξ′/ξ(½+it) = −iΞ′/Ξ is purely reactive (lossless); Foster's monotone reactance dX/dt > 0 is the Laguerre inequality Ξ′² − ΞΞ″ > 0 (⇐ RH; ⇏ RH, TAA Lemma 116 locally invisible ghosts). [C] de Bruijn–Newman: the forward (dissipative) heat flow creates off-line pairs (TAA Lemma 158, correction 16) — here 'ghost = dissipation' is right. [O] An entropy-production functional built without zeros (R5) whose zero set is Γ ≡ 0: none known.
pitfalls: Γ ≥ 0 is automatic: no content (TAA Lemma 159, correction 12).
In the passivity picture a ghost is gain, not dissipation; in the de Bruijn–Newman picture dissipation creates ghosts: say which (TAA Lemma 159, correction 12).

concepts.name: Observability as Hecke-equivariance: a single modular-invariant observable can fail positivity, the class-group-averaged (Euler-product) ones do not
concepts.plain: At discriminant −20 (class number 2) the Epstein zeta of the single form x² + 5y² is modular-invariant but not Hecke-equivariant; it has the off-line zero 0.9329697 + 15.6682495i (Potter–Titchmarsh) and its Weil form turns negative at L* = 3.025 (quartets from 3.775). Both class-group-averaged objects, ζ_K and the genus product L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), stay positive to L = 8. Conjecture: the observable that can be positive is the Hecke-equivariant one (invariant under the class group or equivariant by a character), so “modular invariance as observability” must be strengthened to Hecke-equivariance, which uses every p-adic place at once. This is the Davenport–Heilbronn mechanism seen from the observer side, not new information about ζ.

concepts.name: Narrowed missing piece (Open): a structural reason for the global cancellation in the prime-to-sequence map (the explicit formula’s balance); a per-prime ferromagnetic sign is refuted in the tested families
concepts.plain: Positivity of the Weil form is not carried by any quantity intrinsic to the window form W: metric, curvature, torsion, thermodynamics, smoothing and the Levinson dynamics are all ghost-blind or causal (they see a ghost only when it arrives). Nor is it carried by any per-prime sign or any per-prime positive-semidefinite or passive allocation: built prime by prime, the form stays indefinite and becomes positive only as a global cancellation once all lags are present. The missing piece is a structural reason for that global cancellation in the map from the primes to the window sequence (the balance in the explicit formula), for example a cohomology carrying a positivity (Deninger’s conjectured cohomology) or a global Lee–Yang-type mechanism. Any exact form of it is RH-strength. The earlier, per-prime version of this entry (each prime a ferromagnetic coupling with a fixed sign) was tested and refuted in the tested families. The Riemann Hypothesis is not proved.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Open. Narrowed in v1.7. (1) W-intrinsic quantities cannot see the sign: the window thermodynamics is invariant under W → W + c while positivity is not [Theorem, TAA Lemma 185 rev. 3]; curvature routes (flat Bochner remainder, abelian prime graph, Λ² operator, Poincaré-disk Verblunsky metric) are ghost-blind [Theorem + Numerical]; Gaussian, heat or imaginary-shift smoothing is ghost-blind [Numerical]; in Levinson/Verblunsky coordinates W ≻ 0 ⇔ all |k_m| < 1, the coefficients are free coordinates, so the chain cannot enforce positivity, and ghost onset is non-perturbative [Theorem + Numerical]. (2) Per-prime structure cannot carry it: a single prime step is an indefinite shift operator [Theorem]; the sign of a prime step is the sign of the gap excess g_p − log p, which takes both signs infinitely often [Theorem]; sharing the positive cushion among primes needs at least 267 times the cushion that exists [Numerical]; Euler factors are passive for ζ and for sign-flipped controls alike, and the cascade is lossy [Theorem]. (3) Positivity appears only once all lags in the window are present (last ~6% of primes) [Numerical]. What remains Open is a structural reason for that global cancellation in the prime-to-sequence map; any exact version is RH-strength (Weil positivity; a bound on the fluctuation is von Koch-strength). History of this entry: Open. The single-spin equivalence RH ⇔ Φ Lee–Yang is a Restatement (immediate from ∫Φ(u)e^{hu}du = ¼ξ(½+h/2)); Newman 1976 does not state it, and the many-spin ferromagnetic version adds nothing (v1.15); only a ferromagnetic construction from the primes would be new. RH is not proved. A Gram factor of the Weil form always exists under RH and is, up to rotation, indexed by the zeros, so reading couplings off the Weil form is circular; a construction must define J_pq from primes and ∞ and prove J_pq ≥ 0 independently. Link (29 Oct 2026): two unit circles. Li's map w = 1 − 1/ρ sends the critical line to |w| = 1, and under RH λₙ = Σ_ρ 2sin²(nθ_ρ/2) [Theorem]; Lee–Yang: ferromagnetic coupling puts the partition-function zeros on |z| = 1 [Theorem]. Correction (v1.6.1): the two circles can be matched. In Li's variable z = 1 − 1/s, F(z) = ξ(1/(1 − z)) satisfies F(1/z) = F(z), has positive Taylor coefficients and a₁/a₀ = λ₁ [Theorem], which is the shape of a Lee–Yang partition function in the fugacity z; RH is then the Lee–Yang property of F [Restatement]. What stays open is a ferromagnetic mechanism that produces F. Nonnegative couplings plus a pole are not enough: sign-shuffled ζ·L(χ₄) fails the window test in 20/20 cases [Numerical]. Li's λₙ ≥ 0 for all n is itself a restatement of RH. The genuine-versus-shuffled angle result reads as ferromagnetic versus frustrated, spin-glass-like coupling [Analogy]. RH is not proved.

Each step is an SU(1,1) boost and positivity is “every step subluminal” (Schur; circular as a criterion) [Theorem]

v1.10: the repair is collective, not an edge-prime effect (ζ needs 88–100% of the terms in either order; the pole plane is blind to Davenport–Heilbronn) [Numerical]. On Davenport–Heilbronn’s ghost 2-plane the archimedean part is positive and ζ’s prime terms never break it, while Davenport–Heilbronn’s own terms break it only late (first after 73–100% of the terms; positive semidefinite at 77–97% of the partial sums): the ghost comes from the prime side [Numerical]

v1.10: one global positive-frequency polarization (“Dirac sea”) fills for ζ at every L ≤ 8 with all Krein signs positive, while Davenport–Heilbronn leaves n₋/2 holes [Numerical; equivalent to n₋ = 0]. The separating geometric quantity is the trace-free shear of log|Ξ|, not its curvature (the Riesz measure is ≥ 0 for every function) [Theorem + Numerical; equivalent to Laguerre]

v1.10: two walls: the parabolic (signature) wall (a² = 4q, Kepler E = 0, Levinson |k| = 1, Hodge–Riemann flip; RH ⇔ ζ never reaches it) and the Routh (Krein-collision) wall downstream (RH ⇒ never reached) [Theorem]. Davenport–Heilbronn: parabolic at L* ≈ 3.6–3.9, an L4-like window, Hopf quartets from L_H ≈ 4.3–4.8; ζ none for L ≤ 8 [Numerical]. The missing grading reads as a Rosati-type time reversal Γ with P = ZΓ positive and invariant for every L [Open]

v1.11: by the Hamiltonian–Krein index n₋ = N_real + 2N_quart + 2N_Krein− (212/212 pencils), positivity of the Weil form is stability plus Krein-definiteness (grading Γ = 1), not merely some grading; Davenport–Heilbronn has a non-trivial Γ on L ∈ [4.025, 4.625] [Theorem + Numerical; circular as a criterion]

v1.11: ζ’s local factors carry no rotation (every Euler factor is massless, on the parabolic wall, m² = 0), the archimedean place is a one-sided cone (π sech πr > 0) and the global form is critical in L, t and Ω, so the missing structure must be global and margin-free [Theorem + Cited + Heuristic]

v1.11: a single modular-invariant observable (the Epstein zeta of x² + 5y²) fails positivity at L* = 3.025 while the class-group-averaged ζ_K and genus L-functions do not; log p enters the modular surface only as the Hecke angle θ_p = t log p, so the polarization must be Hecke-equivariant with the angles coherent across all p and a definite archimedean sign [Numerical + Theorem; Conjecture]
pitfalls: Λ = −4b₀ (not −b₀) in Newman's 1976 normalisation; Ξ-type transform of Φ is ¼ξ(½+iz/2), not ξ(½+iz)

Corrected in v1.6.1: v1.6 said no map between Li's circle and the Lee–Yang circle is known. In Li's variable z = 1 − 1/s, ξ becomes a self-reciprocal series with positive coefficients, so the circles coincide; RH remains the (unproved) Lee–Yang property of that series.

Tested and refuted in v1.7 (tested families): a per-prime ferromagnetic sign. No per-prime sign, per-prime positive-semidefinite allocation or per-prime passive section separates ζ from sign-flipped controls; positivity appears only as a global cancellation once all lags are present. The entry keeps its id; its statement is narrowed, not replaced by a new object.
Do not read “ferromagnetic” as Λ(n) ≥ 0: the primes are nonnegative already; what must stay small is the fluctuation (the zero sum), and nonnegative couplings plus a pole are not enough.
Rank 1 is a manual pin, not a score: the entry’s Heuristic priority is 0.380; it is listed first by an editorial decision of the author, and every other entry keeps its scored order.

Correction (v1.14): Davenport–Heilbronn’s first Weil-window crossings move to L ≈ 3.63 (even) / 3.65 (odd) on fine bases (fine grid M = 320; h = 0.0083), and the second pair to ≈ 4.19/4.21 (h = 0.0083); the values 3.80–3.925 (and 6.3–7.4 for the second pair) quoted here are basis values at h = 0.025 or coarser, where the hat factor s(γh)⁴ attenuates the ghost ordinate. The qualitative statements are unchanged; see dh_crossing_basis_dependence.

Correction (v1.15): Newman 1976 (Proc. AMS 61) classifies the class 𝒫 and shows Φ ∉ 𝒫; it does not state RH ⇔ Lee–Yang for Φ, and no theorem states it for all ferromagnetic J ≥ 0. The single-spin Lee–Yang property of Φ (all zeros of ∫Φ(u)e^{hu}du = ¼ξ(½+h/2) on iℝ) is a Restatement of RH; by continuity at J → 0 the many-spin ferromagnetic version fails exactly when the single-spin one does, so it adds no information (see multispin_adds_nothing).

Demoted in v1.16: the manual rank-1 pin (kept since v1.5) is removed after the Lee–Yang Φ bridge test (single-spin Lee–Yang for Φ is RH; the many-spin version adds nothing; GHS and moment tests are passed by Davenport–Heilbronn too; no damping-invariant local condition can imply Lee–Yang). The entry keeps its id, label and statement; it now sits where its computed priority puts it.

concepts.name: Refined missing piece (v1.15): a positive-by-construction transverse space H₊ for the scaling reduction — a no-ghost theorem with the pole pair as the II₁,₁ part
concepts.plain: What is missing is a Hilbert space H₊, positive for a reason independent of the zeros, with the scaling-reduced Weil form Q = Φ*Φ, where (1) H₊ is positive by construction (Φ = Cholesky(Z_L) is circular); (2) Φ is scaling- and Hecke-equivariant and consistent under window restriction (the analogue of DDF operators commuting with the constraints); (3) Φ is an intertwiner built only from Euler factors and Γ data and is not place-local (a sum Σ_v Φ_v*Φ_v over places is ruled out because every local term is indefinite); (4) the analogue of c = 26 must fail for Davenport–Heilbronn (no Euler product) and for the Beurling control. Equivalently: a no-ghost theorem for the scaling reduction of the adele class space, with the pole pair (signature (1,1)) as the Lorentzian II₁,₁ part and H₊ as the transverse V♮-like factor. No-ghost transports positivity, it does not create it, so H₊ must be known positive independently. Over 𝔽_q all four hold (primitive H² with the Hodge index theorem). No candidate tested satisfies all four; the rank-1 entry (ferromagnetic Φ / Lee–Yang) is positive for Davenport–Heilbronn too, so it fails condition (4) on positivity alone. Any exact form is equivalent to RH. [Conjecture; the restatement RH ⇔ no negative-norm states is a Restatement] The Riemann Hypothesis is not proved.
concepts.label: Conjecture
concepts.core: Refined missing piece (v1.15): a positive-by-construction transverse space H₊ for the scaling reduction — a no-ghost theorem with the pole pair as the II₁,₁ part. Sources: TAA research notes, 3 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: v1.19 correction. For zeta, a map of all compactly supported E0 tests, on every window, into a semidefinite quotient with squared norm exactly W is Weil positivity for zeta. An abstract GNS construction assuming RH can inherit formal compatibilities of W (covariance, window restriction, and the zeros-blind explicit formula) and is circular as a proof. Those compatibilities are not the missing source of the sign. Independent positivity of H+ identified with W, without assuming W >= 0, is what is missing. Not every further demand, including an unspecified Hecke action or a Beurling control, is claimed to follow automatically. Place-local squares cannot match the signed local terms one place at a time. The pole pair as an II_1,1 lattice is an analogy; no arithmetic lattice is constructed. No ample class or compatible J matching W is constructed.
v1.20. The window ledger, the bordered count, and the two failed representers do not construct H+. Open ~1.8 is unchanged. The Riemann Hypothesis is not proved.

concepts.name: A square root G with G*G = Z_L is trivial if Z_L ≥ 0; a non-circular G must be zero-free, non-local, equivariant and independently positive
concepts.plain: If Z_L ≥ 0 a square root always exists, so its existence is RH. A non-circular construction must be built without zeros (Euler factors, Γ and the pole only), non-local in the places, consistent across windows, scaling/Hecke-equivariant, and land in a space that is positive for independent reasons. Over F_q the Frobenius orbit in H¹ with the Rosati form is such a G. Open.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: A square root G with G*G = Z_L is trivial if Z_L ≥ 0; a non-circular G must be zero-free, non-local, equivariant and independently positive. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.plain: Arithmetic quantities are measured relative to a reference fixed by the pole; the "error" is the displacement from that reference.

concepts.core: ψ − x, E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) and the relative Gram all subtract a pole/reference term. TAA Lemma 146 records this as an organizing analogy.

concepts.name: Formal intersection lattice vs geometric surface (ghost-blind vs proof-bearing)
concepts.plain: Numbers arranged as an intersection lattice prove nothing by themselves; on a real surface the Hodge index theorem makes them proof-bearing.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: A formal lattice of intersection numbers (TAA Lemma 150 Ψ_n lattice = Weil's form as a lattice) satisfies whatever identities are built in and was ghost-blind (λ_max −0.416 ζ vs −2.226 DH at K = 90; TAA Lemma 150 Prop 2.3). On C×C the same numbers are proof-bearing because the Hodge index is a theorem about the surface (ample class + RR), proved before the αᵢ are known. The composition law can be imposed consistently on any FE data (fakes, DH): only definiteness separates (TAA Lemma 149 DH prime-side onset 3.85; fakes (2,2)) (TAA Lemma 152, correction 5). What carries the numbers: classes Γ_t with a composition law from a flow, an ample class, RR strong enough for Hodge index.

concepts.name: Band criterion γ < 2T_M
concepts.plain: A ζ zero (or ghost) at height γ is visible in the class-number data only if every Maass form with t_j < γ/2 is known and subtracted; the zero’s frequency γ/2 must lie below the unknown-Maass band.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 148 Prop. band [H, N support]: with T_M = 100 the DH-location ghost (85.699, δ =.3085) has count-matched SNR 238 (x = 1e8) / 270 (x = 1e10); with T_M = 35.4 it is 0.15. γ = 143.1, δ =.1: SNR 4.6 (T_M = 100) vs 0.010 (T_M = 35.4). Reaching height γ needs ≈ γ²/48 Maass forms and the zero list below γ ⇒ the readout only re-derives listed zeros.
concepts.formula: detectable ⇔ γ/2 < T_M (Maass list complete to T_M)
pitfalls: Not a theorem; the noise model treats unknown t_j as random.

concepts.plain: For ζ_ℚ(i) = ζ·L(χ₄) the arithmetic side of the window form is ζ’s plus a pole-free part. concepts.name: A ghost makes the window mechanically unstable
concepts.plain: As T → 0 the pressure is −∂λ_min/∂ℓ, so stability is convexity of the lowest eigenvalue in the window length; a ghost eigenvalue falls concavely and makes the compressibility negative. For genuine ζ the window is stable for ℓ in [3, 6.8]. At finite temperature the instability can appear before positivity fails (ghost at height 79.34: from δ = 0.075 at T = 0.2 against first negative eigenvalue at δ = 0.110), a soft-mode precursor that disappears as T → 0.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: A ghost makes the window mechanically unstable.
pitfalls: Corrected by TAA Lemma 185 rev. 3: the finite-temperature precursor at height 79.34 is an artefact of the finite window range; with the window extended the ghost goes negative at window length 8.26, and the instability appears only at or after the first negative eigenvalue. Mechanical stability also fails for genuine L(Δ) and 11a1 while they are positive, so it is not a proxy for positivity.

concepts.name: For PSL₂(ℤ) the Selberg-side form with the continuous spectrum removed is exactly (n−1, 1), with its negative in the pole plane
concepts.plain: Built from the Selberg trace formula on hat windows (hyperbolic classes, elliptic, identity, parabolic, continuous and λ₀ terms), the cusp-form part is positive semidefinite for every tested size (a check of Selberg’s theorem). Geometric minus continuous has exactly one negative direction for every n ≥ 20, converging to span{e^{±x/2}} (residual 0.02 at L = 8.1). Dropping the continuous term gives 1–7 negatives. The same frame as ζ with the pole removed.

concepts.name: The admissible prime weights form a thin slab: narrow along total mass, about 30 times wider along mass-neutral directions
concepts.plain: Scale the p = 2 atoms by (1 + d cos θ) and the p = 3 atoms by (1 + d sin θ) and ask how large d can be before the window form loses positivity. The allowed region is narrowest near 30–37° (close to the total-mass, i.e. pole, direction) and widest near 127° (roughly mass-neutral). concepts.plain: E: y² = x³ − x over F₉ has a = −6 = −2√q, on the Hasse edge. The companion matrix of (x + 3)² is a Jordan block and fails the similitude test (margin −5·10⁻¹⁰), while the true Frobenius −3I (semisimple, Tate) passes (margin 0.50). For an interior genus-2 curve, y² = x⁵ + 2x + 1 over F₇ with P = x⁴ + 2x³ + 14x + 49 and all |π| = √7, the Rosati trace form is positive definite (minimum eigenvalue 2.14).

concepts.name: Generalized Routh criterion 27(m₁m₂ + m₂m₃ + m₃m₁) < M² verified; Sun–Jupiter needs about 41 Jupiter masses at L4 to reach the wall
concepts.plain: The 12-dimensional rotating-frame linearization of the Lagrange triangle agrees with Routh’s criterion on 400/400 random mass triples and 60/60 within 1% of the wall. Sun–Jupiter has 27μ(1 − μ) = 0.0257, 39 times below the wall; a third mass at L4 reaches it at 0.03903 M_sun = 40.9 Jupiter masses, about 2·10⁹ times the estimated L4 Trojan mass (Vinogradova–Chernetenko 2015). In four-body relative equilibria, a cloud at L4 alone destabilises a test particle at L5 first (at 20.2 Jupiter masses), and split clouds become unstable at 9.2–9.4 Jupiter masses. μ is the secondary’s mass share; massless Trojans do not change it.

concepts.name: Sub-Keplerian gas drag makes L4 less unstable than L5: a decay-rate asymmetry, not an accumulation
concepts.plain: With drag relative to a sub-Keplerian gas (η = 0.01, γ = 0.05, μ = 10⁻³) the equilibria shift to 66.35° and −55.21°, and the libration growth rates are 1.40·10⁻⁴ (L4) against 3.32·10⁻⁴ (L5). In integrations of 400 + 400 mirror-paired test particles, 70 survive at L4 against 2 at L5 at t = 12 000, and the survivor ratio passes the observed 1.4–1.9 after about 476–544 orbits and keeps growing, so any ratio is transient. Small-μ windows of asymptotic stability exist at L4 only. This agrees with Murray (1994); the observed Jupiter Trojan excess (1.4 ± 0.2, Grav et al. 2011; 1.6 ± 0.1, Szabó et al. 2007) is usually attributed to capture during migration (Pirani et al. 2019).
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: No-go: a ferromagnetic sign pattern fixes the shape of the unstable mode, not the number of unstable modes

concepts.name: No rigidity in the Levinson chain: Verblunsky coefficients are free, and ζ's update is expanding
concepts.plain: By Verblunsky's theorem the coefficients (k₁, k₂, …) are free coordinates on positive sequences: any next |k| < 1 extends any past, so the recursion itself cannot carry compatibility across windows [Theorem]. Measured as the sensitivity of each new coefficient to the past ones, genuine ζ is not contracting but expanding, with the update norm growing like ℓ^1.5 to about 49 at window length 16, more than any other positive form tested [Numerical]. Loss of contraction never warns earlier than |k| itself (27 ghost runs), and the contraction measure is essentially a function of |k|, E and the hyperbolic distance to the boundary (R² = 0.998). The only true contraction is the transfer matrix evaluated at the zeros, which needs the zeros and is circular. Any rigidity must come from the prime-to-sequence map, not from the chain.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: No rigidity in the Levinson chain: Verblunsky coefficients are free, and ζ's update is expanding. Sources: Verblunsky (1935); B. Simon, Orthogonal Polynomials on the Unit Circle, AMS 2005; Szegő–Kolmogorov theorem.

concepts.name: Birman–Krein bridge: scattering phase = spectral shift; −φ′/φ = spectral density = Wigner delay = Maass–Selberg intercept
concepts.plain: The scattering phase at the cusp counts states; its derivative is a sum of positive bumps, one pair per zeta zero, whose widths tell where the zero sits.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Birman–Krein (Dokl. 144 (1962) 475–478): det S(λ) = e^{−2πiξ(λ)} [Cs]. Cusp of SL₂(ℤ): S = φ (one cusp), φ(½+it) = Λ(2it)/Λ(1+2it), |φ| = 1 (NUM 3.9e−31, t ≤ 60), so dξ/dt = (1/2π)(−φ′/φ)(½+it) (sign convention). THEOREM (Hadamard; NUM ≤ 3.9e−6 with 1517 zeros + tail): −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1/(¼+t²) + Σ_ρ [a/(a²+(t−γ/2)²) + b/(b²+(t−γ/2)²)], a = (1−β)/2, b = β/2: each zero gives two Lorentzians of mass π (winding ghost-blind), widths ghost-sensitive. The only negative term is the ζ pole term −1/(¼+t²) (negativity t ≤ 2.8; TAA Lemma 153, correction 23 refined). DH (Λ entire): −φ′/φ > 0 everywhere (min 0.41 on [0.5,60]) even with its ghost, so density positivity is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 153, correction 29); ghost = narrow Lorentzians (peak 27.27 at t = 42.84; predicted ghost part 25.84). The ratio across the y-axis = φ; for ζ the analogous ratio is χ(s) = ζ(s)/ζ(1−s), χ(½+it) = e^{−2iθ(t)} gives the smooth part θ/π of N(T).

concepts.name: Hecke p-power recursion as a lattice Klein–Gordon (lossless LC-ladder) transfer matrix: Hasse = passband, and ζ’s local factors sit at the massless band edge
concepts.plain: The local transfer matrix [[c, −1], [1, 0]] ∈ SL₂ with c = a/√q is the transfer matrix of a lossless LC-ladder cell with ω²LC = 2 − c = m², equivalently of the lattice Klein–Gordon equation. Elliptic / parabolic / hyperbolic is passband / band edge / stopband, which over 𝔽_q is Hasse / the wall / a ghost (m² = 2 − 2cosh η < 0). Checked on 543 pairs (q, a); for the curve 11a all 429 primes lie in the band with mean m² = 1.9997 (Sato–Tate mean 2). For ζ every cell sits at m² = 0, the massless band edge (unipotent), so ζ’s global positivity cannot be a cascade of local passbands: the “mass” has to come from the archimedean place and the assembly.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hecke p-power recursion as a lattice Klein–Gordon (lossless LC-ladder) transfer matrix: Hasse = passband, and ζ’s local factors sit at the massless band edge.

concepts.name: Ghost count of the arithmetic side
concepts.plain: Write Weil's form as W = Z + P, with P the rank-2 pole term of signature (1,1) and Z the archimedean-plus-primes side, and restrict to test functions supported in a window of length l. The number of negative squares of Z on the window is at most 1 + N+, where N+ is the number of distinct zeros off the critical line to the right, and for every finite N <= N+ it is at least 1 + N once the window is long enough. So the count increases to 1 + N+. In the combined ledger the pole pair at +-i/2 enters exactly like an off-line zero pair with multiplicity -1; its negative direction is the even (cosh) pole vector, i.e. the Perron mode.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Castelnuovo-Severi and Weil's bound
concepts.plain: On a product of two curves, the defect 2 d1 d2 - D^2 is non-negative for every divisor D (Castelnuovo-Severi). Applied to the diagonal and the graph of Frobenius it gives Weil's bound. An odd number of negative directions (a forbidden set with Euler characteristic 2) therefore forces a real eigenvalue pair, and gyroscopic (Krein) rescue is possible only for even n₋. Checked: odd n₋ ⇒ real pair at both odd Davenport–Heilbronn cutoffs (L = 3.875, 7.375) and 27/27 for the hybrid; ζ and L(11a) have n₋ = 0 everywhere.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Kelvin–Tait–Chetaev parity for the Weil pencil: sign det(D⁻¹Z) = (−1)^n₋, so an odd index forces a real pair and a gyroscopic twist can rescue only even n₋.

concepts.name: The positivity cup at E = 0: bowl / flat / peak = definite / semidefinite / indefinite
concepts.plain: Bowl H = ½(p² + x²) is positive definite (null set a point), flat H = ½p² is semidefinite (null set a line), peak H = ½(p² − x²) = ξη is indefinite (null set an X, the separatrix). Over 𝔽_q these are a² < 4q, a² = 4q (the wall) and a² > 4q (a ghost). For ζ the smallest eigenvalue of the Weil form stays > 0 while flattening toward the wall (basis-limited, roughly e^{−L}); Davenport–Heilbronn flips to a peak at L* ≈ 3.82 and ζ·Davenport–Heilbronn at ≈ 5.24. E = 0 is the critical point of the quadratic; whether it is a minimum, flat or a saddle is the positivity question. The flat case is kinetic energy p²/2 alone: positivity needs a confining term in the missing direction.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Curvature per unit energy: the Riesz measure separates nothing, and a pointwise Witten-type condition fails
concepts.plain: The literal curvature density Δ log|Ξ| = 2πΣδ_ρ is ≥ 0 for ζ and Davenport–Heilbronn alike; only its location differs (Davenport–Heilbronn has one zero in each box [84, 88] × [0.05, 0.6] and [112, 116] × [0.05, 0.6], ζ none). In a Weitzenböck-type split Z = T + R (T = D*D), positivity ⇔ κ_min = min⟨Rv, v⟩/⟨Tv, v⟩ ≥ −1: ζ sits at −1 + O(1e−9) at every L, Davenport–Heilbronn at −1.06 / −1.62 / −2.99 for L = 4 / 6 / 8. ζ’s curvature term R is negative, so there is no pointwise dominant-energy condition: positivity must be an operator inequality T ≥ −R (Hardy/Sobolev type), not R ≥ 0.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: RH for zeta-built functions without Euler product
concepts.plain: Weng zeta functions of reductive groups over Q are finite combinations of completed zeta ratios with a functional equation and no Euler product; RH is proved for rank 2 and Sp(4), and for all but finitely many zeros in the Chevalley case under a geometric hypothesis.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Levinson/Schur steps are SU(1,1) boosts: Weil positivity = every step subluminal
concepts.plain: Each Schur/Levinson step of the Toeplitz Weil form is the boost B(k) = [[1, k], [k, 1]]/√(1 − k²), with velocity k = v/c, rapidity artanh k and γ = 1/√(1 − k²). E_M/E_{M−1} = 1 − k_M² = 1/γ_M² (checked to 2e−16 for ζ, 3e−14 for Davenport–Heilbronn), so the Lorentz factors multiply (Π γ_m² = E₀/E_M) and collinear rapidities add (to 1e−6); at z = e^{iθ} the composition carries a Thomas–Wigner rotation. Weil positivity ⇔ every step is subluminal, |k| < 1 (Schur). On span{pole, g} positivity is reverse Cauchy–Schwarz, the inequality behind the twin paradox. ζ: max |k| = 0.384 up to L = 8; Davenport–Heilbronn first reaches |k| ≥ 1 at L = 3.85 (k = 1.23), ζ·Davenport–Heilbronn at 5.075, exactly at their walls. Over 𝔽_q, k₁ = −a/(2√q) exactly, so the speed limit is the Hasse bound.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Levinson/Schur steps are SU(1,1) boosts: Weil positivity = every step subluminal.

concepts.name: Shear, not curvature: the trace-free Hessian of log|Ξ| is the Turán/Laguerre quantity
concepts.plain: u = log|Ξ(t + iy)| is harmonic off the zeros, so Hess u = [[u_tt, u_ty], [u_ty, −u_tt]] is pure shear (u_tt = Re(log Ξ)″) and its trace Δu = 2πΣδ_ρ (the curvature) vanishes off the zeros. On the line u_tt = −λ(t): ζ has u_tt < 0 at all 3900 samples with t ≤ 200; Davenport–Heilbronn flips (shear axes rotate by 90°) at 17 samples in t ≈ 85–86 and 114, exactly its ghost heights. This explains why Jacobi-metric curvature (a trace) was blind to the trace-free Turán part. As an RH criterion it is the Laguerre / Laguerre–Pólya condition (circular).
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Signed (holomorphic) energy detects every ghost before it lands
concepts.plain: Allowing complex zeros, the pair energy sum of (z_j - z_k)^-2 is signed: a conjugate ghost pair contributes a negative term that diverges as it lands on the real axis. For polynomials, real-rootedness is equivalent to this energy staying positive for all forward heat times, and the energy is computable from coefficients alone as a companion-matrix trace. For zeta this restates RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Signed (holomorphic) energy detects every ghost before it lands.

concepts.name: Sum-of-squares form of the window Weil form: Levinson/Szegő factor, and positivity as "no predictor root inside the disk"
concepts.plain: Toeplitz Cholesky is the Levinson recursion: A Z Aᵀ = diag(E_k), with the rows of A the backward predictor (Szegő) polynomials, so Z(g) = Σ E_k |⟨a_k, g⟩|² (checked to 3e-11 for ζ, 2e-9 for Davenport–Heilbronn). Positivity of the window form is equivalent to all pivots E_k > 0, and (Schur–Cohn) to no root of the reversed predictor lying inside the unit disk. As an RH criterion this is circular; its value is that the failure is localized.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Bochner–Raychaudhuri identity for log|Ξ|: Turán/Laguerre is the shear term of the focusing equation
concepts.plain: For the gradient congruence of u = log|Ξ|, the expansion θ = Δu vanishes off the zeros and the rotation vanishes, so the Raychaudhuri/Bochner identity reduces to Δ(½|∇u|²) = 2σ² with σ² = |(log Ξ)″|². On the critical line σ = |λ(t)|, with λ the Laguerre/Turán quantity, and the sign of λ is the orientation of the shear axes; Laguerre–Pólya is the statement that they never flip. Checked for ζ at 7 points (4 on the line, 3 off), maximal relative error 8e−5 (finite-difference limited). ζ never flips for t ≤ 200; Davenport–Heilbronn flips at its ghost heights.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Bochner–Raychaudhuri identity for log|Ξ|: Turán/Laguerre is the shear term of the focusing equation.

concepts.name: dBN zero flow = gradient flow + Calogero–Moser symplectic lift; not conformally symplectic
concepts.plain: The first-order zero flow contracts phase volume at rate −2 dS/dt. That rate is state-dependent, so the flow is not conformally symplectic. Differentiating again gives Calogero–Moser, z̈_j = −8Σ(z_j−z_k)⁻³, which is Hamiltonian, with H_CM = 0 on the dBN submanifold (6e−14). Dissipation = entropy production; the symplectic part is the CM lift.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: dBN zero flow = gradient flow + Calogero–Moser symplectic lift; not conformally symplectic. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026; Calogero 1971 doi:10.1063/1.1665604; Moser 1975 doi:10.1016/0001-8708(75)90151-6.

concepts.name: Davenport–Heilbronn has a positive, even, log-concave Φ kernel
concepts.plain: Λ_DH(½+iz/2) = ∫₀^∞ Φ_DH(u)cos(zu)du with Φ_DH(u) = 8√(π/5)e^{3u}Σa(n)n·exp(−πn²e^{4u}/5). The functional equation makes Φ_DH even, and the n = 1 term dominates the rest (Σ_{n≥2} n e^{−π(n²−1)/5} < 0.33), so Φ_DH > 0. Numerically it is log-concave on [0, 1.6] (max (log Φ)″ = −10.2). So kernel positivity, kernel entropy, heat capacity and low-order Turán inequalities cannot separate ζ from a counterexample.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Davenport–Heilbronn has a positive, even, log-concave Φ kernel. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026; Polymath 2019 doi:10.1007/s40687-019-0193-1.

concepts.name: S(T) = (1/π) arg ζ(½+iT): the fluctuating remainder of N(T)
concepts.plain: The zero count is a smooth main term plus a wiggly remainder S(T); a fake zero off the line only shows up when the count is compared with the sign changes on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: N(T) = θ(T)/π + 1 + S(T) (ζ); the smooth part is the phase winding of χ, S(T) the remainder. Ghost status (TAA Lemma 153, correction 28): S(T) and N(T) count ALL zeros in the strip (argument principle), so S(T) alone is ghost-blind; the ghost shows only against the on-line count N₀(T) (Hardy-Z sign changes): DH 62 sign changes vs N = 66 on [10,120], deficits exactly 2 in [80,90] and [110,120] (TAA Lemma 152). The cusp phase φ smooths S out: its zero information arrives as Lorentzians of width ≥ min(β,1−β)/2.

concepts.name: In Li's variable ξ is a self-reciprocal series with positive coefficients
concepts.plain: Put z = 1 − 1/s and F(z) = ξ(1/(1 − z)). The functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s) becomes F(1/z) = F(z), the critical line becomes the unit circle |z| = 1, every Taylor coefficient of F at z = 0 is positive, and a₁/a₀ = λ₁, Li's first coefficient. This is the shape of a Lee–Yang partition function in the fugacity z, so Li's circle and the Lee–Yang circle are the same circle in this variable. RH is then the Lee–Yang property of F (a Restatement); nothing is proved about the zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: In Li's variable ξ is a self-reciprocal series with positive coefficients.
concepts.formula: F(z) = ξ(1/(1−z)) = Σ aₙzⁿ, aₙ > 0, F(1/z) = F(z), a₁/a₀ = λ₁ = 1 + γ/2 − ½log 4π
pitfalls: Positivity of coefficients is proved: ξ(½ + w) = Σ b_k w^{2k} with b_k > 0 and w = (1 + z)/(2(1 − z)) has positive coefficients. It does not imply that the zeros lie on |z| = 1; that is RH.

concepts.plain: Connes and Consani proved Riemann–Roch for the compactified Spec ℤ, counting sections by integer numbers of generators; it is a one-dimensional "χ = degree + constant" law and cannot see D².

concepts.name: Oscillator semigroup: positive ⇔ real A with symplectic eigenvalues ≤ 1 (archimedean, ghost-blind)
concepts.plain: Positive Gaussian operators exist exactly on the stable (rotation) side; this is real but archimedean, so it cannot tell ζ from a fake.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: [C] Dereziński–Karczmarczyk arXiv:1701.07297 Prop. 10: a·Op(e^{−A}) (A ∈ Sym++(ℂ^{2d})) is Hermitian iff a ∈ ℝ, A real; positive iff a > 0 and A ∈ Sym_p(ℝ^{2d}) (σ(Aθ) ⊂ [−1,1]); following Howe. [T,N] d = 1: Op(e^{−λ(x²+p²)}) = r^N/(1+λ), r = (1−λ)/(1+λ): positive iff λ ≤ 1; normalized elements are contractions with generator −N (harmonic oscillator, the rotation side). The IHO quadratic x² − p² is indefinite, so its Gaussians are not in the positive cone. [T] dissipative A ⇒ Re⟨(λ−A)⁻¹x,x⟩ > 0 for Re λ > 0 (Carathéodory). [R] A contraction semigroup whose generator realizes {ρ − ½} would give Lagarias's Re ξ′/ξ > 0 and, with the functional equation, RH. [A] the oscillator semigroup itself has spectrum {−n}, unrelated to zeros: 'contraction ⇒ no gain lines' is an analogy for it.

pitfalls: Re A > 0 gives bounded operators, not positive ones (positive needs A real, Prop. 10).
Contraction alone + FE would already force β = ½ if the zeros were its spectrum: the content is the realization, not the sign.

concepts.name: Width → area → 2-form: (1/2π)Δ log|ξ| dσ∧dt = Σ δ_ρ
concepts.plain: A zero’s line always has area π however wide it is; stacking these areas over the strip gives the 2-form that counts zeros, and RH would need that count to come from a positive pairing.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Re ξ′/ξ(σ+it) = ∂_σ log|ξ|; each line has area π·sgn(σ−β) independent of its width (width × height = 1); crossing σ = β the area jumps by 2π = flux of ∇log|ξ| around ρ; Poincaré–Lelong/Jensen: (1/2π)Δ log|ξ| dσ∧dt = Σ_ρ δ_ρ (BIB). [N] TAA Lemma 154 fitted amplitudes = 1 to ≤ 3.4e−5 (area π); DH ghost-1 near amplitude −1 at d = 0.30, +1 at d = 0.35. [R] Pairing the 2-form with test functions = zero side of Weil's explicit formula; making it positive = MP4. Local areas are ghost-blind in total; their sign seen from σ > ½ is ghost-sensitive.

concepts.core: 27 per-prime SU(2)/Satake data (a_{p^k}/p^{k/2} = U_k(cos θ_p); 11a1: √12·U₂(−1/√2)·U₁(−1/(2√3)) = −2 = a₁₂; Flath; per-prime Rankin–Selberg ½ ⊗ ½ = Sym² ⊕ ζ). 28 per-prime norm identities (a_p² + |α−ᾱ|² = 4p; (p+1)² − (p−1)² = 4p, m = 2√p, v = (p−1)/(p+1); Kepler |A|² + 2m|E|L² = (mk)²): algebraic, true for every Satake pair. 29 correspondence alone: Jacquet–Langlands via the Shimizu theta lift, Langlands functoriality (Ramanujan via Symⁿ, not RH; Lafforgue used Deligne's RH as input) (not opened). 30 KMS/coefficient (Bochner) positivity (TAA Lemma 164): the Epstein ghost passes. 31 a compact real form on the zero side used as input (TAA Lemma 163): circular. 32 single-place data of n! (Γ, v_p, Γ_p, Gauss sums; the product formula as an identity). Each is ghost-blind or circular; requirements R1–R8′ unchanged.

concepts.name: The Maass–Selberg truncated norm for SL₂(ℤ) verified by direct integration over the truncated fundamental domain, and positive for all T ≥ 1
concepts.plain: ‖ΛᵀE(·,½+it)‖² = 2 log T − φ′/φ(½+it) + (φ̄T^{2it} − φT^{−2it})/(2it), with φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s), agrees with direct integration of |ΛᵀE|² (K-Bessel expansion) to ≤ 5·10⁻¹⁵ in six cases, and is positive on t ∈ [0.02, 60] for T = 1…20. It reads ζ only at 2s, the doubled variable.

concepts.name: With the conductor removed, a smaller L(1, χ_{−d}) gives a larger Weil-form margin; up to L ≈ 4 this is the window’s own small-prime average of χ
concepts.plain: Given log d, smaller L(1, χ_{−d}) (smaller class number) goes with a larger window margin (partial correlation −0.88 at L = 1, −0.70 at 4, −0.48 at 8, negative in every bin). Up to L ≈ 4 this is fully explained by the small-prime average of χ inside the window; log L(1, χ) adds information only for L ≳ 5. Not a positivity mechanism.

concepts.name: First 10⁵ ζ zeros: nearest-neighbour spacings are GUE-like (KS 0.021 against 0.298 for Poisson), with the residual shrinking with height
concepts.plain: Unfolded spacings of the first 10⁵ zeros give a Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance 0.021 to the GUE (Gaudin) law and 0.298 to Poisson; the residual drops from 0.029 to 0.020 across blocks, the known finite-height drift (Bogomolny et al., cited). Spacing statistics are a symptom, not a positivity.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: First 10⁵ ζ zeros: nearest-neighbour spacings are GUE-like (KS 0.021 against 0.298 for Poisson), with the residual shrinking with height. Sources: TAA research notes, 2–3 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: The twist Gram is blind off the centre: identical rows for twists with different L(E_D, s) at s = 1.5, 2
concepts.plain: Four pairs of twists, e.g. (−15, −20) and (−56, −136), have identical Gram rows although their L(E_D, s) differ at s = 1.5 and 2 (0.627 against 0.808 at s = 2). The Gram sees only the centre; a Gram over s would be the Weil form itself, which is circular.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The twist Gram is blind off the centre: identical rows for twists with different L(E_D, s) at s = 1.5, 2. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: Base-regularity test (B) and the B* no-go: B* (Euler product + counting error O(x^θ), θ < ½ ⇒ RH) appears false — a deterministic discretization of a continuous Beurling system keeps an exact zero at 0.75 ± 10i while the measured counting exponent is θ̂ ≈ 0.29 up to x = 5·10⁷ (Numerical refutation; asymptotic θ < ½ not proved); integer-counting error over 9 systems: ℤ bounded (≤ 1), Davenport–Heilbronn bounded, Epstein and ζ_Q(i) θ̂ ≈ 0.32, random discretizations at order √x
concepts.plain: To separate the genuine integers from imitations, count how many 'integers' lie below x and compare with the expected straight line. For ℤ the error never exceeds 1. Imitation number systems built with random or slightly shifted primes wobble by about √x, which first suggested a conjecture (B*): a system with unique factorization whose wobble stays well below √x must satisfy RH. That now looks false. Choosing the imitation primes deterministically, so that they track a smooth system with a planted zero off the line, keeps unique factorization and keeps the planted zero exactly, yet the wobble grows only like x^0.29 as far as it was computed (x = 5·10⁷). So counting regularity alone does not force RH. This is numerical evidence, not a proof: nobody has shown the exponent stays below ½ forever.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: [N] B* (Euler product + N(x) = ρx + O(x^θ), θ < ½ ⇒ RH) appears false: a deterministic discretization of the continuous Beurling system below (g-primes chosen greedily so that the prime-counting discrepancy, prime powers included, stays ≤ 1) keeps an exact zero at 0.75 ± 10i, because ζ_P = ζ_T·e^H with H holomorphic on Re s > 0 [T, given the continuous system], while the measured counting exponent is θ̂ ≈ 0.29 up to x = 5·10⁷ (max|N − ρx| ≈ 4.3·x^0.3; ratio to √x falls from 0.61 to 0.116). Asymptotic θ < ½ is not proved, so this is a numerical refutation, not a theorem. Compare Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer (2006) and Broucke–Vindas (arXiv 2102.08478); prior examples were not exhaustively searched. Consequence: integer-counting regularity is a no-go as a route to RH on its own. [N] Earlier controls to X = 10⁷: random (Poisson) discretizations and integer-supported random multiplicities fluctuate at order √x; that √x noise came from the prime-counting discrepancy, not from discreteness [H]. [T] continuous system ζ_C = (s − ρ₀)(s − ρ̄₀)(s + 10)/(s²(s − 1)), N_C = ρx + O(log² x), positivity min f/t = 0.193 (computer-assisted). [C] DMV 2006 (θ > ½, RH fails), Zhang (RH with regular N), BDV 2020 (RH with large N oscillation), Hilberdink 2005 (the integer and prime exponents cannot both be < ½; not contradicted here, since the prime count is far from li x).
numbers: deterministic discretization: θ̂ ≈ 0.28–0.29 up to x = 5·10⁷ (2,994,465 g-primes); max|N − ρx| ≈ 4.3·x^0.3; ratio to √x 0.61 → 0.116
ψ regression coefficient on the planted term 0.9999993
random controls, ratio to √x: PERT 0.19–0.28; CRAMER 0.6–1.4; ZERO 1.6–2.0; RANDMULT 3.1–4.4
concepts.uncertain: Numerical refutation: θ < ½ for the discretized system is not proved asymptotically; prior examples in the literature were not exhaustively searched.
pitfalls: θ̂ are finite-range slopes (x ≤ 5·10⁷); θ < ½ asymptotically is not proved.
B* was earlier listed as a live conjecture; it is withdrawn on this numerical evidence.
Euler product + counting data still excludes Davenport–Heilbronn and Epstein, but only through the Euler product.

Schur powers stay PSD but heal DH (min 0.13).

concepts.plain: Building the transfer matrix T(a) on the positive part of the reflected form gives about 50% non-positive eigenvalues for every system, with no ζ/DH signal. A matrix-pencil fit finds Davenport–Heilbronn’s off-line ordinate (85.71 against 85.699) but also spurious off-circle nodes for ζ and 11a, so it cannot certify anything.

concepts.name: The bulk form B keeps the diagonal counterterm, on E0 and off it
concepts.plain: B is the spring energy minus M_A times the norm squared. It is defined for every window test, not only for E0. On E0 it coincides with W, because P has been killed. Off E0, W and B differ by P.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: B(F) = H_A(F) - M_A ||F||^2 = (1/2 pi) integral m_A(x) |Fourier F(x)|^2 dx, with m_A the archimedean symbol minus the cosine sum over log n < A. Do not infer infinite rank from unboundedness alone: a finite-rank form made of unbounded linear functionals can be unbounded. The corrected reason uses high frequency. Re psi(1/4 + i x/2) tends to +infinity, while the prime cosine sum is bounded by 2 sum a_n, so some X has m_A(x) at least 1 for |x| at least X. Then B(F) is at least ||F||^2 minus (1+M_A) times the form of the compact time-band-limiting operator K_X, the window compression of the Fourier cutoff |frequency| < X. On the closed finite-codimension subspace where K_X is smaller than 1/(2(1+M_A)), B is at least half the norm squared. That subspace meets smooth E0 on the window in an infinite-dimensional set. So on E0, where W equals B, the form is positive definite on an infinite-dimensional subspace. A map into a finite-dimensional V whose pulled-back pairing equals W would vanish on a kernel of codimension at most dim V, and that kernel would meet the positive subspace. A fixed finite H^{1,1} cannot carry W. The same estimate says B has only finitely many negative directions on one window. That is an analytic description of one window. It is not Weil positivity, and it is not a claim that the form is close to being positive. The geometric target of the right size is not constructed.
concepts.formula: B = H_A - M_A ||F||^2 = (1/2 pi) integral m_A |F-hat|^2
concepts.uncertain: Self-adjointness, compact resolvent, and discrete spectrum of the infinite-dimensional operator B are not proved. Finite Galerkin matrices are the setting of the inertia counts.
concepts.proved: The quadratic-form identity is the ledger. Unboundedness of the symbol is the reason a finite-rank pullback cannot match B on E0.
concepts.tests: Do not promote a finite positive Galerkin matrix to analytic positivity.
pitfalls: Do not write unbounded, therefore not finite rank.
Finitely many negative directions on one window is not a sign theorem.
B inverse applied to the constraint is not an independent constructor, and the infinite-dimensional domain is unproved.

concepts.name: Two explicit representers fail; an independent matching map is still missing
concepts.plain: The bordered criterion would become a construction if a vector h were built from Gamma data, prime data, and the boundary, without inverting B, and if that vector carried the constraint and a negative square. Two candidates were written down in advance. Both fail. The failure of those two is proved, on the stated domain. A general no-go is not.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The identity asked for is B(h, F) = kappa C(F) on the window, equivalently a response equal to kappa cosh(v/2) almost everywhere, for even h. h1 = cosh(u/2) times the window indicator fails at A = 0.6 and at A = 1. The proof splits the archimedean integral at a fixed small a0. The untruncated comparison with the smooth continuation cosh(u/2) diverges, because the Gamma integrand tends to -cosh(v/2) at infinity and cosh sits at the Gamma pole. From a0 to infinity the integrand stays bounded, since h1 is bounded and compactly supported. On the short interval the smooth piece is integrable and the missing translate produces (cosh(L/2)/2) log(1/d) plus a bounded term. The coefficient 1/2 is the one in that expansion. A refinement records a rise of about 0.689 to 0.691 per factor of four in d, against (1/2) log 4 = 0.693. The Jc/Js decomposition in the parent audit is the same split. h2, the Dirichlet cosh, removes the edge logarithm. At A = 1, where the only prime power inside the window is 2, h2 fails because the response has a slope jump a_2 sinh(A/4)/2 = 0.06191 at ±(log 2 - A/2). That jump is exact under those hypotheses. At A = 0.6 the h2 residual is 6.92 percent, numerical only. Polynomial tests F = (d^2/du^2 - 1/4)G with G = (1-t^2)^2 t^k are piecewise polynomial, not smooth; they lie in the form domain, and they lie in E0 by integration by parts using G = G' = 0 at the edges. They disprove the identity on that domain. The smooth case of h1 and of h2 at A = 1 goes through the annihilator lemma. Density of smooth E0 tests in the form domain is plausible and not proved. The missing theorem is a vector h_A, built independently of B inverse, with the full response including M_A and every prime edge, with B(h_A, h_A) < 0, and with both sector conditions. The sector count is the RH-strength half. No such vector is constructed.
concepts.formula: B(h, ·) = kappa C on E0 tests iff the response lies in span{cosh, sinh}
numbers: h1 least-squares residuals, numerical: 37.9 percent at A = 0.6, 19.1 percent at A = 1.
h2 at A = 1, numerical residual about 3.0 percent, on top of the exact jump.
h2 at A = 0.6: residual 6.92 percent, stable across three grids, still only numerical.
concepts.uncertain: Missing theorem, not a result: construct h_A from Gamma, prime, and boundary data, independently of B inverse, so that B(h_A, F) = kappa C(F) + kappa' S(F) for every window F, including the diagonal M_A and the prime-translated edge layers; B(h_A, h_A) < 0; and both sector conditions hold. A finite singular orbit, a 1/log edge law, and a Gamma-only no-go are conjectural. Whether B inverse cosh equals cosh minus a finite edge-layer sum is a conjecture, and only when the inverse exists.
concepts.proved: Failure of h1 at both widths, and failure of h2 at A = 1 under log 2 < A < log 3, on the form domain and on smooth tests via the annihilator lemma. Parent audit, Propositions 4 and 5.
concepts.tests: A proposed h that is defined as B inverse c, or that is checked only on even tests, or that drops the prime shifts, does not meet the missing theorem.
pitfalls: Only these two candidates are excluded. There is no universal Gamma-only no-go.
Do not prove the h1 edge by an untruncated integral against the smooth continuation of cosh. That integral diverges. Split at a fixed small a0.
Polynomial tests are piecewise and not smooth. A density argument from smooth E0 tests is not proved.
B inverse c is not an independent constructor.
Infinite-dimensional invertibility is unproved.
The Riemann Hypothesis is not proved.

concepts.name: A translation-invariant complex structure does not preserve the window kernel
concepts.plain: If the metric is translation-invariant and nonnegative, the Hilbert transform supplies a complex structure compatible with it. That operator does not preserve compact support, and it does not preserve E0. A complex structure for the window form has to move with the window. None has been built. Rank 1 and the open score near 1.8 are unchanged.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: On the line, a nonnegative translation-invariant symbol has the Hilbert transform as a compatible J: the Hamiltonian vector field is minus J times the gradient, and real and imaginary time differ by that J. The Hilbert transform of a compactly supported function is not compactly supported. The two moment constraints that cut out E0 are not preserved. So a J for the window sector, if it exists, is not a convolution operator. Robertson-Schrödinger positivity is positivity of a covariance, diagonals plus a determinant of a 2 by 2 block, once an observable is chosen. There is no canonical time operator in that identity. Weight-12 modular calibrations, including E10 = E4 E6, B10 = 5/66, and the Wronskian of Q^3 and R^2, were rechecked symbolically in the session. They do not select the archimedean counterterm: 2(psi(k/2) - log 2 pi) is not k/12.
concepts.formula: X_H = -J grad H; Hilbert J does not preserve C_c or E0
numbers: B10 = 5/66. The weight identity 2(psi(k/2) - log 2 pi) versus k/12 fails at the weights checked in k0_weight.txt.
concepts.proved: The support obstruction for the Hilbert transform is classical Fourier analysis and is the exact finite-dimensional-versus-window point recorded here. The modular identities are symbolic and were already checked in the session script fam1954_exact.py; the weight mismatch is an inequality of special values.
concepts.tests: A proposed J that is a convolution, or that is positive for a Beurling system as well, does not answer rank 1.
pitfalls: This obstruction does not construct a non-stationary J.
Open ~1.8 is unchanged. Rank 1, kahler_triple_polarization, is unchanged.
Weight 12 is a calibration, not the counterterm K0.

concepts.name: Wick rotation of one Euler frame: t = 2cos θ → 2cos(iφ) = 2cosh φ; elliptic (bounded U_k, poles on |u| = 1 = local unitarity) → parabolic (k + 1, double pole) → hyperbolic (sinh growth); endpoint φ = ½ log p is ζ(s)ζ(s−1) (Eisenstein)
concepts.plain: Each prime's Euler factor is one frame. Changing cos θ to cos(iφ) = cosh φ slides it from bounded oscillation, through the meeting point, to exponential growth. The far end of the slide is exactly the Euler factor of ζ(s)ζ(s−1). An Euler factor never vanishes, so this moves poles, not zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] 1/(1 − tu + u²) = Σ U_k(t/2)u^k, u = p^{½−s} (arithmetic s, weight 2) = p^{−s'} (analytic). Elliptic t = 2cos θ: c_k = sin((k+1)θ)/sin θ, poles e^{±iθ}; parabolic t = 2: c_k = k + 1, double pole u = 1; hyperbolic θ = iφ: c_k = sinh((k+1)φ)/sinh φ, poles e^{±φ}, Re s = ½ ∓ φ/log p. φ = ½ log p: t = √p + 1/√p, factor = 1/((1 − p^{−s})(1 − p^{1−s})), Hecke eigenvalue 1 + p (weight-2 Eisenstein). sl₂: tr exp X = 2cos √det X (det X = θ², 0, −k²). [T] No Euler factor vanishes; a convergent product of non-zero factors is non-zero (zeros only after continuation). [N] errors ≤ 5e−30; ζ(s)ζ(s−1) identity 3.4e−31; sl₂ 6.3e−14 (300 X). |u| = 1 is local unitarity (tempered), NOT the critical line (Re s = 1 arithmetic) (TAA Lemma 160, correction 3). Cusp forms elliptic (Eichler–Shimura + Weil; Deligne); Maass: Ramanujan open, Kim–Sarnak 7/64 bounds the hyperbolic excursion. [A] physics Wick rotation rotates time, here the angle/frequency is rotated (TAA Lemma 160, correction 7). TAA Lemma 162: ζ frames are exactly the four-squares/Eisenstein frames r₄(p)/8 = p + 1; KS coupling-constant metamorphosis ω² = −E/2 is the oscillator version of cos θ → cosh φ.
concepts.formula: cosh φ = cos(iφ); 1/(1 − 2cosh φ·u + u²) = Σ sinh((k+1)φ)/sinh φ · u^k
numbers: p = 5, φ = ½ log 5: poles 1/√5, √5 (Re s = 1, 0)
pitfalls: Local poles never lie on the critical line of a cusp form (TAA Lemma 160, correction 3).

concepts.name: Morse picture of the strata: lobes (extrema), wedge (saddle level), hyperbolic windows (index 1)
aliases: lobes vs wedges vs hyperbolic windows
concepts.plain: Near a non-degenerate critical point a function looks like a quadratic form: a minimum gives closed elliptical loops (lobes), a saddle gives hyperbolas, and the level through the saddle is a pair of crossing lines (the wedge).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Morse lemma: near a non-degenerate critical point f = f(p) ± x² ± y² in suitable coordinates. Index 0 or 2: level sets are closed ellipse-like loops (J. W. McGreevy’s lobes). Index 1: level sets are hyperbolas and the critical level is a crossing line pair (the pure wedge, the dual conic of which is a double point: dual_conic). det Hess = 0 is the degenerate parabolic case (a² = 4q, double line). This is the local version of conic_type_at_infinity, and the block test of blockwise_weil_diagnostic: an off-line pair gives an index-1 (hyperbolic) 2×2 block, a ‘hyperbolic window’ (DH: [84.36,84.77], [85.48,85.91], [114.04,114.29], TAA Lemma 153). [A] Identification with the animation frames.
concepts.uncertain: Chat-level concept; not a lemma result. Morse lemma not opened at source.
pitfalls: Standard Morse lemma; no source opened in a lemma. The reading of the animation frames is an Analogy (code lost, TAA Lemma 152, correction 11).

concepts.name: Toeplitz / Verblunsky coefficients
concepts.plain: Positivity of Toeplitz matrices ⇔ |α_n| < 1; each step a boost of rapidity artanh|α|.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 112 [C Simon]: Carathéodory–Toeplitz–Herglotz; T_{n+1} ≻ 0 ⇔ |α_j| < 1 ∀j < n; n₋(T_N) = #{E_n < 0}, sign flips at each |α_j| > 1. Levinson: PD ⇔ |κ_j| < 1, each step a boost of rapidity artanh κ (true |κ| < 1 for 60 orders; ghost κ₈ = −1.0009). TAA Lemma 117: U(1,1) boost of velocity |α|; |α| > 1 = Krein swap ∘ boost. TAA Lemma 37/TAA Lemma 118: Schur/Verblunsky layer stripping = restatement (circular).

concepts.name: Zeros as frames: simple real zero = elliptic, double zero = parabolic (collision), conjugate pair/quartet = hyperbolic; real zeros leave the line only by collision or from infinity
concepts.plain: Think of each zero on the line as a frame that is still elliptic. Two zeros can leave the line only by first merging into a double zero, the parabolic moment, and then splitting into a mirror pair off the line. The only other route is for off-line zeros to come in from infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] For a continuous family F_t of real entire functions (e.g. de Bruijn–Newman H_t, Rodgers–Tao convention H_t(z) = ∫₀^∞ e^{tu²}Φ(u)cos(zu)du, H_0(z) = ξ(½ + iz/2)/8): (a) a simple real zero stays simple and real for nearby t (Hurwitz + conjugation symmetry); (b) non-real zeros come in pairs z, z̄ (quartets ±z, ±z̄ for even F_t = TAA Lemma 103 ghost quartet); (c) a real zero becomes non-real inside a bounded region only through a real zero of multiplicity ≥ 2 at the transition; otherwise non-real zeros arrive from infinity. [A] Spectral reading: separated F ≠ V on the circle / F = V merge / hyperbolic split (TAA Lemma 158 §H). [N] independent quadrature: zeros 4, 5 of H_t collide at t* = −3.954792524, x* = 66.1974676 (TAA Lemma 111 −3.954792522, diff 2.2e−9), ∂²H ≠ 0 (double); box |Re z − x*| ≤ 4, |Im z| ≤ 1.5: argument principle 2.000000 at t* + 0.05, t* − 0.05, t* − 0.3, real zeros 2, 0, 0; pair 66.4147 ± 0.7812i at t* − 0.3; fold law |Im| ∝ (t* − t)^{1/2} (Polymath §3; TAA Lemma 111 fit 0.51). [T, KGL] only opposite Krein signs exit (4×4 toy, ε = 0.2: window |ω₁ − ω₂| < 0.2, max Re λ 0.0995; same sign ≤ 2.2e−16); graphical Krein sign of H_t alternates (−,+,… on zeros 1–8), so every adjacent pair is a possible exit.
numbers: box count 2.000000 across collision; real count 2 → 0
pitfalls: Global zeros are not frame mergers: no Euler factor vanishes (TAA Lemma 160, correction 1, TAA Lemma 160, correction 4).
Zeros can also arrive from infinity; Hurwitz is local (TAA Lemma 160, correction 11).

concepts.name: Hasse is the parabolic wall; Rosati positivity makes the Routh wall unreachable
concepts.plain: Mode by mode, a stable normal mode corresponds to a Frobenius pair; Hasse a² = 4q is the one-mode (parabolic) wall. Routh is a two-mode collision of opposite Krein signs. Rosati positivity makes all Frobenius pairs Krein-definite, so by Krein–Gelfand–Lidskii collisions are strongly stable (164 genus-2 collisions, max Re 7.8e-16 vs 1.6e-2 at L4 at μ_R). The formal map μ ↔ a/2√q is false: same discriminant, opposite stable side.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hasse is the parabolic wall; Rosati positivity makes the Routh wall unreachable. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.
numbers: research-note score: 4.2 (0.6·significance + 0.4·probability of progress, each on 0–5)

concepts.name: Sundman clock for the F/V collision
concepts.plain: Using the trace a as time and the gap as the conformal factor (dt = gap dtau), the F/V sweep becomes a harmonic oscillator a = 2 sqrt(q) cos(tau). Frobenius and Verschiebung become entire functions of tau, the Hasse bound is the classically allowed region, and the F = V collision is a turning point where the motion bounces. Crossing to the indefinite side needs imaginary tau (the Wick rotation).

concepts.name: The space of binary quadratic forms as the elliptic-curve analogue: definite forms = CM points (elliptic), D = 0 = the cusp (parabolic), indefinite forms = closed geodesics of length 2 log ε_D (hyperbolic)
concepts.plain: The discriminant b² − 4ac is the signature-(2,1) form on binary quadratic forms, and a matrix M corresponds to the form (c, d − a, −b) with discriminant tr(M)² − 4, so |tr| <, =, > 2 is exactly a² <, =, > 4q for the Frobenius form x² + a xy + q y². On the modular surface: D < 0 gives h(D) CM points with the SL₂(ℤ)-invariant label j(τ); D = 0 is the cusp; D > 0 gives h⁺(D) closed geodesics of length 2 log ε_D. Checks: h(D) for 15 discriminants against the class-number formula; j(i) = 1728, j(ρ) = 0, j((1+√−163)/2) = −640320³ to 7·10⁻⁴⁴; integral class polynomials; trace trichotomy 460/460; Deuring’s count of curves over 𝔽_p with trace t, (p − 1)/2 · H(4p − t²), exact for 13 primes; prime geodesic theorem π_Γ/Li = 0.9976 at 10⁶, with periodogram peaks at the Maass eigenvalues. No geodesic length equals log p (ε² = p would make p a unit); ζ’s zeros enter only as scattering poles at s = ρ/2 through the cusp.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Dual conic (adjugate): ellipse ↔ ellipse, hyperbola ↔ hyperbola, line pair ↔ double point
concepts.plain: The family of tangent lines of a conic is itself a conic; for a pair of crossing lines it collapses to the crossing point, counted twice.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The tangent lines of a nondegenerate conic xᵀMx = 0 (3×3) form the dual conic uᵀM⁻¹u = 0 (equivalently adj M). For the affine block xᵀAx = 1: dual yᵀA⁻¹y = 1 (same type). A line pair (rank 2 in P²; J. W. McGreevy's pure wedge) has rank-1 adjugate: the dual is the vertex counted twice (claim 4 correct, for the 3×3 projective matrix). Fixes the 'unique absolute definition' of each stratum up to scale.

concepts.name: Rotating frame: Legendre removes Coriolis from the energy value; it lives in the symplectic form

The Jacobi constant is C_J = 2U − v² = −2E with U = −V_eff. Hill regions depend on U only, so they are blind to the Routh wall.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Unique factorization = the primon Fock decomposition is an isomorphism
concepts.plain: Writing n = ∏ p^{a_p} identifies ℓ²(ℕ) with the tensor product over primes of one-oscillator spaces ℓ²(ℕ₀) exactly when factorization is unique. concepts.name: Gluing connections are flat; a signed curvature must live in the metric

So curvature with a sign has to come from a metric (Petersson, Weil), whose existence over Spec Z is the open part.

Literal for one quadratic; no leverage over ℤ by itself.

concepts.name: Null-line quotient (Gupta-Bleuler form)
concepts.plain: In a non-degenerate space with exactly one negative square, the orthogonal complement of any neutral vector is non-negative and its quotient by that vector is positive definite; a dilation that fixes the neutral line descends to a unitary operator. On finite windows the scale-character representers are negative but tend to neutral, so the quotient is reached only in the limit. On each window the quotient is positive exactly when the arithmetic side has one negative square; there is no version with a margin uniform in the window length, since the margin is squeezed between the smallest eigenvalue of W and the second eigenvalue of Z, both tending to 0. The representer value q(K+-) is about 5 to 40 times lambda_min(W)/kappa^2 (Woodbury), so it tracks the smallest eigenvalue of W.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Polishchuk-Schwarz tilt as the wall limit of a central charge
concepts.plain: On the Hasse lobe the CM point F defines a Bridgeland central charge Z_F(r,d) = -d + F r on the elliptic curve, whose squared length is the norm form and whose Rosati partner under the integer involution iota(r,d) = (-r, d - a r) is complex conjugation. The same involution gives the Galois partner V on the wedge, so the norm is Z_F(v) Z_F(iota v) on both sides. Z_F equals F times the Polishchuk-Schwarz rank at theta = -1/F (Morita image of F). As a approaches the wall, the phases of all line bundles collapse to 0 or 1 according to their slope versus sqrt q, which is exactly the tilted heart; the collapse is like the square root of the distance.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Polishchuk-Schwarz tilt as the wall limit of a central charge. Sources: Polishchuk-Schwarz arXiv math/0211262 (CMP 2003), Prop. 3.9; Bridgeland arXiv math/0212237, Thm 9.1.

concepts.name: A dent moves a zero charge sideways; geometric deformations only rotate
concepts.plain: Zeros are unit charges of log|ξ| (Δ log|ξ| = 2π Σ δ_ρ); a dent moves one sideways at fixed total. The Frobenius angles of one Galois representation are one point of its deformation space (Chebotarev, Brauer–Nesbitt), and deformations through pure representations keep |α_p| fixed, so they rotate the angles and never boost them: no single Euler factor carries a dent. Zero charges, the deformation obstruction and the gluing curvature are three different curvatures.
