concepts.plain: In the circular restricted three-body problem the linearizations at L4 and L5 differ only by the sign of the off-diagonal Hessian entry. Conjugating by diag(1, −1) and transposing shows det(λ² + λ(2J + Γ) − H) = det(λ² + λ(−2J + Γ) − H) for any symmetric damping Γ and symmetric stiffness H, so pure velocity damping −γv keeps the two points exactly isospectral (checked numerically). Breaking the symmetry needs a non-symmetric positional (circulatory) term, which drag relative to a sheared gas flow supplies. The conservative symmetry is the reversing symmetry (x, y, t) → (x, −y, −t).

concepts.name: L4 frequency ratios k:1 occur at quadratic-irrational mass ratios: 27μ(1 − μ) = 4k²/(1 + k²)²
concepts.plain: The two L4 frequencies satisfy ω_s² + ω_l² = 1 and ω_s²ω_l² = (27/4)μ(1 − μ), so ω_s/ω_l = k iff 27μ(1 − μ) = 4k²/(1 + k²)². k = 1 is the Routh value μ_R = (9 − √69)/18, k = 2 and k = 3 are the Deprit–Deprit-Bartholomé exceptional values 0.0242939 (in ℚ(√1833)) and 0.0135160 (in ℚ(√213)). The Kepler (Laplace–Runge–Lenz) 1:1 degeneracy and the Routh 1:1 collision are both rational; what separates them is the Krein sign (same sign, protected by SO(4), against opposite signs, a Hamiltonian–Hopf collision), not rationality.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Three indices that must not be conflated: Fredholm index, negative (Pontryagin) index, conserved charge
concepts.plain: Three different 'indices' must not be conflated: the Fredholm index dim ker − dim coker (a homotopy invariant of an operator); the negative (Pontryagin) index κ = n₋ of a Hermitian form (a congruence invariant by Sylvester's law, which is what the ghost count and the arithmetic Hodge index theorem are about); and a conserved charge (a Noether quantity of a flow). An 'index-zero conservation law' that moves between them is not a theorem. Recorded as a correction in v1.6.1.

concepts.name: Weight-½ Eisenstein series on Γ₀(4): constant term ∝ ζ(4s−1)/ζ(4s), coefficients L(2s, χ_m)/ζ(4s); on the unitary axis (Goldfeld–Hoffstein Re s = ¼) it doubles once, like SL₂
concepts.plain: Goldfeld–Hoffstein (Invent. Math. 80, 1985, Cor. 1.3) give the constant term ∝ ζ(4s+k−2)/ζ(4s+k−1) and the m-th coefficient L(2s+(k−1)/2, χ_m)/ζ(4s+k−1). For weight k/2 (k odd) the Petersson factor is y^{k/4}, so the spectral parameter is S = s + k/4, so the unitary axis is Re S = ½ (Re s = ¼ for k = 1). There the scattering term reads ζ at 4S − 1 = 1 + 4it, the edge, exactly one doubling as for SL₂, while the coefficients are L(½ + 2it, χ_m), on the critical line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Weight-½ Eisenstein series on Γ₀(4): constant term ∝ ζ(4s−1)/ζ(4s), coefficients L(2s, χ_m)/ζ(4s); on the unitary axis (Goldfeld–Hoffstein Re s = ¼) it doubles once, like SL₂. Sources: TAA research notes, 2–3 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: Corrected in v1.14: the research note of 3 Nov first placed the unitary axis at Goldfeld–Hoffstein Re s = ½ and concluded that the weight-½ series “doubles more” than SL₂ (ζ at Re 2 in the constant term, L at Re 1 in the coefficients). The correct axis is Re s = ¼ (S = s + k/4): weight ½ doubles once, and its coefficients sit on the critical line.

concepts.name: Normalizing a Frobenius trace by |a| uses the infinite place of the wrong number: |a| = Π_ℓ |a|_ℓ⁻¹ is untied from p, while √q = |q|_p^{−1/2}
concepts.plain: By the product formula |a|_∞ = Π_ℓ |a|_ℓ⁻¹ depends on the factorization of a_p at primes ℓ ≠ p, while √q = |q|_∞^{1/2} = |q|_p^{−1/2} ties the archimedean norm to the place p itself; only the second is compatible with the functional equation. Under |a| the local factor becomes x² ∓ x + q/a²: the trace is forced to ±1 but the discriminant (a² − 4q)/a² keeps the sign of a² − 4q (420/420 good primes of L(11a) below e⁸; Hasse ⇔ q/a² > 1/4), and the normalization is undefined at the 8 supersingular primes 19, 29, 199, 569, 809, 1289, 1439, 2539. For ζ (degree 1, a_p = 1) the two normalizations coincide.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Normalizing a Frobenius trace by |a| uses the infinite place of the wrong number: |a| = Π_ℓ |a|_ℓ⁻¹ is untied from p, while √q = |q|_p^{−1/2}. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: Moving the scattering axis onto ζ’s critical line makes the scattering phase identically 1, so every zero drops out

concepts.name: Prime term = alpha-derivative of the conjugated Vladimirov symbol
concepts.plain: On unit-invariant functions the conjugated p-adic Vladimirov operator |x|^(a/2) D^a |x|^(a/2) is positive with Mellin symbol |Gamma_p(1/2 + a/2 + i xi)|^2, equal to 1 at a = 0; its a-derivative at 0 is exactly the prime term -2 Re[log p/(p^(1/2+i xi) - 1)] of the explicit formula (archimedean analogue: Re psi(1/4 + i xi/2) - log pi). So the canonical adelic kinetic energy transfers to the potential, not to a positive cushion. Sharp radial p-adic Hardy constant: ((1 - p^((a-1)/2))/(1 - p^(-(a+1)/2)))^2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Prime term = alpha-derivative of the conjugated Vladimirov symbol. Sources: Haran, Invent. Math. 101 (1990); Burnol, arXiv:math/9902080; Vladimirov-Volovich-Zelenov 1994; Tate 1950.

concepts.name: The window Weil operator is not extensive
concepts.plain: The one-particle free energy equals the lowest eigenvalue minus at most T log n, so it grows like -T log l and is never extensive. Second-quantised free fermions are exactly extensive for the zero operator and extensive with a surface term of about 0.26 for the archimedean part alone, but not for genuine zeta, L(Delta) or 11a1 up to l = 10: the density of low eigenvalues per unit length keeps growing, so the Euler relation fails by 30 to 150 percent. Whether a thermodynamic limit exists for genuine zeta is open.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The window Weil operator is not extensive. Sources: Grenander and Szego, Toeplitz Forms (1958).

concepts.name: No time change carries the geodesic lengths 2 log ε_D to the prime lengths k log p (Livšic; multipliers are conjugacy invariants)

The counts agree (78 441 geodesic classes against 78 498 primes below 10⁶, both ~ Li in N = ε²), but the fine structure differs: only 998 distinct lengths below log 10⁶ (one per trace) with multiplicity up to 288. A monotone matching exists asymptotically (ℓ_k / log p_k → 1.00008) but is a relabelling, not a flow.

concepts.name: Sign of a prime step is the sign of the prime-gap excess
concepts.plain: With the main term shared out by prime intervals, the net mass of a prime step is (g_p - log p)/sqrt p up to O(log p/p), so its sign is the sign of the gap excess. Gaps exceed and undershoot log p infinitely often, so no fixed per-prime sign exists; bounding the partial sums is equivalent to RH by von Koch.

concepts.name: A covariance of W would be a weight, not a normalized state; that positivity is not established
concepts.plain: A covariance Gram is positive because a state or a weight is positive. A generic positive Gram need not include a commutator. A nonzero Robertson-Schrodinger commutator needs noncommuting operators. A commutative positive functional can still be independent of the zeros. W is unbounded, so a covariance realization would be a weight on test functions, not a normalized state on bounded translations. That positivity is not established.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Withdrawn: the claim that a commutative functional cannot be an independent sign (the so-called Bochner trap). A positive-definite distribution is the Fourier transform of a positive tempered measure. Stiffness is the quadratic form of a Hamiltonian; covariance is a two-point function; poles are the boundary pair; zeros are spectral data. The local archimedean phase delay is the kernel K, prior. The ratio of completed zeta values Lambda(1/2 - it) / Lambda(1/2 + it) equals 1 by the functional equation, so no group-delay positivity is drawn from it. Real F defines a self-adjoint convolution only when F sharp equals F. On the test core (E0, G0), Q0 and the dilation satisfy [Q0, D] = i. They do not commute. A fixed-window self-adjoint realization still depends on boundary conditions of the domain.
numbers: Audit: Lambda(1/2 - it) / Lambda(1/2 + it) agrees with 1 to 1e-8 at t = 1 and t = 5, as the functional equation requires.
concepts.proved: The functional equation gives the ratio 1. The Bochner-Schwartz correspondence is classical and is not re-proved here; the correction is that it does not forbid an independent functional.
concepts.tests: Must not be used to claim a state whose two-point function is W. No such state is constructed.
pitfalls: RS in this entry is Robertson-Schrödinger, not Rankin-Selberg.
A vacuum spectral density proportional to |Lambda|^2 is not asserted.
A theta functional is not asserted to change sign at the zeros.

concepts.name: CR3BP Hessian, Morse index and Hill pinch, as a dictionary for the Hasse / Σ valve
concepts.plain: In the circular restricted three-body problem the Hessian of the effective potential, the Morse index of the Lagrange points, and the pinching of Hill zero-velocity curves are the classical shape of a chamber and its valve. The best hit is the L1 pinch against a Hasse wall. Jacobi’s constant is an energy cage for a potential one already has. It does not build the arithmetic metric.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Classical twin of the Beurling chamber and of the mix wall Σ, not a constructor. In the circular restricted three-body problem the Hessian of the effective potential U_eff, the Morse index of L1–L5, and the pinching of Hill zero-velocity curves as the Jacobi constant C varies, classify bound against migrating motion. Dictionary, analogies first. L1–L3 indefinite, Morse index 1, against the hyperbolic chamber Δ > 0, exterior fakes, and n₋ = 1 (analogy, about 2.7). L4/L5 definite peaks against the elliptic chamber, with a sign flip in the restricted problem relative to “g ≻ 0 means bound” (analogy, about 2.5). The zero-velocity pinch at L1 against a Hasse wall, |k_1| = 1, or Σ, as a topological valve (analogy, about 2.8; the best classical hit). Periapsis and apoapsis, radial velocity zero inside the cage, against turning points inside formal Q ⪰ 0 (analogy, about 2.6; not occupancy). The primary wall Σ = graph L*(t) against the principal Hill boundary, the first valve. The fold at t ≈ 0.976, L* ≈ 3.6875, against apsidal stationarity along the wall, not a second gateway. The branch switch t ∈ [1.450, 1.458], L* from 4.775 to 6.813, against a change of connected components (ghost recombination), the closest twin of an L1-to-L2 threshold jump; an analogy, not an identity. Secondary sheets of Σ (51 samples, about 1.5–2.5 above L*) against further Hill thresholds (L2/L3), not extra Hasse walls of the pencil. 1 − |k_M|² as a local defining function of Σ (62/62) against the first Hessian eigenvalue, or C − 2U_eff. Jacobi’s constant and the Hill curves are energy cages for an already chosen potential: a restatement of “metric ⇒ chamber”, which is locked. The zeros-blind Kepler object is the Hessian written from masses and the force law before any orbit. That twin orients Open ~1.8 and does not fill it. RH is not proved. Sources: TAA research notes, 5–6 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: Analogy only: a classical or residual twin of the chamber, not a constructor. Over ℚ the zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L is still missing (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved.

concepts.name: Cusp-form vanishing is not the geometric cusp; a residual Spec T collision is a pinch-twin of Σ
concepts.plain: Three uses of “cusp” stay apart. The geometric cusp is a pinched end. A cusp form vanishes there, which is a boundary condition, the twin of the pole annihilator, and not the pinch itself. A congruence f ≡ g mod 𝔭 is a collision of Hecke eigenlines, a residual twin of the wall where the Weil form’s smallest eigenvalue hits zero. On the Beurling pencil the mod-p arithmetic is Waterhouse’s list, which the formal Hessian cannot see.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Three different “cusp” words, kept apart, then compared with the Hessian / Morse / zero-velocity package and with the Kähler package. (1) The geometric cusp of X_0(N), or a Weil–Petersson degeneration, is a puncture where a hyperbolic metric pinches. The Weil–Petersson pair (ω_WP, g_WP) is another Kähler triple; ω_WP is skew and is a name collision with W_L (numerology, about 1.2). (2) Cusp forms S_k(Γ) vanish at those cusps — a boundary condition, the kernel of restriction-to-cusps, already the twin of the pole annihilator ker P. Vanishing is not the geometric cusp, not a Jacobi-field caustic, and not a periapsis. (3) Congruence / mod p: residual collisions in Spec T (f ≡ g mod 𝔭) are a degeneration of a Hecke eigenline, the residual twin of the discriminant wall Σ where λ_min(W_L) = 0 (analogy, about 2.4–2.7). Do not identify an Eisenstein congruence with L1, or an irreducible residual representation with L4/L5, beyond bookkeeping (a softer analogy, about 2.3). On the Beurling pencil the literal mod-p arithmetic is Waterhouse: interior gaps are supersingular traces (p divides t) excluded by congruence conditions on p mod 3, 4, 12 and on the degree n. That is Honda–Tate existence of an isogeny class, not face incidence and not the formal Hessian (n₋ = 0 on all 72 gaps). Classical twin: existence of a central configuration is not the same as “the formal Hessian at a would-be Lagrange point is definite” (analogy, about 2.6). RH is not proved. Sources: TAA research notes, 5–6 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: Analogy only: a classical or residual twin of the chamber, not a constructor. Over ℚ the zeros-blind pair (ω, J) whose compatible g reproduces W_L is still missing (Open ~1.8). RH is not proved.

concepts.name: Kramers–Kronig relations
concepts.plain: Causal response: real (dispersive) and imaginary (absorptive) parts determine each other. Absorption’s sign is the passivity condition.

concepts.name: No-ghost theorem ↔ Gupta–Bleuler quotient of the window form (Analogy)
concepts.plain: In string theory 24 transverse oscillators each contribute ½ζ(−1) = −1/24 to the vacuum energy, giving intercept a = 1; null spurious states decouple and the physical quotient has no negative-norm states (no ghosts), with one tachyon at level 0. On the arithmetic side, Weil’s window form has one negative square (the pole), the pole’s null line is quotiented out (Gupta–Bleuler), and the quotient is positive exactly when RH holds. The dictionary is good at the level of "a null line quotiented out of an index-1 space". It breaks at what forces the critical point: in the string an algebra (Virasoro, central charge 24) forces it; on our side nothing does.

concepts.core: Primes as removed loops: each prime block is k-fold windings of one orbit, but ζ’s Weil form has no p–q cross terms. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: Equivalence-principle gap across a collision: TAA Lemma 157 gap 1 − 2β is 0 before and at the merge and opens ∝ (t* − t)^{1/2} after; RH read as ζ on the EP side, at its edge (at infinity)
concepts.plain: TAA Lemma 157's gap between the two Verschiebungs is zero while a zero sits on the line and opens once a pair splits off. If you call that gap the difference between inertial and gravitational mass, RH says ζ obeys the equivalence principle, but only just.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: [T, TAA Lemma 157] ⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v, v⟩ = 1 − 2β for an eigenvector with eigenvalue β + iγ. Along a dBN collision: 0 before (both real), 0 at the double zero, ±(1 − 2β) after, growing like (t* − t)^{1/2} by the fold law. [N] DH certified gaps 0.617034364913, 0.301660161219, 0.148712100902, 0.448515389254 (TAA Lemma 156/TAA Lemma 157). [A] 'inertial = gravitational' ↔ dual = adjoint. Flags: the EP is postulated in physics (renaming, not mechanism); the gap is computed from zeros (circular unless Θ† comes from an Euler-product metric, MP4 sharp).
pitfalls: Postulated in physics: reading RH as the EP is a restatement (TAA Lemma 160, correction 8).
No Lagrangian with these two masses exists.

concepts.name: Weil positivity is real-time (Bochner, unitary group) positivity, not Euclidean (Osterwalder–Schrader, contraction semigroup) positivity
concepts.plain: Read through the transfer matrix, Γ and the pole are the real-energy part of the kernel’s spectrum and the zeros its imaginary-energy part; RH says the nontrivial spectrum is purely imaginary, i.e. unitary time evolution, which is Bochner positivity rather than OS reflection positivity. As a criterion this is the Hilbert–Pólya restatement.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Weil positivity is real-time (Bochner, unitary group) positivity, not Euclidean (Osterwalder–Schrader, contraction semigroup) positivity. Sources: TAA research notes, 2–3 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: Robertson–Schrödinger, BPS, Hodge index, and no-ghost are related architectures, not one identity
concepts.plain: A positive Gram, a metric square on a Kähler surface, the Hodge index on an algebraic surface over a finite field, and a no-ghost quotient are cousins. They are not the single formula “every mechanism is a square plus an indefinite boundary.” Clifford multiplication exists for an indefinite metric, so it is not a source of positivity. The arithmetic polarization that would match W is not built.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Checked pieces, each in its own setting: Cl(1,1) and a Euclidean Clifford relation both exist; primitive real (1,1) forms on a Kaehler surface are anti-self-dual, which is Riemannian geometry of a complex surface; the finite-field sign is the intersection form, a different theorem; the Hodge index on C x C is what Weil's RH for curves uses; a Bogomolny charge has vanishing Hessian and the norm is the metric square; the level-2 Virasoro norm at h = -1 equals (c - 26)/2, algebra only, and c is a central charge, not a speed and not a topological charge. Goddard-Thorn and Brower transport positivity from an already positive transverse space. Semilocal Sonin is one candidate energy condition, not the unique one. Torsion corrections in a Lichnerowicz formula are convention-dependent. Connes 1999: the global trace formula is equivalent to RH for all Groessencharakter L-functions (over Q, zeta and every Dirichlet L-function). In characteristic p, Delta_Lambda subtracts the projection Q'_{Lambda,0} from S_Lambda; the order makes the difference positive. Subtracting a positive operator does not by itself. The pole plane as an II_1,1 lattice is an analogy. Rank 1, the missing compatible J, is unchanged.
numbers: Audit: Clifford relations for signature (1,1) and for the Euclidean plane; Virasoro norm (c-26)/2 at h = -1; BPS toy Hessian of a constant charge is 0.
Analogy score on the 0-4 research-note scale: 2.4 (structural resemblance, no load-bearing map).
concepts.tests: Must not be quoted as a construction of H_+.
pitfalls: Do not say that only the Hodge pair produces a sign. Positive representations, metrics, and positive states also do.
Do not identify the Kähler anti-self-dual equation with the finite-field Hodge index.
Do not say Spec Z times Spec Z is absent. The sought correspondence geometry, a polarization matching W, is not built. Connes-Consani have a square of sites without that package.

concepts.name: Metaplectic / Kubota cocycle
concepts.plain: A 2-valued cocycle on SL₂ behind half-integer weight; structure without sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §4: Kubota cocycle is a phase (Ax3); Hilbert product formula 300/300, quadratic reciprocity; θ weight ½ is metaplectic (a fourth root, TAA Lemma 141 §7) — mod 2 data, ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 151: θ multiplier eighth roots = Weil index; local covers split over SL₂(ℤ_p), p odd [BIB]; obstruction at 2 and ∞ = half-twist ±1.

concepts.name: Half Tate twist ℚ(½)
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ℚ(1) cyclotomic, H² = ℚ(−1); ℚ(½) not canonical: ℓ-adic F(½) needs a chosen √p (Katz–Rojas-León, opened); g_p² = (−1/p)p gives canonical √(p*) ∈ ℚ(ζ_p); √p for p ≡ 3 mod 4 costs √−1 (disc ℚ(√p) = 4p: ramified at 2; p* < 0: sign at ∞). Over ℝ canonical: Connes's E(f)(g) = |g|^{½} Σ f(qg) and C(1) = (j,λ) ↦ |j|λ. Two product formulas: ∏|x|_v = 1 (size: norm map, scaling flow, √ = critical line) vs ∏(a,b)_v = 1 (phase, obstruction at 2). HEURISTIC nexus: Deninger's cohomology contains an honest ℚ(½), MP4 stated on H¹(½); all twist data ghost-blind.

concepts.name: Functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s)
concepts.plain: ζ’s completed version is symmetric under s ↦ 1 − s. Ghosts satisfy it too, so it cannot prove RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s); DH satisfies FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8 off the line (TAA Lemma 146). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Symmetry is phase data, never sign.

concepts.name: Bost–Connes KMS states
concepts.plain: A quantum statistical system whose partition function is ζ(β); its positive KMS states and phase transition at β = 1 see ζ only at real β > 1, never the zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: BC95 (Thm 5; CM08 3.32): Q-structure, Gal(Q^cycl/Q) symmetry, positive KMS states, ζ(β) real for β > 1; no trace equal to the Weil distribution found (TAA Lemma 30). TAA Lemma 38: strongest rigorous bridge; BC time is dual to rapidity, (β,t) = (Re s, −Im s); BC ordered phase ⇔ ω > ½. TAA Lemma 39: BC = tensor product over primes twisted by Galois. TAA Lemma 54/TAA Lemma 118: KMS/passivity uses ζ at real β > 1 ⇒ ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 162: the precise form of 'local boosts become global rotations' is KMS periodicity in imaginary time (Bisognano–Wichmann/Unruh); p^{−it} is the Bost–Connes time evolution; DH has no primon gas. TAA Lemma 164: B2 negative: KMS/Bochner positivity = non-negative multiplicities; Epstein Z_Q passes and has off-line zeros; BC's arithmetic = multiplicativity (Hecke algebra, Galois), i.e. the Euler product.
numbers: TAA Lemma 159: BC95 Thm 5 re-read (lit/lemma31/bc95.txt): 0 < β < 1 unique KMS (III₁); β > 1 simplex over embeddings of ℚ^cycl (I∞), normalization 1/ζ(β), T_c = 1; §1 KMS strip F(t + iβ) and log Tr e^{−βH} = sup(S − βφ(H))
TAA Lemma 159: φ_β(t) = ζ(β+it)/ζ(β) positive definite (Toeplitz min eig 1.3e−10 at β = 2); DH −7.78
pitfalls: BC95 Thm 5(a) states β < 1 (β ≤ 1 from CM08 3.32) (TAA Lemma 38 flag).

concepts.name: Archimedean place and Γ_ℝ factor
concepts.plain: The "prime at infinity": its Gamma factor contributes a term to the Weil form that can be positive or negative depending on the window.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Γ_ℝ contributes the arch functional to W; arch-only positivity holds on thresholds a* (TAA Lemma 127), ghost-blind.
pitfalls: ∞ is not the frame bundle.

concepts.name: Gauss-sum unitarity |g| = √p (RH for a CM curve as a unitarity identity)
concepts.plain: A quadratic Gauss sum has absolute value exactly √p: this is the statement that the finite Fourier transform is unitary. For the CM curve y² = x³ − x and p ≡ 1 mod 4, the Frobenius eigenvalue is a Gaussian integer π with ππ̄ = p, so RH for this curve is the same kind of unitarity identity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |g|² = p (checked numerically for all odd p ≤ 691) = Plancherel for the finite Fourier transform, the same |x|^{½} twist as TAA Lemma 145. For p ≡ 1 mod 4, π ∈ ℤ[i], ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π, so |α| = √p is automatic. Over ℚ the analogue |ε| = 1 of a root number holds for Davenport–Heilbronn too: necessary, not sufficient. Open: a ζ-analogue in which the eigenvalue itself is a Gauss sum.
concepts.formula: |g|² = p, ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π
pitfalls: Unitarity identities of this kind are Ax3 (phase); over ℚ they are satisfied by DH too and cannot replace the sign.

rels.note: CM case: |π|² = p as a norm identity
Gauss sum = Weil index phase of the reflection (TAA Lemma 151)

concepts.name: Herbrand–Ribet: ω¹⁻ᵏ eigenspace of Cl(ℚ(μ_p)) and p | B_k
concepts.plain: The p-part of the class group of ℚ(μ_p) splits into pieces labelled by powers of the Teichmüller character ω. The piece ω¹⁻ᵏ is nonzero exactly when p divides the Bernoulli number B_k; for p = 691, k = 12 this is the ω⁻¹¹ piece.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: For odd p and even k, 2 ≤ k ≤ p−3: A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) ≠ 0 ⇔ p | B_k (Herbrand 1932 ⇒, Ribet 1976 ⇐). p = 691, k = 12: B₁₂ = −691/2730, class in ω⁻¹¹ = ωᵖ⁻¹² (same character, since ω has order p − 1); odd character ⇒ minus part. TAA Lemma 66: 691 has two irregular indices (12, 200), so Cl/691 is 2-dim (ω⁻¹¹, ω⁻¹⁹⁹); ρ_{Δ,691} ss = 1 ⊕ ω¹¹, the non-split extension gives the ω⁻¹¹ class via CFT (Greenberg–Monsky lattices).
pitfalls: Notation: det ρ_Δ = χ_cyc¹¹ (cyclotomic character), whose reduction mod 691 is ω¹¹; the class itself sits in ω⁻¹¹ (TAA Lemma 66).
Ribet 1976 used weight-2 forms on Γ₁(p), not Δ.
Some authors write ωᵖ⁻¹²; it is the same eigenspace.

rels.note: size statement implied by the main conjecture
sizes, not signs: ghost-blind residual data (TAA Lemma 66)

concepts.name: Mazur–Wiles main conjecture ("Euler characteristic = L-value")
concepts.plain: The size of each Teichmüller piece of the class group (and of the Iwasawa module up the cyclotomic tower) equals the p-part of an L-value; slogan: an algebraic Euler characteristic equals an analytic L-value.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Mazur–Wiles 1984: characteristic ideal of the χ-part of the Iwasawa module = ideal of the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function. Finite-level consequence: #A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) = p-part of L(0, ωᵏ⁻¹) (Ribet, Berkeley slides). TAA Lemma 66: main conjecture = Hilbert–Pólya-type with free p-adic unitarity (γ eigenvalues are 1-units); μ = 0 is not a positivity; no positivity found on the Iwasawa side (OPEN).
pitfalls: Iwasawa theory measures sizes (orders, characteristic ideals), never the sign of D²; it cannot by itself give Weil positivity.
"Euler characteristic = L-value" is a slogan (Heuristic wording), the theorem is the equality of ideals.

concepts.name: E₂ anomaly (E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy))
concepts.plain: E₂ fails to be modular; fixing it costs a non-holomorphic term 3/(πy) tied to the pole. One reading treats the failure as a 2-class.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: E₂(−1/z) = z²E₂(z) + 12z/(2πi)… corrected by E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy), modular of weight 2. Ghost-blind (phase/automorphy data).
concepts.uncertain: Exact transformation constant quoted from standard theory; the 2-class reading is conjectural.

concepts.name: Half turn = sign flip (S² = −I, root number, Hardy Z sign changes)
concepts.plain: Turning by 180° is a sign: it flips modular forms of odd weight, gives the root number, and is the sign change of Hardy’s Z at each zero on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: S² = −I in SL₂(ℤ) acts by (−1)^k on weight k (odd weights vanish; weight ½ needs the metaplectic cover). s ↦ 1 − s is the 180° rotation about ½; its sign is the root number (+1 for ζ, −1 for 37a1, forcing L(E,1) = 0). Hardy Z(t) = e^{iϑ(t)} ζ(½ + it) is real; it changes sign at each on-line zero of odd order. An off-line pair adds 2 to N(T) and no sign change. TAA Lemma 152 NUM (t ∈ [10,120], step 0.01): ζ 38 sign changes / 38 zeros; DH 62 / 66, the two deficits of 2 exactly in [80,90] and [110,120] (off-line pairs 85.699, 114.163). ℝP¹ = directions mod 180°; tautological bundle = Möbius band (the sign).
numbers: DH: 62 sign changes vs N = 66; 5 vs 7 on [80,90] and [110,120]
pitfalls: Ghost-blind at on-line zeros (DH flips like ζ); off-line zeros appear only as missing flips against a global count N(T) (argument principle, Turing-type): detection, not positivity (TAA Lemma 152, correction 8).
TAA Lemma 158: every quadratic form has Q(−x) = Q(x): the half turn persists through the F/V merge; ghost-blind. The signal is the sign pattern (definite → indefinite).

rels.note: s ↦ 1 − s half turn; root number
the wedge is the sign layer, not the missing surface (TAA Lemma 152, correction 8)

concepts.name: Hecke on S³ (Lubotzky–Phillips–Sarnak): for p ≡ 1 mod 4 the p+1 norm-p quaternions act on S³/±1 and on PSL/PGL(2,F_q) Cayley graphs; constant function eigenvalue p+1 (= ζ frame √p + 1/√p after normalizing), all other eigenvalues |λ| ≤ 2√p (Ramanujan via Deligne/Eichler) = elliptic frames; unique factorization ⇒ (p+1)-regular tree
concepts.plain: Multiplying by the p+1 quaternions of norm p is an averaging operator on the 3-sphere. The constant function is its one 'big' eigenvector, which is the ζ-type piece. Every other eigenvalue is at most 2√p, which is the Ramanujan bound and the compact, rotation-type piece.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N] X^{5,13} (2184, PGL bipartite) max nontrivial |λ| 4.2497 ≤ 4.4721; X^{13,17} (2448) 7.0902 ≤ 7.2111; X^{17,13} (1092) 7.8509 ≤ 8.2462; X^{5,17} (4896) 4.3089 ≤ 4.4721. Hecke T_p on SO(3) harmonics ℓ ≤ 15: max |λ| 4.2841 (p = 5), 7.0075 (p = 13). Primitive norm-p^k counts (p+1)p^{k−1} (k ≤ 3). [C] LPS Combinatorica 8 (1988) 261–277; CPAM 39 (1986) S149–S186 (bibliographic + reference list). [T] trivial rep ↔ Eisenstein/ζ (hyperbolic, poles side); cusp part ↔ compact, Ramanujan. DH has no Hecke eigen-system here (c(2)c(3) = −κ² ≠ c(6) = 1).
pitfalls: The 2√p bound uses Deligne (Weil conjectures) — it is input, not output.
The trivial eigenvalue p+1 is ζ's frame; ζ's zeros are not eigenvalues here.

concepts.name: Moser/Souriau: bound Kepler orbits at fixed E < 0 form S²×S² with coordinates j± = (L ± A′)/2, |j₊| = |j₋| = 1/(2√(−2E)); H²(S²×S²) intersection form [[0,1],[1,0]] (signature (1,1): diagonal +2, anti-diagonal −2 — Hodge-index shape); perturbations of a compact orbit average to slow precession of A at fixed |A|, unbound orbits only deflect
concepts.plain: Each bound Kepler orbit of a given energy is labelled by two points, one on each of two spheres, so the space of orbits is a product of two spheres. Its intersection pattern has one positive and one negative direction, the same shape Weil used. A small push to a closed orbit only makes it precess slowly; an open orbit is just deflected once.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] (1e−15, 200 random bound states) L·A′ = 0 ⇒ |j₊| = |j₋|; [C] Moser CPAM 23 (1970) 609–636 (regularization: Kepler flow at E < 0 ↔ geodesic flow on S³; oriented great circles of S³ = S²×S²). Exact Kepler: A conserved at every energy (no precession, no snapping back, TAA Lemma 162 correction to); E = 0 changes only the rescaling A′ = A/√(∓2E): so(4) vs so(3,1). [A] product surface with one positive and one negative direction, cf. Weil's C×C; Euler product ↔ hidden symmetry, DH κ-mix ↔ symmetry-breaking perturbation: precession (zeros move on the line) vs escape (Krein collision). [T] FE rigidity: in span{Λ(χ), Λ(χ̄)} the FE holds only for c = κ (one complex line), so an A4 test family must leave the span. Hydrogen level n = (j,j), j = (n−1)/2, Casimir (n²−1)/4: every n, no prime distinction.
pitfalls: In exact Kepler A does not precess at any energy.
S²×S² ↔ Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ is Analogy.

rels.note: orbit space of the SO(4) picture

concepts.name: Nash–Kuiper flexibility / Onsager threshold
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: No 'Nash–Kuiper transform': Nash 1954 / Kuiper 1955 C¹ isometric embeddings (flat torus in ℝ³, crumpled sphere); rigidity of convex surfaces for C^{1,α}, α > 2/3 (Borisov; Cohn-Vossen, Herglotz, Pogorelov for C²); h-principle α < 1/(1+n+n²) (CDS), 1/5 for 2D disks (DIS); threshold open in [1/5, 2/3] (½ suggested). Onsager 1/3 settled (CET 1994; Isett; BDLSV 2019). Cao–Hirsch–Inauen 1/3⁻ is Monge–Ampère, not isometric. ANALOGY: DH = the Nash–Kuiper surface (FE + phases, no Frobenius/H¹/cup ⇒ zeros unpinned).

concepts.name: Apsides = zeros of the dual-minus-adjoint gap form: for v′ = Xv, X ∈ sl₂(ℝ), r·v = ½⟨(Xᵀ − X^∨)v, v⟩; apsides are the null lines of the squeeze part; circle ⇔ gap ≡ 0 ⇔ dual = Euclidean adjoint (τ = i)
concepts.plain: In a two-dimensional orbit the radial speed is exactly TAA Lemma 157's dual-minus-adjoint gap. It vanishes at the apsides, where position and velocity are perpendicular, and it vanishes everywhere only for a circle, which is the case where the dual and the adjoint agree.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] ω-dual X^∨ = −X (Hamiltonian), Euclidean adjoint Xᵀ; r·v = vᵀXv = ½⟨(Xᵀ − X^∨)v, v⟩ = vᵀ Sym(X) v (TAA Lemma 157 gap form, reference metric). Apsides (r ⊥ v) = null directions of Sym(X) (the 𝔭/squeeze part of the polar decomposition). For the preserved metric g_τ (S_t) X is skew, so the S-adjoint of X equals X^∨: the gap is identically 0 — the apsidal gap measures reference (i) vs preserved (τ) complex structure. Invariant form: e_K = tanh d_H(i, τ), e_H² = 1 − e^{−2d_H(i,τ)} (any SL₂-conjugate; 200 random, 6e−8). [N] 200 random X: 1e−12; orbit t = 1: 4 zeros of r·v per period at the 45°/135° axes. Ghost-blind (archimedean, one frame).
pitfalls: The gap uses the Euclidean (reference) adjoint; for the preserved metric g_τ it is identically zero.
Eccentricity is gauge-dependent: a squeeze conjugation changes e but not F, V (TAA Lemma 161, correction 4).

concepts.name: Cup product / Poincaré duality pairing
concepts.plain: The pairing of cohomology classes; it gives the duality partner of a zero, ghosts included.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Duality partner via cup product (TAA Lemma 93); positivity needs conjugate + Hodge structure (HR).

concepts.name: Cusp forms & Petersson positivity
concepts.plain: Cusp forms have positive Petersson norm — a real positivity, but it does not see ζ’s zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ⟨f,f⟩ = ∫|f|²y^k dμ > 0; HR = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind for ζ (TAA Lemma 146).
pitfalls: Positive but about cusp forms, not ζ’s spectral weights.

concepts.name: Hecke operators
concepts.plain: Averaging operators on modular forms; self-adjointness gives real eigenvalues but not the Ramanujan bound.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hecke self-adjoint ⇒ a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 146). TAA Lemma 160: a_{p^k} = p^{k/2}U_k(t_p/2) — each Hecke eigenvalue is one frame; multiplicativity = product of frames; per-frame ellipticity (Ramanujan) is not known to imply GRH (Open). TAA Lemma 162: LPS Hecke on S³/±1 and PSL/PGL(2,F_q) graphs: trivial p+1 vs |λ| ≤ 2√p (4 graphs, ≤ 4896 vertices; S² harmonics ℓ ≤ 15).
pitfalls: a_p are not BSD generators.

concepts.name: PV ↔ TS: dT∧dS = dP∧dV (Maxwell as one area identity); work = heat = enclosed area; PdV, TdS two primitives of one exact 2-form
concepts.plain: The first law makes the pressure–volume picture and the temperature–entropy picture two maps of the same area form: every cycle encloses the same area in both, which is why work equals heat. Work is an area (a flux), not a cohomology class.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] dU = T dS − P dV ⇒ 0 = d(dU) = dT∧dS − dP∧dV, so ω := dT∧dS = dP∧dV on the (fixed-N, 2-dim) state surface: (P,V) and (T,S) are two Darboux charts of one area form, ∂(T,S)/∂(P,V) = 1, and the four Maxwell relations are this identity in the charts (P,S), (T,V), (P,T), (S,V) (Wikipedia 'Maxwell relations' §Jacobians, opened; Ritchie AJP 36 (1968) 760 not opened). Equal area holds for every region, not only cycles; orientation preserved (engine cycles clockwise in (V,P) and in (S,T)). [N] ideal and vdW (a = 1, b = 0.2) gases: Jacobian 1 ± 2e−9 at 200 random points; ellipse cycle W = ∮PdV = 1.272345 = Q = ∮TdS = π·0.9·0.45; Maxwell (∂T/∂P)_S = (∂V/∂S)_P = 0.8 (ideal), 0.9 (vdW). [T] Cochains vs cohomology: P dV and T dS are not closed; both are primitives of ω (d(PdV) = d(TdS) = ω) and differ by dU (first law). State space is contractible, so H¹ = 0: work over a cycle is the flux of ω through the enclosed region (Stokes), not a cohomology class. The honest cohomology in the arithmetic picture: d log ξ is closed on ℂ∖{zeros} (the Fisher zeros are the holes); periods 2πi·multiplicity [N: ζ box at 14.13 → 1.0; DH box around ρ₁ → 1.0; box around ρ₁ and 1−ρ̄₁ → 2.0]: counts, ghost-blind.
pitfalls: It is one 2-form in two charts, valid where (P,V) and (T,S) are both coordinates (fails on coexistence lines).
Work is not a cohomology class on a contractible state space; first law = [δQ − δW] = 0.

concepts.name: Compact vs non-compact real forms of so(4,ℂ) = sl₂ℂ ⊕ sl₂ℂ: so(4) = su(2)⊕su(2) (Killing (0,6), S³), so(3,1) = sl(2,ℂ)_ℝ ((3,3), H³/Lorentz), so(2,2) = sl(2,ℝ)⊕sl(2,ℝ) ((4,2)); SO(2,2)₀ = (SL₂ℝ×SL₂ℝ)/±1 on AdS₃ = SL₂ℝ by x ↦ g x h⁻¹ is the F/V animation's own G×G, the non-compact twin of SO(4) on S³; rotation = elliptic, boost = hyperbolic (ζ: φ = ½ log p), null rotation = parabolic
concepts.plain: The same complex symmetry has three real versions: all rotations (compact, the 3-sphere), the Lorentz group (rotations plus boosts), and two copies of SL(2,ℝ) acting on anti-de Sitter space, which is the group the F/V animation already uses. Only the all-rotation version has bounded orbits and finite unitary pictures. ζ's prime frames are boosts.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Killing signatures computed: so(4) (0,6), so(3,1) (3,3), so(2,2) (4,2). SL₂ℝ×SL₂ℝ preserves det (signature (2,2)) on M₂(ℝ); diagonal = conjugation preserves tr = (F+V)/√q (2e−12). Lorentz: [K_i,K_j] = −ε J_k (convention), N± = (J ± iK)/2 commute only after complexification; K → iK gives so(4) (Killing (0,6)) — Weyl's unitary trick. Compact ⇔ bounded orbits, unit-circle eigenvalues, every finite-dim/unitary rep unitarizable; SO(3,1): non-trivial irreducible unitary reps infinite-dimensional. e^{iθJ} = cos θ + iJ sin θ needs J² = 1 (fails for spin-1 J_z: 0.235). Pauli: L² + A′² = −1/(2E) (E < 0, A′ = A/√(−2E)), A′² − L² = 1/(2E) (E > 0); L·A = 0; E_n = −1/2n² (1e−13). [A] definite energy = sign of the Casimir = compact real form (Theorem for Kepler; Analogy for ζ). [O] which real form is ζ's G×G. TAA Lemma 163: objective scoring K1–K7: SO(2,2) on AdS₃ unique 7/7 for the frame side ( adopted, scoped); SU(1,1) = SL₂ℝ, SL₂ℂ = so(3,1); sp(4,ℝ) not a form of so(4,ℂ).
pitfalls: N± split is complex; real boosts mix the two factors.
Sign of [K,K] is convention; the relative flip vs [J,J] is what matters.
"Purely imaginary generators" is the Hermitian physics convention.

concepts.name: Connes–Consani 2021: Weil positivity at the archimedean place (support [2^{−1/2}, 2^{1/2}])
concepts.plain: Connes and Consani explain why Weil’s form is positive for test functions too narrow to see the prime 2: it dominates a trace on Sonin space.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Selecta Math. (N.S.) 27 (2021) no. 4, art. 77 (arXiv 2006.13771, opened). Weil's inequality: f smooth positive definite, supp f ⊂ (1/2, 2), f̂(±i/2) = 0 ⇒ W∞(f) ≥ 0 (proved by Yoshida 1992 by explicit computation); ⇔ QW(g) = W∞(g∗g*) ≥ 0 for supp g ⊂ [2^{−1/2}, 2^{1/2}], ĝ(i/2) = 0. Support (1/2,2) chosen so that no rational prime enters. Thm 1: if also ĝ(0) = 0, W∞(g∗g*) ≥ Tr(ϑ(g) S ϑ(g)*), S = projection on Sonin space; Thm 6.11: without ĝ(0) = 0, ≥ Tr(...) − c|ĝ(0)|², 13 < c < 17. Their abstract method alone reaches I = [u⁻¹,u], u = 1.10246 (Cor 8) / 1.15077 (Rem 9); [1/2,2] needs Sonin/prolate and numerics (§6). In log scale: f supported in |u| < log 2 = the first prime atom; TAA Lemma 25's OS-RP fails exactly when the atom log 2 enters. Ghost-blind (archimedean only).

concepts.name: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (Connes–Consani RR)
concepts.plain: The χ in the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch is an Euler characteristic: sections minus obstructions of a divisor D. It is a number attached to D, not a character of a Galois group.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CC23 over 𝕊: χ(D) = dim H⁰(D) − dim H¹(D) = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (TAA Lemma 147). TAA Lemma 145 parity: a linear χ is odd in D and never contains D²; the Hodge-index step needs a quadratic χ (D²/2 term). TAA Lemma 147: χ(D) + χ(−D) = 2 (deg₂D ∉ ℤ). TAA Lemma 160: χ-type vs h-type counts (invariant_vs_refined_count): χ conserved, h^i semicontinuous; for zeros, total count conserved, on-line count changes only at collisions.
pitfalls: Notation clash: this χ is an Euler characteristic, not the character χ (or ω) of the 691 class-group eigenspace.

concepts.name: Ramanujan congruence τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691 (Δ ≡ E₁₂)
concepts.plain: The cusp form Δ agrees with the Eisenstein series E₁₂ modulo 691, because 691 divides the numerator of ζ(−11). It is the meeting point of the Eisenstein (reference) and cusp-form (primitive) parts of the Hecke algebra.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691; ζ(−11) = −B₁₂/12 = 691/32760 (constant term of E₁₂ ∝ ζ(−11)/2 = 691/65520, TAA Lemma 70). TAA Lemma 66: τ(p) ≡ 1 + p¹¹ mod 691 for all 9592 p < 10⁵; Hecke congruence moduli N_k = |num(B_k/2k)| = 691, 3617, 43867, … (k = 12, 16, 18, …); bridge = closed point where Eisenstein and cuspidal components of Spec 𝕋 meet. TAA Lemma 70 (Mazur77 at source): Eisenstein ideal 𝕋/𝔍 ≅ ℤ/n, modulus = numerator of an Euler-depleted ζ(1−k); cusp encodes it as a negative zeta value; positivity invisible (timelike f ≡ spacelike E).
pitfalls: The congruence is mod 691 data: it says nothing about the sign of the Weil form (TAA Lemma 66: bridge = where positivity is lost).
E₁₂ has all its zeros off Re s = 6 (unconditional, TAA Lemma 66) — an "all ghost" Euler product.

rels.note: weight-12 rung: E₁₂ reference vs Δ primitive
Eisenstein = reference, cusp form = primitive split

concepts.name: What each 𝔽₁ approach builds in place of Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ
concepts.plain: Each 𝔽₁ theory either collapses the square back to Spec ℤ (Durov), replaces it by something huge (Borger's Witt space, Connes–Consani's tropical square), or skips it (Deninger). None yet carries a proved sign.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: [C, opened] Manin/Soulé: ask for Spec ℤ ×_{Spec 𝔽₁} Spec ℤ, motivated by C × C in Weil's proof (Soulé 2004 §1.2). Durov: forces Spec ℤ ×_{𝔽₁} Spec ℤ ≅ Spec ℤ, 'unsuitable to pursue Deninger's program' (López Peña–Lorscheid). Borger (Λ-rings): 𝔽₁-structure on flat X = commuting Frobenius lifts ψ_p; 'Spec Z ×_{Spec F1} Spec Z must be defined to be the Witt space W*(Spec Z)'; 'says nothing about the archimedean place'. Haran (abstract only): F-rings with an arithmetical surface Spec O_K × Spec O_K. Connes–Consani: square of the arithmetic site = topos N̂^{×2} with ℤ_min ⊗_B ℤ_min (reduced: Newton polygons), points over ℝ_max⁺ = product of points, Frobenius correspondences Ψ(λ) as congruences (CC16); H¹/RR on the square open (CC19); ℤ ⊗_𝕊 ℤ non-trivial over 𝕊-algebras (Connes essay). Deninger: no square; H¹ with flow. [T,N] Witt link: big Witt W_12(ℤ): F_nV_n = n (ghost), V_nF_n = V_n(1)·, projection formula V_n(x·F_n y) = V_n(x)·y, F₂F₃ = F₆, integrality — the pairing side (sign-free) of TAA Lemma 157's two Verschiebungs (Analogy).
numbers: Witt checks: F_nV_n = n, projection formula, F₂F₃ = F₆, integrality (N = 12)
pitfalls: Witt 'ghost components' are unrelated to TAA ghosts (off-line zeros).
Haran: abstract only, not opened.
Earlier TAA record (lit/lemma30/verified_refs.md) called 'ℤ⊗_{𝔽₁}ℤ = ℤ' for Borger a deduction; Borger's own definition gives W*(Spec ℤ) (TAA Lemma 158, correction 8).

concepts.name: The n! bridge: n! carries every place (Γ/Stirling at ∞; v_p(n!), Morita's Γ_p and Gauss sums at p), tied by the product formula; each place is ghost-blind, so what is missing is a positivity coupling all places at once
concepts.plain: The factorial already contains the archimedean data (the Gamma function) and the p-adic data (how often each prime divides it). Each piece alone cannot tell ζ from a fake; what is missing is something that ties all of them together with a sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [Theorem] Chebyshev: log n! = Σ_{d≤n} Λ(d)⌊n/d⌋ (log = Λ ∗ 1; exact for n = 10, 100, 1000). Legendre: v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p − 1) (100!, p = 2, 3, 5, 7). Stirling/Γ: n! = Γ(n+1), Γ the archimedean factor (error 2.7e−12 at n = 1000). Product formula |n!|_∞ Π_p |n!|_p = 1 (exact for n = 20). F₁ limit |GL_n(F_q)|/(q−1)^n → n! (2, 6, 24); the F₁ reading is a Heuristic (Tits/Soulé, not opened). [Cited] Morita 1975 p-adic Γ_p (values in ℤ_p^×); Gross–Koblitz 1979: Gauss sums = π-power × products of Γ_p values. Link to the SL(2,F_p) half representations: character values (±1 ± √(εp))/2 with √(εp) the quadratic Gauss sum, g_p² = εp; consistency mod p ((p−1)/2)!² ≡ (−1)^{(p+1)/2} for p < 1000. Ghost check: DH shares Γ; its c ∗ a = a·log needs composite c (6, 12, 14, …), so the bridge separates DH only through the support of Λ (the Euler product). Verdict: no new non-archimedean element is needed; what is missing is a positivity coupling all places at once (R8′). The product formula is the only known all-places coupling and is an identity with no sign; provisional definition: a signed product formula on the square (Open).

separates DH only through the support of Λ

concepts.name: Self-dual / anti-self-dual split as push / shear
concepts.plain: In four Euclidean dimensions the Hodge star splits a field strength into self-dual and anti-self-dual parts. The energy is the sum of their squares and the topological density is the difference. On a Kähler surface the self-dual (1,1) part is the Kähler direction (push) and the anti-self-dual part is the primitive part (shear), so push minus shear is the Hodge-index form pointwise. Saturating the instanton (Bogomolny) bound means zero shear, which is stronger than Hodge index.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Self-dual / anti-self-dual split as push / shear Belavin–Polyakov–Schwarz–Tyupkin, Phys. Lett. B 59 (1975) 85–87.
concepts.formula: ⋆²=1 on Λ²(R⁴); F^± = (F±⋆F)/2; |F|² = |F⁺|²+|F⁻|²; F∧F = (|F⁺|²−|F⁻|²) vol; |F|² ≥ |⟨F,⋆F⟩| with equality iff F = ±⋆F; for F = aω+P (P primitive (1,1)): F∧F = (2a²−|P|²) vol
numbers: real (1,1)-forms on C² form R·ω ⊕ Λ⁻ (dim 4); ω self-dual, primitive forms anti-self-dual (error 2e−16)
Lorentzian signature: ⋆² = −1 on 2-forms (exact), so the split is complex there
pitfalls: the real split needs Euclidean signature
½(E²+B²) is T⁰⁰, not a Lorentz invariant; B²−E² and E·B are indefinite (502/498 signs in 1000 samples); what is positive is u ≥ |E×B| (dominant energy)
energy positivity alone carries no information: it holds for every field

concepts.name: Standing frame of the F/V frame geometry: SO(2,2)₀ = (SL₂ℝ×SL₂ℝ)/±1 on AdS₃ = SL₂ℝ (x ↦ g x h⁻¹), compact dual SO(4) on S³ — the unique candidate meeting seven criteria read off the animation (all frame types; trace-preserving conjugation; transitive sweep through t = ±2; real traces only; real form of so(4,ℂ); all Satake frames of ζ and cusp forms; minimal)
concepts.plain: Of seven candidate symmetry groups for the per-prime frame picture, only SO(2,2) acting on SL(2,R) does everything the animation shows; its compact twin is SO(4) on the 3-sphere. That settles the figures' standing frame, not the RH question.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Candidates evaluated: SO(4) fails K1/K6 (no boosts, ζ frames absent); SO(3,1) ≅ PSL₂ℂ fails K2/K3/K4/K7 (complex traces, loxodromics, no real G×G); SL₂ℝ alone and SU(1,1) (= SL₂ℝ by Cayley) fail K3 (conjugation orbits dim 2) and K5; GL₂ℝ² fails K5/K7; Sp(4,ℝ) ≅ Spin(3,2) not a form of so(4,ℂ), contains so(2,2) as a vector stabilizer. Minimality: the anti-diagonal is an irreducible module of the diagonal sl₂. Satake: ζ's frame (p+1)/√p = endpoint of the spherical unitary dual (trivial rep.); tempered ⇔ |t| ≤ 2 (SU(2) classes). DH: no frames (undefined). Scope: frame side only; ζ's zero-side real form is RH-equivalent.
pitfalls: Frame side only: it does not say which real form ζ's hidden symmetry on H¹ has (that is RH).
SU(1,1) and SL(2,ℂ) are not new candidates: Cayley transform; SL₂ℂ = so(3,1).

concepts.name: Tate count / Picard number (ghost-blind)
concepts.plain: Counting algebraic classes on C×C does not see whether eigenvalues are on the circle.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ρ(C×C) = 2 + Σ m(λ)m(q/λ) (Tate 1966, S–S §14.6); = 2g for squarefree, fakes too (TAA Lemma 93 Prop 2.3).

concepts.name: Thermodynamic geometry: Ruppeiner/Weinhold metrics, contact structure (Mrugała), and the compatible J that a 2-dim state surface always has
concepts.plain: Thermodynamic stability gives a positive metric on the space of states, and the first law gives a contact structure. On a two-dimensional state space a compatible complex structure always exists, so the hard part of MP4, a J commuting with a flow, has no thermodynamic counterpart yet.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C] Ruppeiner g_R = −Hess S (positive by stability), Weinhold g_W = Hess U, ds_R² = ds_W²/T; flat for non-interacting systems; Lorentzian signature for negative heat capacity (Reissner–Nordström) (Wikipedia, opened). Mrugała 2000 (opened): thermodynamic phase space = (2n+1)-dim contact manifold, Legendre submanifolds = equilibrium states; contact ↔ first law, metric ↔ second law; his G = dp dx + θ⊗θ has signature (n+1, n) (TAA Lemma 116, correction 1). [T] On a 2-dim oriented state surface with metric g and area form ω = f·vol_g (f > 0), J := rotation by 90° in g satisfies J² = −1, g(J·,J·) = g, ω(·, J·) = f g: the triple always exists, so it carries no content here; MP4's content is commutation with a flow (TAA Lemma 157/TAA Lemma 158), and equilibrium thermodynamics has no flow. [N] ideal gas at (U,V) = (3,2): g_R = diag(1/6, 1/4), ω = 1/3 dU∧dV, J² + 1 = 1e−16, Ruppeiner curvature 0; ω = √(2/3)·vol_W identically (sympy); vdW (1, 0.2): curvature 0.2244 (interaction), J² + 1 = 2e−16. TAA Lemma 116: Euler (multiplicative) field ⇒ flat; χ₄ field curved: curvature measures non-multiplicativity, not zeros. Stability = convexity ⇔ Legendre transform finite/involutive (TAA Lemma 153 window; Fenchel–Moreau); non-convex ⇒ convex hull (Maxwell construction, BIB).
pitfalls: In 2D the compatible J is free; do not count it as a missing piece (TAA Lemma 159, correction 13).
Gibbs, Hermann, Weinhold and Ruppeiner primary papers not opened.

rels.note: positivity free, commutation is the content

concepts.name: The Weil form is the Jacobi integral of the scaling-generator flow D v̇ = Z v
concepts.plain: The pencil Zv = λDv is a linear Hamiltonian system with symplectic form D; vᵀZv and every vᵀZ(D⁻¹Z)^{2k}v are conserved (drift ≤ 6e-15 for ζ, DH, L(11a)). For self-dual L-functions Z has no antisymmetric part: the twist sits entirely in D, as Coriolis sits in ω. There is no position/velocity split, so configuration-space Hill regions are an analogy. RH-blind (holds for DH).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The Weil form is the Jacobi integral of the scaling-generator flow D v̇ = Z v. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.
numbers: research-note score: 3.4 (0.6·significance + 0.4·probability of progress, each on 0–5)

concepts.name: Consani: archimedean cohomology, N at infinity, Γ-factor as a characteristic polynomial
concepts.plain: At the infinite place there is a proved cohomology whose Frobenius has the Gamma factor as characteristic polynomial; it is purely local.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Consani, Compositio 111 (1998) 323–358 (abstract read): a double complex with a monodromy-type operator N at the archimedean fibre, viewed as 'maximally degenerate' (analogue of LMHS); proves Deninger's conjecture that the archimedean Γ-factor is the (regularized) characteristic polynomial of an archimedean Frobenius on the N-invariants of the hypercohomology. Local only: says nothing about zeros (ghost-blind: DH has the Γ-factor of an odd character mod 5).

concepts.name: λ₂ is monotone under nested windows (Cauchy interlacing)
concepts.plain: On a fixed grid, the window spaces are nested: the test functions for a window of length ℓ are among those for any longer window. By Cauchy interlacing every eigenvalue of the arithmetic side Z_ℓ, in particular the second one λ₂, is non-increasing in ℓ. So "λ₂ never reaches 0 as the window passes each log p" is the same as "the infimum of λ₂ over all windows is ≥ 0": the decisive statement is a limit, not a sequence of events at the points log p. The theorem holds for every form, including Davenport–Heilbronn, so it locates where RH is decided rather than deciding it.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: λ₂ is monotone under nested windows (Cauchy interlacing). From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: V_ℓ ⊂ V_ℓ′ (ℓ < ℓ′) ⇒ λ_k(Z_ℓ′) ≤ λ_k(Z_ℓ) for every k; RH ⇔ inf_ℓ λ₂(Z_ℓ) ≥ 0 (by the ghost count; circular as a route)
numbers: ζ, box grid h = 0.02: the largest step-to-step increase of λ₂ on ℓ ∈ [0.3, 6] is −3.6e−6 < 0
h = 0.005: the step in λ₂ across log 7, log 11, log 13 and log 16 is at most 1.6 times the median step (no jump at log p)
base case: λ₂ > 0 for ℓ ∈ (0.2295, log 2] (TAA Lemma 182)
pitfalls: Monotonicity needs nested sections (a fixed grid); on families with a fixed number of boxes the sections are not nested.

concepts.name: The Hodge star squares to the fermion parity in even dimension
concepts.plain: On the exterior algebra of an oriented K-dimensional space ⋆² = (−1)^{k(K−k)} on k-forms, which equals (−1)^k exactly when K is even. For K = 2 this is +1 on degrees 0 and 2 and −1 on degree 1, the pattern of Deninger's real H⁰, H² and quaternionic H¹; the tie to arithmetic is an analogy.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The Hodge star squares to the fermion parity in even dimension. Sources: Deninger, arXiv:2204.02714.

concepts.name: The literal Osterwalder–Schrader form ⟨Θf, f⟩ = W(x+y) is about half negative for ζ, ζ pole-removed, Davenport–Heilbronn and 11a alike
concepts.plain: Reflection positivity in the Osterwalder–Schrader sense fails for the Weil kernel: the pole column is 2cosh(t/2), signature (2,0); the archimedean kernel is −Σ e^{−(2n+½)t} ≤ 0 for t > 0, so the form fails already at the smallest window before any prime enters; each on-line zero pair contributes a (1,1) block. At L = 8.025 roughly half of the eigenvalues are negative for every system tested, so the test does not separate ζ from Davenport–Heilbronn.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The literal Osterwalder–Schrader form ⟨Θf, f⟩ = W(x+y) is about half negative for ζ, ζ pole-removed, Davenport–Heilbronn and 11a alike. Sources: TAA research notes, 2–3 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: Window thermodynamics cannot see where zero is
concepts.plain: Adding a constant to the window operator shifts F, U, G and H by that constant and leaves entropy, pressure, heat capacity, compressibility, the baroclinic measure and the fold locus unchanged, while positivity changes. So no criterion built only from these quantities is equivalent to positivity of the window form.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Window thermodynamics cannot see where zero is.
concepts.formula: W -> W + c: F -> F + c, (S, P, C, kappa_T) unchanged

concepts.name: Mechanical stability of the window is not positivity
concepts.plain: Convexity of U in (S, l) is equivalent to positive isothermal compressibility, and the fold of G over the (T, P) plane is the same locus. Genuine zeta is mechanically stable at all computed lengths for T >= 0.2, but genuine L(Delta) and the elliptic curve 11a1 are unstable on many intervals while positive. A ghost at height 14.13 makes the window unstable only at or after the first negative eigenvalue; an apparent earlier warning at height 79.34 disappears when the window is extended (the ghost goes negative at l = 8.26).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Mechanical stability of the window is not positivity. Sources: Callen, Thermodynamics (1985).

rels.note: the height-79.34 early warning is a finite-window artefact

concepts.name: Max-plus Weil functional is dominated by the diagonal, hence ghost-blind
concepts.plain: For g = +-e^{u/hbar} with a strict maximum, g*g~ dequantizes to the max-plus autocorrelation sup_y[u(y)+u(y-x)], which is <= 2 max u with equality only at x = 0. Prime atoms at |x| >= log 2 are exponentially subdominant, the archimedean term on the O(sqrt hbar) peak is positive, so the hbar -> 0 value is positive for any datum with this functional-equation shape, Davenport-Heilbronn included. Numerically DH's most negative direction turns positive under sign(v)|v|^t at t about 3, 5, 20 (L = 4.5, 6, 8).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Max-plus Weil functional is dominated by the diagonal, hence ghost-blind. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: Non-normal residue ||P - P*|| is a gauge quantity and a collision detector
concepts.plain: The Riesz projection onto an eigenvalue is self-adjoint exactly when its eigenvector is orthogonal to the rest, which is a property of the chosen matrix, not of the spectrum. A normal model diag(zeros) gives ||P - P*|| = 0 even for ghosts; a companion matrix gives large values for real zeros. Under heat flow the residue diverges like |t - t_collision|^{-1/2} at every collision (ghost landing, and zeta's own backward collisions), symmetrically before and after, and then settles to the real-zero baseline; the projection onto the colliding pair stays bounded. So it does not separate ghosts from real zeros without first assuming a self-adjoint model, which is the Hilbert-Polya assumption.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Non-normal residue ||P - P*|| is a gauge quantity and a collision detector.

concepts.name: Primary sign rule for a_p of y² = x³ − x
concepts.plain: For p ≡ 1 mod 4 write p = a² + b² with b even; the sign of a in a_p = 2a is fixed by a 2-adic normalisation (a + b ≡ 1 mod 4). The individual sign is phase data; RH is about the size |a_p| ≤ 2√p, not the sign.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: p = a² + b², b even, a_p = 2a with a + b ≡ 1 mod 4 (π primary mod (1 + i)³); checked for all 14 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 120 (p = 5, 13, 17: a_p = −2, 6, 2). The individual sign is a 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); RH = |a_p| ≤ 2√p is a size statement. The distribution of the signs (Sato–Tate for CM curves) is a separate question; no citation given here. TAA Lemma 150 Prop 3.3: checked on all 147 primes ≡ 1 mod 4 below 2000. Individual sign = 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); the averaged sign is the Sarnak bias 1 − 2r (TAA Lemma 150 §2.1). CM angles: χ² = 0.34 on 10 bins (n = 39,175, p < 1e6), 50.07% positive; Hecke/Deuring equidistribution [BIB, not opened].

concepts.uncertain: Sato–Tate/Hecke–Deuring citation for CM sign distribution not verified; none given.
pitfalls: The minus sign in a₅ = −2 is not the positivity sign of RH: it is a phase (choice of primary generator), and RH bounds the size.

concepts.name: Maass–Selberg relations
concepts.plain: Norm of truncated Eisenstein series expressed via φ and φ′; positivity there is automatic.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §8.1: Maass–Selberg ‖Λ^T E‖² minimum 0.611 (ζ) vs 1.383 (DH) over 540 points ⇒ ghost-blind; it only constrains ζ(w) ≠ 0 for Re w > 1 (already known). TAA Lemma 153 (G): on s = ½+it, ‖Λ^T E‖² = 2 log T − (φ′/φ)(½+it) + (φ̄T^{2it} − φT^{−2it})/(2it) (form as in TAA Lemma 69, checked there to ≤ 1.9e−15 by quadrature against Sarnak's (25)); a line in log T with slope 2 and intercept −φ′/φ(½+it) (J. W. McGreevy's y-intercepts). The intercept is not a positive density: −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1.907 at t = 0.5, −0.135 at t = 2, +0.005 at t = 3 (TAA Lemma 153, correction 23). concepts.name: Gaussian (imaginary-shift, Husimi, heat) filters are ghost-blind
concepts.plain: The Gaussian-windowed (Husimi) values of the window Weil form, the one-dimensional analogue of the paper's time component, stay positive for genuine zeta, for all nine injected ghosts at the first zero and for the Davenport-Heilbronn function, although the exact window form fails for every one of them. They detect only gross prime-sign controls, about one grid step later than the exact form. Detection returns only when the Gaussian is wide enough to be cut by the hard window edge. Heuristically a Gaussian of width s sees a ghost displaced by delta only through exp(s^2 delta^2), while a compactly supported window of length l sees it through exp(delta l): compact support (exponential type) is the positivity probe, and the smoothing discards it. Gaussian smoothing is a forward heat flow, which only propagates positivity to coarser scales.

concepts.name: E0 is dense in L² and not closed; on one window the kernel is closed of codimension 2
concepts.plain: Tate's b(f) = (f(0), integral f) and the log-line moments ev_0(F), ev_1(F) are different. Smearing links them. On the log line the two exponential moments are unbounded on L², so E0 is dense and smooth functions in E0 are not closed. On one finite log-line window both exponentials are square-integrable, so the kernel is closed of codimension 2. There is no global orthogonal projection that removes those moments.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: E0 = {ev_0 = ev_1 = 0} on the log line is a convolution ideal and is stable under the sharp involution. It is not the kernel of Tate's b. Smearing satisfies b(Theta_F f) = diag(ev_0 F, ev_1 F) b(f), so Theta_F maps the entire Schwartz-Bruhat space into ker b if and only if F is in E0. Equivalently, b(Theta_F f) = 0 for every f if and only if ev_0 = ev_1 = 0. The operator L = d^2/du^2 - 1/4 bijects compactly supported smooth functions onto E0 in that class and preserves support hulls; positivity transports across it. That bijection is Connes-Consani 2021, Lemma 3.3, and the transport is their Proposition 3.5, prior. On the test core (E0, G0), Q0 = L Q L^(-1) and the dilation satisfy [Q0, D] = i. They do not commute. A fixed window still needs boundary conditions before the operator is self-adjoint. A real convolution by F is self-adjoint only when F sharp equals F.

On windows of half-width L = 2, 4, 8 the distance from a fixed test function to the closed kernel is about 0.820, 0.346, 0.050.
concepts.proved: Unboundedness of point evaluation and of integration against a non-square-integrable exponential. The bijection across L is cited, not re-proved.
pitfalls: Do not call E0 a closed codimension-2 subspace of L².
L in the boundary logs is a half-width. A in the spring logs is a full width.
Translations are abelian. A noncommutative enlargement is for a Robertson-Schrödinger commutator, not a requirement for an independent positive functional.

concepts.name: After the counterterm, the net prime contribution has the sign of the autocorrelation
concepts.plain: Grouped as a Rayleigh quotient, the archimedean density contributes through a nonnegative weight 2 - 2 rho, while each prime leaves -2 a_n rho(log n). That signed term is what remains after the counterterm has taken the diagonal. It is not the prime spring energy, which stays nonnegative.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: W(F)/||F||^2 = K(0) + integral k_infinity(a) (2 - 2 rho(F, a)) da - 2 sum a_n rho(F, log n), rho(b) = <F, T_b F> / ||F||^2. The weight 2 - 2 rho is nonnegative for a real isometry. The coefficient of a_n is minus twice the autocorrelation, so a prime helps or hurts that mode according to the sign of rho. The bottom of the spectrum is concave in the weights (K(0), k_infinity, a_n), so the nonnegative set is convex. Elementary reorganization of the same quadratic form, not a new inequality.

concepts.name: Window Weil form as nonnegative spring energy minus a counterterm
concepts.plain: For real F extended by zero outside a window of full width A, and for N at least e^A, the Weil form is the pole term plus a finite spring energy E_N minus M_N times the norm squared. M_N = -K(0) + 2 sum_{n<=N} a_n. The sum over all n diverges. Couplings past the window cancel. On E0 the pole term is zero, and positivity is whether E_N dominates M_N. The identity restates W; it does not prove the inequality.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: For real F extended by zero outside a window of full width A, and N at least e^A: W(F) = P(F) + integral k_infinity(a) ||F - T_a F||^2 da + sum_{n<=N} a_n ||F - T_log n F||^2 - M_N ||F||^2, with a_n = Lambda(n) n^(-1/2), k_infinity(a) = e^(-a/2)/(1-e^(-2a)), and M_N = -K(0) + 2 sum_{n<=N} a_n, K(0) = Re psi(1/4) - log pi. Without the cutoff the prime sum diverges. Terms past the window cancel. Each piece of E_N is nonnegative. The archimedean Levy representation is prior. An explicit functional with a quartic potential of coupling lambda >= 0 has Hessian at 0 equal to W. Away from 0 the Hessian is W plus a nonnegative term coming from that quartic potential. The Hessian stays quadratic in the variation. A Hessian identity restates W and does not sign it.
concepts.formula: W = P + E_N - M_N ||F||^2, N >= e^A, F = 0 outside the window; on E0, P = 0

concepts.name: Finite bordered inertia: index 0, or index 1 with q at most 0
concepts.plain: For a finite invertible symmetric matrix B and one nonzero constraint c, positivity on the hyperplane c perpendicular holds in exactly two cases. Either B is already positive semidefinite, or B has exactly one negative direction and the scalar q = c^T B inverse c is less than or equal to zero. Two or more negative directions cannot be removed by one constraint. This is linear algebra. It is not yet a theorem about the infinite-dimensional bulk form.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Let B be real symmetric and invertible, c nonzero, q = c^T B inverse c. The negative index of B on the kernel of c is n-(B) - 1 + 1 when q > 0, and n-(B) - 1 when q <= 0. The nullity of the restriction is 1 when q = 0 and 0 otherwise. The restriction is therefore positive semidefinite if and only if n-(B) = 0, in which case q is necessarily positive, or n-(B) = 1 and q <= 0. If n-(B) >= 2 the restriction still has a negative direction. The parent audit gives the congruence proof. Infinite-dimensional use needs B invertible on a stated domain and c in the domain of B inverse. Those hypotheses are not verified for the window operator. The vector B inverse c is defined from B. It is not an independent constructor.

concepts.name: Under trace-class assumptions the cutoff splits into two Hankel pieces minus a remainder
concepts.plain: Once the semilocal traces are assumed to exist, W minus P splits as a difference of two cutoff operators minus a remainder X. A positive compression of a cutoff was compared with W on a few tests and did not match. That mismatch is numerical. It is not a theorem that every compression fails.

The positive compression Q = S P-hat S was larger than or equal to W on three tests at A = 1, and at A = 0.6 the compression still depended on the set S while W did not. Those comparisons are double precision and uncertified. They close the tested compressions. They are not a universal no-go.

concepts.name: Regularity of a local ring is not a global principal generator, and not a sign
concepts.plain: A power-series ring over the p-adic integers is regular of dimension 2. Quotienting by one equation leaves a regular ring exactly when that equation is nonzero in m/m squared. That is a Jacobian condition. The Iwasawa numbers mu, lambda, and nu measure growth. They are not this Jacobian class, and they do not carry a sign. A regular local ring is a unique factorization domain. A global ring of integers need not be. Noetherian is a finiteness condition on ideals, not a Noether charge in mechanics.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Lambda = Z_p[[T]] is regular local of dimension 2. Lambda/(f) is regular if and only if f is not in m squared. The element T squared - 27 is a singular example, an arithmetic cusp in that local model. Auslander-Buchsbaum says a regular local ring is a UFD. Z[sqrt(-5)] is Noetherian and not a UFD: 6 = 2·3 = (1+sqrt(-5))(1-sqrt(-5)), and 2 and 1+sqrt(-5) are irreducible because no element has norm 2. This does not reopen a global Jacobian, a Rosati involution, or a Picard lattice. Those routes stay at whatever status the atlas already gave them. The toy separates a growth invariant from a rank in m/m squared. It supplies no positivity.
concepts.formula: regular local <=> f not in m^2; regular local => UFD; not conversely for global rings
numbers: Norm form a^2 + 5 b^2 never equals 2. Class number 2 for Q(sqrt(-5)) is the classical citation, not recomputed here.
concepts.proved: The norm obstruction in Z[sqrt(-5)] is rechecked by the audit. Auslander-Buchsbaum and the Iwasawa growth formula are cited.
pitfalls: Do not translate Noetherian into a Noether charge.
Do not promote a local UFD to a global principal generator.
Closed Jacobian, Rosati, and Picard paths are not reopened.

rels.note: mu, lambda, nu are growth; the Jacobian condition is a class in m/m^2; neither signs W

concepts.name: A skew pairing on H1 becomes symmetric on the product, with both signs
concepts.plain: On a curve the intersection of 1-forms is alternating. On the product of the curve with itself, the Kunneth rule turns that into a symmetric form, minus the product of the two pairings. For an elliptic curve of area 1 the mixed real primitive class of type (1,1) squares to -8. The real class in types (2,0) and (0,2) squares to +8. One sign pattern, two signs. Not every class is negative.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: E(u, v) = integral u wedge v. Holomorphic and antiholomorphic forms are isotropic, and i times the integral of alpha wedge its conjugate is positive on H^{1,0}. The product pairing is I(a tensor b, c tensor d) = -E(a, c) E(b, d). With E(dz, d z-bar) = -2i, the mixed vector dz tensor d z-bar plus d z-bar tensor dz has square -8. The vector dz tensor dz plus d z-bar tensor d z-bar has square +8. The mixed sector is not the whole primitive H^{1,1}. This is hand algebra for one normalization. It is not a map from E0.
concepts.formula: I = -E ⊗ E; mixed real primitive square -8; (2,0)+(0,2) square +8
numbers: Area-1 normalization. Exact, rechecked symbolically in the v1.20 audit.
concepts.proved: Bilinear expansion of the Kunneth rule on the two real vectors. Finite dimensional. Not a theorem about W.
pitfalls: Do not say that all of H^{1,0} tensor H^{0,1} is negative.
Do not identify this calculation with a polarization for zeta.

rels.note: a finite sign pattern with both a negative and a positive direction
the mixed vector is not the whole primitive lattice

concepts.name: Each local term is a product-state covariance, and that covariance is subtracted
concepts.plain: Every local piece of the ledger has a product-state reading. A prime contributes log p times the norm squared minus a positive AR(1) covariance. The archimedean place is an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck tower. The positive covariances enter with a minus sign. They account for the terms. They do not make B positive.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: W_p(F) = log p ( ||F||^2 - <F, P_p F> ), where P_p = sum_k p^(-|k|/2) T_{k log p} is positive semidefinite, the covariance of a critical boson, or an AR(1) process. The archimedean symbol is the OU tower with rates (2j+1)/2. E0 is the statement that the rate-1/2 OU response is supported in the window. The individual prime responses leak: their local poles cancel only when all places are kept together. This is an exact term-by-term reading. As a source of the sign it is closed. Observation, not a theorem: the OU rate (2j+1)/2 is the distance from 1/2 to the pole s = -2j of the archimedean Gamma factor. For j at least 1 those poles are cancelled in xi by the trivial zeros. The j = 0 pole at s = 0 survives in Lambda and is the moment removed by E0.
concepts.formula: W_p = log p (||F||^2 - <F, P_p F>), P_p positive semidefinite
numbers: Session, A = 2, G = sin^8, uncertified: arch +0.090, p = 2 about +9.092, p = 3 about -9.001, p = 5 about -0.0016, spring total 0.1788.
Rounded displayed parts sum to 0.1794. The cancellation is the point of the figure, not a certificate.
concepts.proved: The prime identity is completion of the square against a positive Toeplitz covariance. Positivity of a finite section is linear algebra and is rechecked for a short AR(1) block in the v1.20 audit.
concepts.tests: Must not be quoted as a sign mechanism. The covariance is subtracted.
pitfalls: Closed as a sign source, on this reading: a subtracted positive form does not dominate the diagonal by itself.
Not a universal theorem that no positive compression can ever match W. The tested compressions mismatched W. That is a smaller statement.

concepts.name: The pole term is 2 ev+ ev-, equally 2(C squared minus S squared)
concepts.plain: The pole contribution is the product of the two exponential moments. In real even and odd coordinates it is 2(C squared minus S squared). In complex coordinates it is twice the real part of C+ times the conjugate of C-. It is the term that E0 is built to kill.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ev±(F) = integral F(u) exp(±u/2) du. P(F) = 2 ev+ ev- = 2(C^2 - S^2) = 2 Re(C+ conjugate C-). On a centered window, reflection splits this into a rank-one positive update on the even sector and a rank-one negative update on the odd sector: W_even = B_even + 2 c c^T and W_odd = B_odd - 2 s s^T. Globally the moment functionals are unbounded, so E0 is dense in L2. On one finite window both exponentials are square-integrable, so the kernel is closed of codimension 2. That topological distinction is already in v1.19.
concepts.formula: P = 2 ev+ ev- = 2(C^2 - S^2) = 2 Re(C+ conj C-)
concepts.proved: Definition of the pole term in the explicit formula, rewritten in even-odd and complex coordinates.
pitfalls: The even formula alone is not E0. The odd sector has its own constraint.

rels.note: same pole term, written as a product of moments

concepts.name: At width 1 the second candidate fails by a prime-2 kink of slope 0.06191
concepts.plain: The Dirichlet candidate is smooth inside the window, so the archimedean part of its response is smooth there. The shift by log 2 brings a kink of the window edge into the interior. The slope jumps by a_2 sinh(A/4)/2. A combination of cosh and sinh has no jump, so the candidate is not a representer. The same sentence for every representer, at every width, is a conjecture.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hypotheses: A = 1, so log 2 < A < log 3 and the only prime power in the sum is n = 2. h2 is Lipschitz, with kinks at the two window edges, hence in the form domain. On the open window the archimedean integrals are analytic in the edge distances, and h2 itself is analytic. The translate by log 2 is supported up to A/2 - log 2 and contributes a slope jump a_2 sinh(A/4)/2 = 0.06191, with a_2 = log(2)/sqrt(2). The opposite edge gives the symmetric jump. No other shift enters. The annihilator lemma then excludes span{cosh, sinh}. For a general width, several shifts can land on the same point and cancel. No claim is made. The guess that every representer carries a finite singular orbit, or that the edge profile is a universal 1/log law, needs a propagation argument that is not given.
concepts.formula: jump = a_2 sinh(A/4)/2 = 0.06191 at A = 1, n = 2 only
numbers: Finite difference at spacing 10^(-4): 0.06189. At spacing 10^(-3): 0.06172. Prediction 0.06190632.
concepts.uncertain: A finite edge-orbit ansatz, a universal 1/log law, and a Gamma-only no-go are conjectures.
concepts.proved: The jump computation and the annihilator step, under the hypotheses above. The audit script recomputes the exact jump and one finite difference.
pitfalls: Exact only for this width, where a single prime power enters.
The numerical residual of h2 at A = 0.6 is not this exact jump.

concepts.name: The counterterm adds local mean statistics; it is not a global idele coupling
concepts.plain: M_A is a sum of separate local means, one place at a time. There is no coupling on principal ideles in this identity, so it is not a proved product-formula defect. If the prime sum runs over all prime powers inside the cutoff, the capped mean is a sum over those primes, not a one-prime expression.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Each place contributes its own truncated expectation of log |x|_v. The archimedean mean is K0 = psi(1/4) - log pi. For the primes, a_n = Lambda(n) n^(-1/2) already sums prime powers. Written as a Gibbs capped mean over every prime power with k log p < A, the diagonal is 2 times the sum over p < exp(A) of the local mean of log p times min(N_p, K_p(A)). A formula that shows only one p on the right-hand side does not match a sum over all such prime powers. The classical product formula, product over places of |x|_v = 1, is a different statement. It is not a coupling that has been constructed on principal ideles, and it is not the source of the sign.
concepts.formula: M_A = -K0 + 2 sum_{log n < A} a_n = -2 sum_v (local mean_v); prime part sums over p
numbers: At A = 2 the session records M_A = 11.22465. At A = 1, M_A = 6.35244. At A = 0.6, with no prime inside, M_A = -K0 = 5.37218.
concepts.proved: The second expression is the definition of M_A used throughout the ledger. The expectation form is the audited reading of that constant.
pitfalls: Do not call this a proved product-formula defect.
No global idele coupling is claimed.
A single-prime right-hand side is the wrong way to write the sum over all prime powers.

M_A is the counterterm in B

concepts.name: Rankin-Selberg unfolding produces square coefficients, not the Weil form
concepts.plain: The integral of y to the 12, times |Delta| squared, times an Eisenstein series, unfolds to a Gamma factor times the Dirichlet series of tau(n) squared. The coefficients are squares because the interior pairing is positive and the unfolding is honest. Self-adjointness of Hecke operators makes tau(p) real. None of this is an identity for W. The Petersson norm of Delta is a finite positive number. Decay of the cusp integrand is why that integral converges. It is not a degeneration of the pairing.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Rankin (1939) and Selberg (1940): the integral of y^12 |Delta|^2 E(z, s) d mu equals Gamma(s+11) (4 pi)^(-(s+11)) times sum tau(n)^2 n^(-(s+11)). The atlas already records a positive Petersson norm, about 1.035·10^(-6). Congruences such as the one at 691 are arithmetic. They are not real positivity of W. A positive-definite lattice extracted from a Rankin-Selberg explicit formula is a different theorem and is not a formula for the Weil form on log-window tests.
concepts.formula: integral y^12 |Delta|^2 E(z,s) = Gamma(s+11) (4 pi)^(-(s+11)) sum tau(n)^2 n^(-(s+11))
numbers: <Delta, Delta> about 1.03536205680432e-6, already in the atlas, finite and positive.
concepts.proved: Cited unfolding. Not reproved here. The negative statement is that the identity does not mention W.
concepts.tests: Must not be used as a bridge from square coefficients to Weil positivity.
pitfalls: Square coefficients are not W.
Cusp decay is convergence of the integral, not degeneration of the norm.
The weight-12 calibration is not the archimedean counterterm.

rels.note: positive interior pairing, square coefficients, no information about zeta zeros
a finite positive norm of Delta; cusp decay is not a degeneration
