concepts.name: Semilocal trace: the bulk symbol is a scattering time delay, not a Hodge theorem
concepts.plain: With finitely many places, enough to cover the window, the Connes trace identity says that a twisted pairing equals W minus P. The phase of that cutoff turns into the symbol of the bulk form by a logarithmic derivative. That is a scattering dictionary. It is not a sign theorem and it is not Hodge positivity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Connes 1999, Theorem VII.4, is the semilocal trace formula. The dictionary used here: for S containing the archimedean place and every prime p < exp(A), -I_S(F, F) = W(F) - P(F) on window tests. The semilocal Fourier transform factors as M_c times J, with a phase c_S, and -i d/dy log c_S = -m_S, so the symbol of W is the negative of that Wigner time delay. The identity is semilocal. A global Gamma-Euler product with phase identically 1 is not claimed. The trace is not the Hodge index.
concepts.formula: -I_S(F,F) = W(F) - P(F) for S covering the window; -i d/dy log c_S = -m_S
concepts.uncertain: Convergence of the limiting traces is an assumption, flagged for any signed-leakage reading. X in the Hankel decomposition is numerical where a number is quoted.
concepts.proved: The trace formula is cited, not reproved. The phase-to-symbol step is the audited dictionary, exact inside that semilocal normalization.
concepts.tests: Must not be quoted as RH, and must not be quoted as a Hodge-index theorem.
pitfalls: Semilocal only. Finite S containing infinity and every p < exp(A).
Not Hodge positivity.

rels.note: the bulk symbol is the negative Wigner delay of the semilocal phase
a trace identity is not the Hodge index
the pairing in I_S uses the twisted star

concepts.name: The semilocal pairing uses a twisted involution, not the naive star of chi f
aliases: (chi f) star = chi inverse f star
concepts.plain: The weight chi(u) = exp(-u/2) has to sit inside the convolution in a definite way. The corrected involution satisfies (chi f) star = chi inverse times f star. Pairing two functions by the ordinary star of (chi f) with itself is a different, wrong, formula. No global phase c = 1 is claimed.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: With f star (u) = conjugate f(-u) and chi(u) = exp(-u/2), the identity (chi f) star = chi^(-1) f star is a one-line calculation, rechecked in the v1.20 audit. The semilocal distribution is h = chi times (f convolved with f star). Equivalently h = g convolved with g sharp, where g = chi f and g sharp (u) = exp(-u) conjugate g(-u). That sharp is not the ordinary star of g. The numbers computed in the session used the corrected h. A formal graph of a flow, built from the bulk pairing, is not a cycle class, not a numerical group, and not a Hodge structure.
concepts.formula: (chi f)* = chi^(-1) f*, chi(u) = exp(-u/2); h = chi · (f * f*)
concepts.proved: The involution identity is elementary and is rechecked by the audit script. The semilocal normalization is the correction recorded against the earlier scratch formula.
pitfalls: Do not replace the twisted sharp by (chi f) star (chi f) star.
Do not claim a global Euler phase c = 1. That statement is formal only.
A formal graph integral is not a cycle.

rels.note: semilocal pairing is tau of chi times (f1 convolved with f2 star), not the naive star

concepts.name: Exact window ledger: the Weil form is the pole term plus a bulk form
concepts.plain: On a log window the Weil form splits as a pole term P plus a bulk form B. The bulk form is nonnegative spring energy minus a diagonal counterterm. Killing the poles removes P and leaves the counterterm in place. The split is an identity. It does not sign W.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: For a window test F, W(F) = P(F) + B(F). P = 2 ev+ ev- = 2(C^2 - S^2) = 2 Re(C+ conjugate C-). B = H_A - M_A times the norm squared, and the same B is (1/2 pi) times the integral of m_A |Fourier F|^2. H_A adds the archimedean Levy springs and the prime springs for log n < A; each spring is nonnegative. M_A = -K0 + 2 sum Lambda(n) n^(-1/2), with K0 = psi(1/4) - log pi = -5.37218. The formula for B is valid off E0 as well as on it. W equals B on the joint kernel of the two moment functionals, which contains E0. This restates the v1.19 spring identity with the pole term kept visible off E0.
concepts.formula: W = P + B, B = H_A - M_A ||F||^2, E0 kills P only
numbers: K0 = psi(1/4) - log pi = -5.3721834192256654, from the session ledger.
concepts.proved: Algebraic completion of the square for real translations, on the prior archimedean Levy kernel. Checked again in notes/v120/tests/audit_v120.py for K0 and for P vanishing on E0.
concepts.tests: A sign for B on every window test in E0 would be Weil positivity. The identity does not supply it.
pitfalls: Do not write W = B off E0. Full W is B + P.
Do not say that E0 removes the counterterm. E0 kills P. The diagonal M_A ||F||^2 remains inside B.

concepts.name: Criticality: genuine L-functions are gapless in three directions, so any proof of positivity must be margin-free
concepts.plain: (L) Under RH the spectral measure of the Weil Toeplitz form is pure point (the zeros), Szegő’s condition fails and Π(1 − k²) → 0 [Theorem, conditional on RH]. (t) Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao): ζ cannot be pushed strictly inside along the heat flow [Cited]. (Ω) The archimedean factor is minimal admissible [Conjecture]. Measured slopes of log Π(1 − k²) per unit L: −0.43 for ζ, −0.67 for L(11a); Davenport–Heilbronn breaks (|k| ≥ 1) at L = 3.825. No uniform spectral gap or compactness margin exists, so a proof must be identity-type (a sum of squares or a polarization), as Hasse is over 𝔽_q [Heuristic]. Criticality does not separate ζ from L(11a); it separates genuine L-functions from Davenport–Heilbronn.

concepts.name: Sharpened gap: a positivity linear in the coefficients c_m(S) off the unitary axis (the u = 2S − ½ direction); positivity in the discriminant variable exists but only averages
concepts.plain: The 45° bypass reads the weight-½ coefficient c₁ along u = 2S − ½, where c₁ ∝ ζ(u)/ζ(2u) has ζ on its own line. Maass–Selberg gives positivity only on Re S = ½, where zeros enter as zeros of c₁ and quadratically; an off-line zero lives at Re S ≠ ½, where no norm exists. Positivity in the discriminant direction does exist (Rankin–Selberg Σ_m |L(½ + 2it, χ_m)|² |m|^{−w} has nonnegative coefficients), but it controls averages over m, not zeros of a single L. Missing: a family of positive linear conditions in c_m(S), as Weil’s criterion is a family of linear conditions, one per test function. Open.

concepts.name: Conjecture-level target: a Hopf-type fibration of Spec ℤ (a global Kustaanheimo–Stiefel map) as a Deninger triple with a compact circle/Bohr-torus flow
concepts.plain: The KS map that turns Kepler into an oscillator is the Hopf fibration of S³. In the knots–primes dictionary, its arithmetic analogue would be a three-dimensional foliated system with a compact flow whose closed orbits are the primes; RH would say the net form is a sum of squares in that coordinate. A literal circle action is impossible because the periods log p are incommensurable; the compact object would be the Bohr torus. RH is not proved.

concepts.name: Half-density normalization |x|^{½}
aliases: critical line = spectrum of unitary scaling
concepts.plain: Multiplying by |x|^{½} makes scaling unitary on L²; this is why the critical line is at ½.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 145 Thm twist: |x|^½ = (dx/d*x)^½ is unitary L²(dx) → L²(d*x); U_λ unitary with generator −(x∂_x + ½); Mellin is unitary only on Re s = ½ (Plancherel 0.35355339 both sides; at Re 0.4 a weighted norm 0.53173). Cusp gauge y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4). TAA Lemma 153 (E): (U_λ f)(x) = λ^{½}f(λx) on L²(ℝ₊,dx): U_λ x^{−s} = λ^{½−s} x^{−s} (NUM ≤ 2.2e−16), |λ^{½−s}| = 1 for all λ iff Re s = ½ (x^{−s} is a generalized eigenfunction, not in L²). Critical line = unitary spectrum of scaling; this is unitarity (Ax3), not positivity. TAA Lemma 159: β = ½ (the critical line) is inverse temperature ½, i.e. half-density weights n^{−½}, inside the Hagedorn-divergent region (Analogy for the identification).
pitfalls: There are two ½’s (TAA Lemma 145 corrections): the unitary twist and the critical line.

concepts.name: Theta inversion θ(1/t) = √t θ(t)
concepts.plain: Poisson summation gives the functional equation; phase data.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(1/x) = √x θ(x) gives Riemann’s FE and the boundary terms f(0), f̂(0) of 1/(s(s−1)) (TAA Lemma 36 §6). TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion for x² + 5y² to 3e−30; Weil representation unitary, (ST)³ = Gauss sum · I; unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 145: θ FE error 6.3e−26; TAA Lemma 146: θ S-error ≤ 2.5e−16, Fresnel = half-density × Weil index. TAA Lemma 151 centrepiece: θ(1/t) = √t θ(t) and ϑ(−1/τ) = √(τ/i) ϑ(τ) to ≤1.5e−51; √(1/i) = (1 − i)/√2 primitive 8th root (√2 in the phase); t^{¼}θ(t) inversion-invariant; unitary inversion on L²(ℝ₊,dx) is x^{−1}f(1/x) (TAA Lemma 151, correction 6). TAA Lemma 153: √(1/i) = e^{−iπ/4} is the Maslov factor of a negative-definite Hessian (stationary phase).

concepts.name: The prime 2 as the wild place
concepts.plain: The only even prime is 2 (not √2). At 2 the Gauss halves break: (p − 1)/2 is not an integer, every model y² = f(x) has bad reduction, and the Hilbert symbol / metaplectic cocycle is wild. √2 enters through (2/p), which depends on p mod 8.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Supplementary law: (2/p) = +1 ⇔ p ≡ ±1 mod 8; √2 ∈ ℚ(ζ₈), so (2/p) is the character χ₈ (the √2 family). At p = 2, (p − 1)/2 is not an integer and every Weierstrass model y² = f(x) is bad at 2; the Hilbert symbol and the metaplectic (Kubota) cocycle are wild at 2. All of this is phase data, hence ghost-blind.
pitfalls: The even prime is 2, not √2; √2 appears only through the character (2/p) = χ₈(p).
√2 is not a prime (TAA Lemma 150, correction 1); √2 enters via χ₈ and, separately, via Goldfeld's √2 (prime squares).

concepts.name: The F/V sweep as an orbit sequence: invariant conics S_t = [[1,−t/2],[−t/2,1]] of g_t keep their apsidal axes at 45°/135° for all t; e_H² = 2t/(t+2); after Bohlin z², Kepler e_K = t/2 = (F+V)/2√q, F/√q = e_K + i b/a; circle → ellipse → parabola (t = 2, F = V, escape) → hyperbola; binding margin 1 − t/2 = 1 − e_K
concepts.plain: As t grows from 0 to 2 the invariant ellipse of the frame stretches along a fixed 45° line, like a planet given ever-larger kicks at periapsis. At t = 2, where F and V meet, the orbit becomes a parabola and escapes; beyond that it is a hyperbola. After squaring (Bohlin's map) the eccentricity is exactly t/2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] gᵀS_tg = S_t; eigenvectors (1,1),(1,−1) ∀t > 0 (t = 0: S = I). Hooke eccentricity of S_t = 1 (t < 2) and S_t = −1 (t > 2, transverse axis on (1,1)): e_H² = 2c/(1+c), c = t/2 = cos θ | cosh φ; Wick form 1 − tan²(θ/2) → 1 + tanh²(φ/2); other family 1/e² + 1/e′² = 1. Table: t = 1.8165, 1.9.9871, 2.5 1.0541, 4 1.1547; e_H → √2. Bohlin (z ↦ z², Bull. Astr. 28 (1911) 113–119): focal conic with e_K = t/2 exactly (fit residual 1e−9), apsidal line 45° → 90°; F/√q = e_K + i b_K/a_K (elliptic), e^{±φ} = e_K ± b_K/a_K (hyperbolic); r_a/r_p = (1+e_K)/(1−e_K) = −((1+u)/(1−u))², u = F/√q (Cayley). Margin: S_t on (1,1)/√2 = 1 − t/2 = λ_min(S_t) = 1 − e_K = −2E r_p/μ (Kepler binding at fixed periapsis). Periapsis kick from a circle, v = k v_c: e = k² − 1, apsidal line and r_p fixed, escape k = √2 (⇔ t = 2). [N] 38 checks PASS. [A] 45° tilt = the fixed apsidal axis of the animation's normalized norm conic (q-normalized coordinates).
concepts.formula: e_H² = 2t/(t+2); e_K = t/2; F/√q = e_K + i·b/a; margin = 1 − t/2
pitfalls: The F/V real line is in the eigenvalue plane, the apsidal line in phase space (TAA Lemma 161, correction 5).
r_a/r_p ≠ F/V; e ≠ tanh φ (TAA Lemma 161, correction 6).
Definite energy is eroded by the kick, not produced by it (TAA Lemma 161, correction 9).

Hurwitz order: #norm n = 24σ(n), n odd. B = (−1,−11)_ℚ (ramified at 11, ∞), maximal order O = ℤ⟨1, i, (1+j)/2, i(1+j)/2⟩, norm form Q ⊕ Q with Q = x² + xy + 3y²; θ_O = 1 + (12/5)Σ(σ(n) − 11σ(n/11))qⁿ + (8/5) η(z)²η(11z)² (n ≤ 300, exact). [C] Eichler 1954 Arch. Math. 5 355–366 (Brandt/basis problem; bibliographic). [A] 'definite energy' (TAA Lemma 161) ↔ definite quaternion algebra (compact quotient).

concepts.name: Gauss half: quadratic character, (p ± 1)/2 and the (p + 1)/4 square-root formula
concepts.plain: Every odd prime p splits the nonzero residues into (p − 1)/2 squares and (p − 1)/2 non-squares; the quadratic character (x/p) records which. For an elliptic curve y² = f(x), a_p is minus the sum of these characters, and its value mod p is a Gauss-half power.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: a_p = −Σ_x (f(x)/p) for y² = f(x); Hasse: a_p ≡ coefficient of x^{p−1} in f^{(p−1)/2} mod p. For p ≡ 3 mod 4, (p + 1)/4 is an integer and √a = a^{(p+1)/4} mod p (691 → 173). y² = x³ − x: a_p = −2, 6, 2 for p = 5, 13, 17; a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, so N₆₉₁ = 692. The Gauss halves see only the coherent H¹(E, 𝒪), i.e. a_p mod p; the bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p needs positivity (Castelnuovo/Hodge index). TAA Lemma 150 Prop 3.1 (THM+NUM): verified for p = 3,5,7,11,13,17,29,37,41,691; 70,563 square roots a^{(p+1)/4} and a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, p < 2000. The half records a_p mod p (Hasse invariant = Frobenius on coherent H¹); the bound needs positivity (TAA Lemma 150 Thm 2.2).
pitfalls: a_p mod p is phase-type information; it does not give the size bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
The ½ of (p ± 1)/2 is a counting half; relating it to the half-density ½ is an analogy.

concepts.name: Hilbert reciprocity at 2: the odd halves become sign bits
concepts.plain: At odd primes the halves (p − 1)/2 count squares; at 2 the corresponding quantities ε(u) = (u − 1)/2 and ω(u) = (u² − 1)/8 are sign bits. Hilbert reciprocity says the sign at 2 is fixed by the odd places and ∞. This is phase information, not positivity.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: (−1/p) = (−1)^{ε(p)}, (2/p) = (−1)^{ω(p)}. 2-adic Hilbert symbol: for a = 2^α u, b = 2^β v with u, v odd units, (a,b)₂ = (−1)^{ε(u)ε(v) + αω(v) + βω(u)} (Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III, Thm 1). Product formula ∏ᵥ (a,b)ᵥ = 1 over all places including ∞ ⇒ the 2-adic sign is determined by the odd places and ∞; it is a restatement of quadratic reciprocity with both supplementary laws. ℚ₂^×/squares has order 8; ℤ₂^×/squares = {±1, ±5} has order 4: two sign bits, ε (sign of −1) and ω (the √2 / χ₈ bit). Checked: product formula holds for 3000 random pairs |a|, |b| ≤ 5000; ε, ω for u = 1, 3, 5, 7: (0,0), (1,1), (0,1), (1,0). Phase data (Ax3), ghost-blind: Davenport–Heilbronn shares the same reciprocity.
numbers: Serre III Thm 1 formula vs PARI hilbert: 3000/3000
product formula 300/300 and the 2-adic unit-symbol table re-checked (Nov 2026); label unchanged

concepts.plain: The cusp scattering coefficient has modulus one on the critical line — true with or without RH.

concepts.name: Fundamental domain of SL₂(ℤ): elliptic (CM points), parabolic (cusp), hyperbolic (closed geodesics)
concepts.plain: The modular surface has two cone points, one cusp and many closed geodesics: the three kinds of motion seen on the quotient.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Elliptic points i (stabilizer ⟨S⟩) and ρ = e^{2πi/3} (⟨ST⟩) = CM points of discriminant −4, −3; one cusp (0 = S·∞ ~ i∞ for SL₂(ℤ); for Γ₀(N) the cusps 0 and ∞ are distinct, swapped by the Fricke involution); hyperbolic classes ↔ closed geodesics of length 2 log ε (Selberg's primes). Interior: Δ ≥ 0 (selberg_eigenvalue_mass_shell); cusp: unitary scattering φ (eisenstein_resonances_rho_half); CM points: Epstein/Hecke (epstein). The cusp ties them: its constant term carries ζ.

concepts.name: Kepler: LRL vector closes so(4) = su(2) ⊕ su(2) for E < 0, so(3,1) for E > 0, e(3) at E = 0
concepts.plain: The hidden symmetry of the hydrogen atom switches type with the sign of the energy, as the conic does.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Kustaanheimo–Stiefel quaternion lift: x = q i q̄ (Hopf map S³ → S², |x| = |q|²) with the bilinear U(1) constraint turns 3D Kepler at energy E into the 4D isotropic oscillator with ω² = −E/2; E < 0 real ω (rotation), E > 0 inverted oscillator (boost) — the Wick rotation; the commutant of the constraint in u(4) is u(2)⊕u(2) ⊃ su(2)⊕su(2) = so(4)
concepts.plain: Squaring a quaternion turns the Kepler problem in 3D into a perfectly round oscillator in 4D. Bound orbits become ordinary oscillations and unbound ones become an upside-down oscillator, which is the same switch as a Wick rotation.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] KS (J. reine angew. Math. 218 (1965) 204–219): x = q i q̄, fibre q ↦ q e^{iα}; dx kills the fibre, and on the horizontal space (⟨q i, q′⟩ = 0) dx = 2|q| × isometry (5e−10). With ds = dt/r: q″ = −ω²q, ω² = −E/2, |q′|² + ω²|q|² = μ/2 (coupling-constant metamorphosis; ΔE 1e−10, Kepler ẍ = −μx/r³ to 4e−7). E > 0: inverted oscillator → hyperbola (2e−6). 2D case = Levi-Civita/Bohlin z ↦ z² (TAA Lemma 161): e_K = e_H²/(2 − e_H²). u(4) (16 generators) ∩ commutant of the constraint = 8-dim u(2)⊕u(2), derived algebra 6 = su(2)⊕su(2) ≅ so(4) (bound Kepler); the two u(1) = constraint and oscillator H. [A] J. W. McGreevy. Ghost-blind (archimedean).
pitfalls: The 4D oscillator symmetry is U(4); only the su(2)⊕su(2) commuting with the constraint descends to Kepler.
Spelling: Kustaanheimo–Stiefel.

concepts.name: Legendre ↔ Fourier: stationary phase, half-density amplitude, Maslov phase
concepts.plain: The Fourier transform of a wave is, to leading order, its Legendre transform in the phase, a half-density in the amplitude, and a quarter-turn sign for each concave direction.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ∫e^{i(S(x)−px)}dx ≈ √(2π)|S″(x_p)|^{−½} e^{−iS*(p)} e^{iπ sgn S″/4}, S′(x_p) = p, S*(p) = p x_p − S(x_p) (critical-value Legendre transform); exact for quadratic S (Fresnel). Tangent of slope p meets the y-axis at S − xS′ = −S*(p): the intercepts give the phase; the half-density |dx|^{½} → |dp|^{½} gives the amplitude |S″|^{−½}; the Maslov factor records the Hessian signature and jumps at caustics (S″ = 0), where stationary phase fails (Airy; TAA Lemma 153 NUM). TAA Lemma 153 NUM: rel. err 0.012 (λ=20), 0.003 (λ=80), both signs. e^{−iπ/4} = √(1/i) is the factor in ϑ(−1/τ) = √(τ/i)ϑ(τ) (TAA Lemma 151; 9e−17). Riemann–Siegel θ(t) = (t/2)log(t/2π) − t/2 − π/8 + 1/(48t) + … (NUM); −π/8 as a Maslov-type phase is Heuristic.
pitfalls: Intercepts give the phase, not the half-density; the amplitude comes from the curvature S″ (TAA Lemma 153, correction 15).
Hörmander / Guillemin–Sternberg: bibliographic data only (unopened).

concepts.name: Half representations of SL(2,F_p): p+4 irreps of dims 1, p, p+1 ((p−3)/2 of them), p−1 ((p−1)/2), and two each of dims (p+1)/2 and (p−1)/2 — the induced rep from the quadratic (Legendre) character splits in half, with unipotent character values (1 ± √(εp))/2 and (−1 ± √(εp))/2, ε = (−1/p) (quadratic Gauss sum); needs F_p a field — the precise place where (p ± 1)/2 separates primes from odd composites
concepts.plain: Over the field with p elements, SL(2) has exactly two pairs of 'half-size' representations, of dimensions (p+1)/2 and (p−1)/2, and their characters carry the square-root Gauss sum. This needs p to be prime. For hydrogen, (n ± 1)/2 appears for every n, so it does not single out primes.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N] p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13: Σ dim² = p(p²−1); the unipotent class sum on Ind_B^G(Legendre) has eigenvalues giving χ(u) = (1 ± √(εp))/2 with multiplicity (p+1)/2 each; second orthogonality Σ|χ(u)|² = 2p. [C] Fulton–Harris §5.2 (table via Braun–Nebe, from Dornhoff Thm 38.1: ξ₁,₂(c) = ½(1 ± √(εq)), η₁,₂(c) = ½(−1 ± √(εq))). For composite n, SL(2,ℤ/n) = Π SL(2,ℤ/p^k) (CRT): reps are tensor products, no new n-halves. [T] Hydrogen (j,j), j = (n−1)/2, Casimir ((n−1)/2)((n+1)/2) for every n; odd n ⇔ integer j (parity, cf. hilbert_reciprocity_at_2). L is not 'the prime', A′ not ±1 (vectors, |j₊| = |j₋|). [H] per-prime, phase data ⇒ ghost-blind (DH shares the local quadratic characters).
pitfalls: The (p+1)/2 reps are halves of a principal series, not cuspidal; the (p−1)/2 are halves of the discrete series.
Ghost-blind: local quadratic data.

concepts.name: Yoshida window positivity
concepts.plain: For test functions supported in a small enough window, Weil positivity holds unconditionally.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Yoshida: W ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ small window; TAA Lemma 10 window ≤ log 3. Below ghost onsets, so ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 153: CC21 credit Yoshida (ASPM 21, 1992, 281–325) with W∞(f) ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ (1/2,2), f̂(±i/2) = 0, i.e. |log x| < log 2 (before the prime 2).
pitfalls: Unconditional windows never reach ghost onset.
Atlas window ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) vs CC21/Yoshida (1/2, 2) ↔ log 2: different statements/normalizations, not reconciled here.

concepts.name: Λ = 0 exactly for every finite product of ≥ 2 strictly Hasse degree-2 factors at distinct primes; (a) infinitely many non-real zeros for all t < 0 (Kronecker close pairs + local Rouché on F + sF″; Bohr + Hurwitz), (b) real-rooted for t ≥ 0 (Pólya 1927, Laguerre–Pólya class)
concepts.plain: Zeros from different primes come arbitrarily close because the logarithms of primes are rationally independent, which is unique factorisation. Running the flow backward makes every such pair collide, so the product sits exactly at threshold 0, whatever the a_p are. This is a statement on the local unitarity line, not GRH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Λ = 0 exactly for every finite product of ≥ 2 strictly Hasse degree-2 factors at distinct primes; (a) infinitely many non-real zeros for all t < 0 (Kronecker close pairs + local Rouché on F + sF″; Bohr + Hurwitz), (b) real-rooted for t ≥ 0 (Pólya 1927, Laguerre–Pólya class)
concepts.formula: collision t_c ≈ −d²/8; F_{−s} = F + sF″ + O(s²)
concepts.uncertain: No exact reference found; the method is close to Csordas–Smith–Varga and Dobner (possibly folklore). Hasse-level, not GRH.

concepts.name: One cusp, three readings: orbifold, Tate curve, archimedean monodromy
concepts.plain: Closing the cone angle 2π/m of the triangle orbifolds S²(2,3,m) runs from the Platonic solids (m = 3,4,5, Euler characteristic 2/|G|) through the flat case m = 6 to the modular orbifold at m = ∞, whose cusp is a pseudosphere horn of area 2π with unipotent holonomy T = 1+N, N² = 0. Arithmetically the cusp of X(1) is the Tate-curve degeneration (multiplicative reduction, nonzero N). At good primes Frobenius is semisimple and elliptic of trace a_p/√p; the inert value a_p = 0 is the order-2 point i, and the Hasse edge is a scalar, not a unipotent element. At the archimedean place an operator N playing the role of the logarithm of monodromy exists for local factors (Consani). On the modular surface the Riemann zeros appear as scattering resonances at Re s = 1/4, outside self-adjoint control. A polarized (N, log-Frobenius) package on a global cohomology would give Weil positivity; this is conjectural and RH is not proved.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: One cusp, three readings: orbifold, Tate curve, archimedean monodromy

concepts.name: Push–shear balance: ∫(τ/2)² − ∫|H°|² = ½B with B = ∫(Δu)² − ∫|Hess u|² = ∮[κ(u_n²+u_s²) − 2u_s∂_s u_n] (corner terms on polygons); 0 on ℝ², ½∫K|∇u|² on closed surfaces (Bochner)
concepts.plain: Over a whole surface the isotropic and shear parts of a Hessian balance exactly; any surplus is a boundary or curvature term.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Quartet capacity: which real Lie algebras carry an off-line quartet {±δ ± iγ}: none in so(4) or in sl₂⊕sl₂ on ℝ²⊕ℝ²; yes in so(2,2) on ℝ²⊗ℝ² (a_i + b_j), sp(4,ℝ) ≅ so(3,2) and sl₂ℂ on ℂ²; Krein collision in sp(4,ℝ): only opposite signatures leave the axis — the real form of the frame group does not decide ghosts
concepts.plain: An off-line zero shows up as a group of four eigenvalues. Whether a symmetry group can produce such quartets depends on the representation, not on whether the group is compact; inside the 4D symplectic group they appear exactly when two oscillations of opposite energy sign collide.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N] random generators: quartet fractions 0, 0,.394,.354, 1.0; boost 0.3 ⊗ rotation 2 gives ±0.3 ± 2i exactly. Krein (sp(4,ℝ)): equal frequencies, coupling.05: opposite signs max|Re|.025, same 4e−17; instability band ω₂ ∈ [.951, 1.050]. so(2,2) = stabilizer of a vector in so(3,2) (dim 6, Killing (4,2)). concepts.name: Hill topology of the Weil form sees only signature events, not Routh quartets
concepts.plain: {Z_L < 0} on the unit sphere is homotopic to S^{n₋−1}. For DH, L* = 3.875 is the birth of two antipodal caps, the L1-type neck opening is at L = 4.025 (n₋ = 2), and the quartet at 4.775 changes nothing. DH on 4.025–4.625 is the twin of L4 below μ_R: indefinite but Krein-rescued. ζ: empty to L = 8, lowest critical level 4.9e-11.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hill topology of the Weil form sees only signature events, not Routh quartets. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: ξ is the global product over places: Λ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2)·ζ(s) = ∏_v ζ_v(s); the archimedean factor is the partition function of a continuum, each Euler factor (1 − p^{−s})^{−1} a one-mode boson at energy log p; the functional equation comes from the adelic Poisson summation and the product formula (Tate 1950)
concepts.plain: The completed zeta function is a product of one local factor per place: a continuum partition function at ∞ and a single bosonic mode at energy log p for each prime. The functional equation is the product formula. This makes the ingredients thermodynamic, not the positivity. [Cited]
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: ξ is the global product over places: Λ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2)·ζ(s) = ∏_v ζ_v(s); the archimedean factor is the partition function of a continuum, each Euler factor (1 − p^{−s})^{−1} a one-mode boson at energy log p; the functional equation comes from the adelic Poisson summation and the product formula (Tate 1950). Tate’s thesis: local zeta integrals at every place, global zeta integral over the idèles; Λ(s) = Λ(1 − s) from Poisson summation on the adèles and |x| = ∏_v |x|_v = 1 on ℚ^×. This makes the ingredients of ξ thermodynamic (one partition function per place); it does not supply the positivity, which is the missing global statement. Sources: TAA research notes, 4 Nov 2026.
pitfalls: Ghost-blind: Davenport–Heilbronn has the same Γ factor and functional equation; only the Euler product (one boson per prime) separates them, and neither the product structure nor the functional equation implies positivity of the Weil form.

concepts.name: CM case: the Hasse triangle is Fermat's two-squares triangle
concepts.plain: For y² = x³ − x (CM by Z[i]) the Hasse triangle at p ≡ 1 mod 4 has integer legs 2a, 2b with a² + b² = p, and its angle is the argument of a Gaussian prime; at p ≡ 3 mod 4, a_p = 0 and α_p/√p = ±i. All Frobenius elements lie in one field Q(i), so a coherent family of local i's exists, yet RH for this L-function is open: local coherence is not the missing piece.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CM case: the Hasse triangle is Fermat's two-squares triangle
numbers: checked for all p < 2·10⁴ (1136 primes ≡ 3 mod 4 with a_p = 0)

concepts.name: Split/inert duality for a CM curve (32a1)
concepts.plain: For y² = x³ − x one character, χ₄(p), decides both properties. Split primes have i ∈ Q_p, are ordinary, and have the angle of a Gaussian prime, equidistributed for the uniform measure (Hecke), not Sato–Tate. Inert primes have i ∉ Q_p, are supersingular (Deuring), and have a_p = 0 and angle exactly 90°; there Frobenius satisfies π² = −p and anticommutes with complex multiplication, so π/√p is a 90° rotation. The two classes are the fibres of the Galois character of Q(i), a duality rather than an isomorphism. The same holds for every CM curve, and RH for their L-functions is open.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Split/inert duality for a CM curve (32a1)
concepts.formula: χ₄(p)=+1: a_p = 2a, a²+b² = p, θ_p = arg(a+bi); χ₄(p)=−1: a_p = 0, π² = −p, π∘[i] = [−i]∘π; CM angle law ½δ_{π/2} + (1/2π)dθ

concepts.plain: Each prime's Frobenius is a rotation of the sphere, so it has a cone angle. The flow sharpens the cone backward until it becomes a cusp, exactly at the local Newman time. Forward it relaxes toward a half-turn. Past the cusp the rotation becomes a boost.

concepts.name: Johnson–Lippmann operator: a spin-dependent Laplace–Runge–Lenz operator commuting with the Dirac–Coulomb Hamiltonian
concepts.plain: For the relativistic hydrogen atom there is a first-order operator, built from spin and the Coulomb direction, that commutes with the energy and anticommutes with Dirac's K. It plays the role of a supercharge: the hidden symmetry made one level more fundamental. Analogy only for RH.

concepts.name: Kaluza–Klein circles, the infinite torus, and adelic solenoids
concepts.plain: A Kaluza–Klein circle gives a complex structure on its charged modes only. The pseudosphere is a warped circle of radius e^{−u}, and only the neutral (constant-term) mode reaches the cusp, where the scattering coefficient Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s) carries ζ. The per-prime phases p^{−it} fill the infinite torus ∏S¹, the dual of the multiplicative group of positive rationals. That torus differs from the solenoid 𝔸/ℚ, which is the dual of the additive rationals; the p-adic solenoid is the inverse limit of S¹ under z ↦ z^p. The product formula makes ℚ^× preserve Haar measure, so the compatible structure is an invariant measure, not an invariant metric. The expected dynamical system for Spec ℤ (three-dimensional, orbits of length log p) has not been constructed.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Kaluza–Klein circles, the infinite torus, and adelic solenoids

concepts.name: The 1/24 identities (1/24 = −ζ(−1)/2, η²⁴ = Δ, Θ_Leech) and the verdict: in Weil’s form the 1/24 acts only through the weight
concepts.plain: The 1/24 is real and global: 1/24 = −ζ(−1)/2, the exponent of q in η, and η²⁴ = Δ, of weight 12 = 24·½. It is ζ(2), an absolutely convergent Euler product, carried to s = −1 by the functional equation. But in the window model of Weil’s form the 1/24 enters only through the Γ-factor (the weight). Lowering the weight below 12 breaks positivity almost at once (a one-sided edge), but that edge is generic: 11a1, with weight 2 and no 1/24 in this sense, sits on the same kind of edge, even tighter. For ζ the 1/12 = B₂/2 enters only through Stirling’s 1/(12z) term, which is the same for every Γ-factor and identical for Davenport–Heilbronn, so it cannot tell a true zero from a planted ghost. Verdict: the 1/24 does not supply the positive metric on the primitive part.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The 1/24 identities (1/24 = −ζ(−1)/2, η²⁴ = Δ, Θ_Leech) and the verdict: in Weil’s form the 1/24 acts only through the weight. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).

concepts.name: Weight ladder (modular weights)
concepts.plain: Modular forms come in weights; at each rung the Eisenstein series E_k is the reference. A “stratification” of modular structures is this ladder.

concepts.name: On E×E over ℂ: ⋆² = 1, ⋆ = γ₅ on spinors (up to sign), Λ⁺ = ℝω ⊕ Re Λ^{2,0}, primitive (1,1) = ASD; Hodge index = only SD (1,1) class is ω; τ = (1/12π²)∫(|W⁺|² − |W⁻|²) = 0, blind to RH
concepts.plain: Over the complex numbers, the polarization is the self-dual (right-handed) direction and the primitive classes are anti-self-dual. Curvature produces the topological signature through its Weyl part, but that signature is zero for every such surface and does not see Frobenius.

concepts.name: Euler factors as passive but lossy sections
concepts.plain: Each normalised Euler factor (1 - p^(-1/2))/(1 - p^(-s)) is contractive on the half-plane right of the critical line, and so is its sign-flipped version, so per-factor passivity cannot tell zeta from controls; the product of the normalisations tends to zero, so the cascade dissipates everything, and no Euler factor is lossless on the line.

concepts.name: The Galois deformation obstruction is a second-order curvature
concepts.plain: Deforming a flat connection by εu gives curvature ε·du + (ε²/2)[u∧u]; staying flat to second order needs the cup-bracket [u∪u] to vanish in H². For Galois representations this is the obstruction class in H²(G_Q,S, ad ρ) of Mazur's deformation theory, and for Kähler groups Goldman–Millson show the deformation space is the quadratic cone it cuts out. For modular representations the relevant obstructions vanish, so the Galois side stays flat: it cannot carry a curvature with a sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The Galois deformation obstruction is a second-order curvature. Sources: Mazur, Deforming Galois representations (1989); Goldman and Millson, Publ. Math. IHES 67 (1988); Diamond, Flach and Guo, Ann. Sci. ENS (2004).

concepts.name: The critical-line wave: Hardy Z and the Riemann–Siegel phase
concepts.plain: On the critical line ζ(1/2+it) = Z(t)e^{−iθ(t)} with Z real, so the real and imaginary parts are one real wave seen through a rotating phase. Each simple zero is a sign change of Z, so the phase of ζ jumps by π. The mean of Re ζ on the line is 1; Gram's law is the separate statement (−1)^n Z(g_n) > 0 at Gram points, and it fails first at n = 126. Sign changes equal N(T) for all T iff RH holds and all zeros are simple. Under RH, (Z′/Z)′ = −Σ(t−γ)^{−2} − (log G)″, which forbids wrong-sign extrema wherever the sum dominates (checked for 5.7 ≤ t ≤ 400).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The critical-line wave: Hardy Z and the Riemann–Siegel phase

concepts.name: Weil operator, star and the eighth turn
concepts.plain: On weight-one H^1, C = i^(p-q) is a complex structure, star = C composed with conjugation is antilinear with square -1 and commutes with C, so the quaternion triple is (i, star, i star), not (C, star, C star). The Deligne-torus element h(e^{i pi/4}) is a real square root of C (eighth turn) adding no new structure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Weil operator, star and the eighth turn. Sources: arXiv:2204.02714; arXiv:1001.1621.

concepts.name: E₂* as the derivative of the Kronecker limit (cusp-scattering footprint)
concepts.plain: E₂'s modular anomaly is the derivative of the √y piece of the Eisenstein series' constant term, i.e. a trace of the cusp's continuous spectrum.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] ∂_z log(√y|η(z)|²) = (πi/12)·E₂*(z), E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) (from (1/2πi) d log Δ = E₂, Zagier Prop. 7, and ∂_z ½ log y = −i/(4y)). Kronecker's first limit formula: E(z,s) = Σ′ y^s/|mz+n|^{2s} = π/(s−1) + 2π(γ − log 2 − log(√y|η|²)) + O(s−1). Constant term 2ζ(2s)[y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s}], φ = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s) (TAA Lemma 153 Birman–Krein). Ghost-blind (symmetry layer). [N] identity to 2e−62 (3 points); limit formula 3.9e−21 at ε = 1e−20; φ identity 1.1e−61. The other LLM's IHO ↔ E₂-anomaly 'inverse-area' bridge: no support (arXiv 2012.09875, 2412.09274 opened: no modular forms).
pitfalls: Ghost-blind: says nothing about MP4.
No IHO/E₂ bridge in the cited physics papers.

concepts.plain: One prime survives a definite amount of backward heat flow; a product of two primes survives none, because near-coincident zeros collide.

concepts.name: The lattice whose axes are the normalized Euler factors sees only local Hasse: it is blind to Davenport–Heilbronn, and the archimedean factor is indispensable
concepts.plain: The orthogonal sum of the binary forms (1, −a/√q, 1) of the normalized Euler factors is positive definite for L(11a) at 428/428 good primes below e⁸ (Hasse/Deligne), while ζ·ζ at t = 0 sits on the local wall at every prime ((x − y)², discriminant 0, degenerate). Davenport–Heilbronn’s pseudo-factors (1, −a(p), 1), a(p) ∈ {±1, ±0.284}, are all positive definite, so local positivity cannot separate it from ζ. Gram forms built from local data alone, without the archimedean factor, are indefinite at every L (n₋ from 27 to 220 for ζ on L = 1.5–8).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The lattice whose axes are the normalized Euler factors sees only local Hasse: it is blind to Davenport–Heilbronn, and the archimedean factor is indispensable. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026.

concepts.name: The Maass–Selberg norm of truncated Eisenstein series is positive unconditionally, so cusp positivity does not see RH
concepts.plain: −φ′/φ(½ + it) = 4Σ(1 − β)/|1 + 2it − ρ|² − 4/(1 + 4t²) with β < 1 gives a positive Maass–Selberg norm without RH; the Davenport–Heilbronn analogue is positive too. Positivity at the cusp is ghost-blind.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The Maass–Selberg norm of truncated Eisenstein series is positive unconditionally, so cusp positivity does not see RH. Sources: TAA research notes, 1 Nov 2026.

concepts.name: Unique factorization = non-resonance of the prime torus; Euler product = separable Bohr lift
concepts.plain: For a multiplicative monoid of positive reals, unique factorization holds exactly when the logs of its atoms are rationally independent, i.e. the torus flow with frequencies log p has no resonance (Kronecker: the line is dense; Bohr–Jessen value distribution). A Dirichlet series has an Euler product with multiplicative coefficients exactly when its Bohr lift to the prime torus factorizes into one-coordinate pieces. Davenport–Heilbronn’s −DH′/DH puts 32–70% of its weight (L = 3–8) on non-prime-powers, i.e. on couplings between prime oscillators.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Unique factorization = non-resonance of the prime torus; Euler product = separable Bohr lift. Sources: TAA research notes, Oct 2026; Bohr–Jessen 1930 doi:10.1007/BF02547516.

concepts.name: Beta integral, Maslov dequantization and entropy
concepts.plain: As hbar -> 0, hbar log B(a/hbar, b/hbar) tends to -(a+b) times the Shannon entropy of the split a:b, with an O(hbar log hbar) correction from Stirling. The integral collapses onto the saddle x* = a/(a+b) of a log x + b log(1-x), a max-plus problem, and the Beta(a/hbar, b/hbar) law satisfies a large-deviation principle with rate (a+b) KL(x*||x). With four points fixed, the Koba-Nielsen integral is the Beta function (Veneziano), and its high-energy fixed-angle limit is the same saddle. The Sato-Tate law is Beta(3/2,3/2), with constant pi/8 = Gamma(3/2)^2/Gamma(3). The CM split-prime law is Beta(1/2,1/2), with constant pi. This concerns the Gamma factors and the a_p distributions, not the zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Beta integral, Maslov dequantization and entropy
concepts.formula: hbar log B(a/hbar, b/hbar) = a log(a/(a+b)) + b log(b/(a+b)) + (hbar/2) log hbar + hbar(log(2pi)/2 - log(ab/(a+b))/2) + O(hbar^2)

concepts.name: The χ = −1 "effective pole" is half of ζ’s pole, entering through ζ_ℚ(i) = ζ·L(χ₄)
concepts.plain: Split the prime atoms by the character χ₄. The atoms with χ₄ = −1 equal one half of (odd-n ζ prime part − χ₄ prime part), an exact identity. They carry half of ψ(x)’s main term, i.e. half the pole, while the χ₄ part has no main term. On windows the cancellation is only approximate, because it comes from a main term (the prime number theorem in progressions), not from a symmetry.

concepts.core: The χ = −1 "effective pole" is half of ζ’s pole, entering through ζ_ℚ(i) = ζ·L(χ₄). From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).

concepts.name: Φ is not in Newman's class 𝒫 (unconditional), so b₀ < ∞; the Lee–Yang property of Φ is RH
concepts.plain: Newman's sufficient condition (an even potential growing like a polynomial) fails for Φ because Φ decays doubly exponentially. Lee–Yang for Φ is therefore not available from that theorem.

The single-spin Lee–Yang property of Φ (all zeros of ∫Φ(u)e^{hu}du = ¼ξ(½+h/2) on iℝ) is a Restatement of RH; by continuity at J → 0 the many-spin ferromagnetic version fails exactly when the single-spin one does, so it adds no information (see multispin_adds_nothing).

concepts.plain: Scaling the primon energies by V^{−1/3} gives an exact ultrarelativistic-type equation of state PV = U/3, with the Hagedorn point at x = 1. Every cycle encloses the same area in TS and PV (ellipse: 0.0457797069 both), and ∂(T,S)/∂(P,V) = 1. This is the literal TS → PV symplectomorphism. It holds for any kernel, so it is RH-blind.

concepts.name: Sector map w = e^{iπs/2}
concepts.plain: Mapping the critical strip to a 90° sector puts the critical line on the 45° ray; the functional equation becomes w ↦ i/w.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: arg w = πσ/2: strip edges σ = 0, 1 → rays 90° apart, critical line → the 45° ray. s ↦ 1 − s is w ↦ i/w (reflection in the 45° ray composed with |w| ↦ 1/|w|; fixed points ±e^{iπ/4}), not a reflection (TAA Lemma 152, correction 6); the reflection in the 45° ray is s ↦ 1 − s̄, w ↦ i w̄ (NUM 4.5e−28, 4.0e−28). In this picture the 45° ray is the critical line, not a null ray.

concepts.name: Contact form and Legendre surface of the window equation of state
concepts.plain: On five-dimensional space with coordinates U, S, l, T, P the form dU - T dS + P dl is contact. The computed equation of state is a Legendre surface which, because the heat capacity is a strictly positive variance, is a global graph over both (T, l) and (S, l). Legendre transforms to F, G and H are strict contactomorphisms; the G chart fails exactly where the isothermal pressure slope vanishes.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Contact form and Legendre surface of the window equation of state. Sources: Arnold, Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics.

concepts.name: The m = 1 plus-space coefficient is ∝ ζ(½ + 2it)/ζ(1 + 4it): ζ’s zeros on its own line are zeros of a Fourier coefficient, which the norm sees only squared
concepts.plain: On the unitary axis the first coefficient of the weight-½ Eisenstein series is c₁ ∝ ζ(½ + 2it)/ζ(1 + 4it); it vanishes at t = γ/2 (6·10⁻⁹ contribution at γ₁/2). The truncated norm contains it only as |c₁|² times a positive weight, an upper bound on |ζ(½ + 2it)|. An off-line zero ρ₀ would make c₁ vanish at the non-unitary point S = (ρ₀ + ½)/2, where no norm exists: the positivity is blind to it.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Finite Guinand–Weil dictionary for truncated Weil forms
concepts.plain: Each Galerkin vector of the truncated Weil form corresponds to a band-limited test function whose zero sum equals the quadratic form exactly; the omitted archimedean tail is a totally positive increment, giving two-sided certification with an explicit budget.

concepts.name: The 45-degree flip is a real structure, not a star
concepts.plain: The 45-degree flip z -> i conj(z) is antilinear with square +1 (a reflection fixing the 45-degree ray, conjugate to complex conjugation by e^{i pi/4}); on a single complex line every antilinear map squares to a positive number, so no quaternionic structure lives on one eigenvalue line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The 45-degree flip is a real structure, not a star.

concepts.name: The factorial of one half and the Fourier quarter-turn
concepts.plain: Gamma(1/2) = sqrt(pi) and (1/2)! = sqrt(pi)/2. The Gaussian e^{-pi x^2} is fixed by the Fourier transform, F^4 = 1, and the Hermite functions are its eigenfunctions with eigenvalues 1, -i, -1, i. Poisson summation for the Gaussian gives the theta inversion, and its Mellin transform gives xi(s) = xi(1-s). This explains the symmetry s <-> 1-s, not the critical line. The archimedean term alone is positive only for support below 0.2143; with the pole (or on the pole-free space) the threshold is 0.7432.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The factorial of one half and the Fourier quarter-turn

concepts.name: Frame and clock invariance of Krein data at L4
concepts.plain: At L4 (μ = 0.01) the rotating-frame linearization over one synodic period equals the inertial-frame monodromy to 5e−12: the Floquet multipliers and Krein signs are identical, and only the picture changes (a potential maximum stabilized by Coriolis versus a tidal saddle). A time change dt = r₁^α ds rescales the eigenvalues by r₁^α at the fixed point (exactly 1 at L4/L5) and leaves the number of real pairs and every Krein sign unchanged. No frame or clock makes positivity easier; some only make it visible.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.plain: The angle of each prime comes from the Galois group of Q through the Frobenius element; its eigenvalues are algebraic integers and, after the Tate-twist normalization by p^(w/2), lie on the unit circle (Deligne). The étale fundamental group of Spec Z itself is trivial (Minkowski).

concepts.name: Gross-Zagier as rank-one positivity
concepts.plain: L'(E,1) L(E_D,1) equals a positive explicit constant times the Neron-Tate height of a Heegner point: positivity of one central derivative, equal to the length of one vector. It does not locate other zeros.

concepts.name: Window Weil form as jump kinetic energy minus a mass plus a pole
concepts.plain: For zeta the window form splits exactly as W = J - M I + Pole, with J a positive jump (log-Vladimirov) form from the arch and prime atoms, M = 2 sum Lambda(n) n^(-1/2) minus the arch value at 0, and Pole of inertia (1,1). Positivity forces at most one level of J below M. Zeta has exactly one (the constant mode) for all tested windows, and its second level sits only 2.8e-4 to 9e-10 above M (critical); controls have 22-198. For Davenport-Heilbronn, Delta and 11a1 the jump form is indefinite (signed coefficients), so this is a Lambda >= 0 property, not an RH mechanism; ghost-blind.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Window Weil form as jump kinetic energy minus a mass plus a pole. Sources: Haran 1990.

concepts.name: Möbius function as fermion parity of the primon gas
concepts.plain: With one boson and one fermion for every prime, μ(n) = (−1)^F on squarefree levels. The supercharge Q = Σ_p √(log p) b_p a_p† has Q² = 0 and {Q, Q†} = log n on level n, and the Witten index of level n is Σ_{d|n} μ(d) = δ_{n,1}. By P. Hall, μ(n) is the reduced Euler characteristic of the boundary of the simplex on the primes of n, so Möbius inversion is a ∂² = 0 statement.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Möbius function as fermion parity of the primon gas. Sources: Spector, Commun. Math. Phys. 127 (1990); Julia, Les Houches 1989 (Springer Proc. Phys. 47, 1990); Rota, Z. Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie 2 (1964).

concepts.name: Ruled quadric through a saddle: null lines, signature (1,1)

Its lines are null (zero proper time); proper time lives on the two-sheet hyperboloid. The mutual moment of two lines is symmetric, of constant sign within a ruling and zero across rulings, so no assignment of primes to lines reproduces Legendre symbols, which are antisymmetric on primes ≡ 3 mod 4.

concepts.name: Curvature routes to positivity are ghost-blind: flat Bochner remainder, flat prime graph, indefinite Λ² operator, fixed-sign Verblunsky metric
concepts.plain: Four ways of getting positivity from a curvature sign all fail. (1) The flat-translation Weitzenböck split W = Σ|c_n|‖(1 ∓ τ_{log n})f‖² + ℛ has a remainder ℛ that depends only on |c_n|, so it is identical for ζ and every sign flip, and it is hugely negative (λ_min(ℛ) ≈ −155 for ζ at window length 7, against λ_min(W) ≈ +1.6e−5). (2) The prime-translation graph is an abelian Cayley graph, hence Bakry–Émery/Ollivier flat, so no curvature gap. (3) The curvature operator on Λ² of the window space is indefinite even for genuine forms. (4) In Verblunsky coordinates the Kähler metric of −log det is a product of Poincaré disks, with fixed negative curvature for every positive Toeplitz form, so what separates genuine from fake is whether the path stays inside the disks, not a curvature sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Curvature routes to positivity are ghost-blind: flat Bochner remainder, flat prime graph, indefinite Λ² operator, fixed-sign Verblunsky metric. Sources: Klartag, Kozma, Ralli and Tetali, arXiv:1501.00516; Jeuris and Vandebril, KU Leuven report TW 660 (2015).

concepts.name: The only scaling-and-Fourier invariant Hermitian form on Tate’s two boundary numbers is hyperbolic or zero
concepts.plain: Fourier transform swaps f(0) and the integral of f. Unitary scaling multiplies them by opposite powers of |a|. The only Hermitian forms invariant under both are real multiples of the off-diagonal matrix. A nonzero multiple has signature (1, 1). The zero multiple is degenerate. The boundary does not supply a positive sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: b(f) = (f(0), integral f). b(Ff) = sigma b(f), b(U_a f) = diag(|a|^(-1/2), |a|^(1/2)) b(f), and F U_a = U_(1/a) F. Smearing by F on the log line multiplies b by diag(ev_0 F, ev_1 F), so Theta_F maps the entire Schwartz-Bruhat space into ker b if and only if F is in E0. Equivalently, b(Theta_F f) = 0 for every f if and only if ev_0 = ev_1 = 0. Checked symbolically: invariance under all positive scalings and under sigma forces the diagonal entries to vanish and the off-diagonal entry to be real. The Weil pole term is of this hyperbolic type. Finite-field graph pairings (q^(-n/2), q^(n/2)) obey the same diagonal law as discrete samples, not as Mellin moments.

concepts.name: Both parity sectors carry a constraint; the even test is not E0
concepts.plain: On a reflection-invariant finite Galerkin space whose even and odd blocks are invertible, B is positive semidefinite on E0 exactly when each sector passes the bordered test: negative index 0, or negative index 1 with q at most 0. The even test alone is not E0. The odd index seen in two runs is numerical.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: For an R-invariant finite Galerkin space with invertible sector blocks, B is at least 0 on E0(I) if and only if [n-(B_even) = 0, or n-(B_even) = 1 and q_even <= 0] and [n-(B_odd) = 0, or n-(B_odd) = 1 and q_odd <= 0]. This is the parent audit's Lemma 2. The reflection RF(u) = F(-u) commutes with B, because the symbol is even, and it commutes with P. Cosh is the even constraint and sinh is the odd constraint. In the A = 0.6 and A = 1 runs the odd block had negative index 0. That is numerical, not a general fact. Full-window W is a different question: if the even block has index 1 and is invertible, W_even is positive semidefinite if and only if q_even <= -1/2. If the odd block is positive definite, W_odd is positive semidefinite if and only if q_odd <= 1/2.
concepts.formula: B >= 0 on E0 iff both sectors pass: index 0, or index 1 and q <= 0
numbers: Odd-sector negative index 0 at A = 0.6 and A = 1 is numerical, uncertified, and not claimed in general.

concepts.tests: An estimate that uses only even tests does not see E0.

concepts.name: Purity as distortionless transmission: weight strata = attenuation classes
concepts.plain: On a perfect cable every frequency fades at the same rate; RH-type purity says every Frobenius eigenvalue has the same size, and rescaling by √q makes the fading disappear altogether.

concepts.core: Lossless = unitary (|φ| = 1 on the line; after the half-density gauge no attenuation) [T]. Distortionless = every mode shares one attenuation rate [T for the line]. Frobenius eigenvalues |α| = q^{w/2}: α^n decays/grows at rate (w/2) log q, so the weight strata (rings |z| = q^{−σ}) are attenuation classes; purity (one ring) = distortionless [Restatement for Frobenius]; dividing by q^{1/2} (half Tate twist, the e^{−αx} factor) turns distortionless into lossless [T]. For ζ (no Frobenius) this is an Analogy. DH off-line zeros = modes with another attenuation = distortion [R, TAA Lemma 144 overdamped ghost]. Hyperbolic side: characteristics x ± ct are the null lines of dx² − c²dt²; Wick rotation t → iτ makes it dx² + c²dτ² (OS link) — a different sign flip from C → −C in the LC energy (TAA Lemma 153, correction 30). concepts.name: One model form: a null conic, a timelike point, and a positive polar
concepts.plain: A single quadratic form on a plane can be indefinite, negative on one vector, and positive on the polar of that vector. The zero set is a conic. Drawn in an affine chart it is the parabola q = t squared over 4. That curve is the model discriminant conic. It is not a Hasse wall, not the parabolic wall, not the Routh wall, and not a sheet of Sigma. Focus and directrix are extra Euclidean structure on the chart.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: B(v, v) = v_T^2 - 4 v_Q v_Z. The null set Q = 0 is a smooth conic. The point h = (0:1:1) has Q(h) = -4. On its polar, Q = v_T^2 + 4 v_Z^2, which is positive definite. The axis span(h, x_infinity) has signature (1, 1), and x_infinity = (0:1:0) is null. Its polar is Z = 0, which contains x_infinity, so the complement is degenerate. Sylvester's law in this finite dimension: one negative square and Q(h, h) < 0 imply positivity on the polar. This is the shape the bordered criterion asks for. concepts.name: Prime torus in action-angle variables: H₀ = Σ k_p log p is linear in the actions, so KAM nondegeneracy fails and small divisors are RH-blind
concepts.plain: On the prime torus the angles are θ_p = t log p, the actions are the exponents k_p of n = Πp^{k_p} and the energy is log n: the Euler product is Liouville integrability of a free system whose Hamiltonian is linear in the actions, so Kolmogorov’s twist condition fails and KAM does not apply as stated; the archimedean factor and the pole are the only non-separable coupling. The small divisors |Σ k_p log p| for primes behave like random log-frequencies and the pigeonhole bound, with a Baker-type Diophantine lower bound; the Hilbert monoid {1 mod 4} has the exact resonance 9·49 = 21². Beurling systems that are non-resonant still fail positivity, so non-resonance is RH-blind.

concepts.name: Einstein–Cartan: spin enters as torsion
concepts.plain: In Einstein–Cartan theory the spin of matter couples to the torsion of a metric-compatible connection; torsion is algebraic (fixed pointwise by spin) and gives only a weak contact interaction. In the Lichnerowicz formula for a Dirac operator with skew torsion H the torsion enters as s·dH − 2s²‖H‖², which works against positivity. So 'a first-order operator whose square is the push, with spin entering through torsion' has no forced helpful sign for the torsion part.

Phys. 2 (1961) 212–221; Sciama, Recent Developments in General Relativity (1962) 415–439; Bismut, Math. Ann. 284 (1989) 681–699; Ferreira, Proc. Edinburgh Math. Soc. 56 (2013) 501–508, Thm. 2.1.

concepts.name: One log-gas and its frozen limit
concepts.plain: Under the de Bruijn-Newman backward heat flow, the zeros of H_t move by dz_k/dt = 2 sum_{j != k} 1/(z_k - z_j), the gradient flow of a logarithmic (Coulomb) energy. An off-line pair collides onto the real axis in finite time. RH is equivalent to Lambda = 0, i.e. every charge already on the axis at t = 0. The Hopf-Cole transform turns the heat equation into Hamilton-Jacobi in the hbar -> 0 limit, with a min-plus (Hopf-Lax) solution. Koba-Nielsen weights are 2D Coulomb-gas Boltzmann weights, and the Stieltjes equilibrium of charges in a Gaussian field sits at Hermite zeros, which the beta-Hermite ensemble freezes onto as beta grows. GUE pair correlation of zeros (conjectural) is the beta = 2 log-gas. The picture explains symmetry and statistics; it gives no positivity.
concepts.label: Analogy

Its spectrum λ = 2√p cos θ has the trivial eigenvalue p + 1 (the pole) and the Ramanujan/Kesten–McKay band |λ| ≤ 2√p, the analogue of a Hill region; at the band edge dλ/dθ = 0, the exact zero-velocity curve, and outside it θ is imaginary (evanescent, ghost-like). 70 supersingular 2-isogeny graphs (37 ≤ p ≤ 419) are all Ramanujan (max nontrivial |λ| = 2.8237 < 2√2); a discrete Morse count of a potential on them gives ≈ n/2 saddles, forced by χ = n − 3n/2. The local band is known (Deligne/Hasse); what is not local is the coherence of θ_p = γ log p across all p for one γ.

concepts.name: SU(2)×SU(2) as a compact 'product surface': SO(4) = (SU(2)×SU(2))/±1 acts on S³ = SU(2) by x ↦ g x h⁻¹, stabilizer of 1 = diagonal (conjugation, preserves trace = F+V); Peter–Weyl L²(G) = ⊕ V_π ⊗ V_π* is the compact analogue of Künneth; dictionary to Weil's C×C (Δ ↔ diagonal, Γ_F ↔ translate, Lefschetz ↔ trace, Hodge index ↔ Haar positivity, automatic for compact G)
concepts.plain: The four-dimensional rotation group is two copies of SU(2), one acting from the left and one from the right, so the 3-sphere behaves like a 'product' with a diagonal. That mirrors the curve-times-curve surface Weil used, and on a compact group the positivity Weil needed comes for free. The catch is that ζ's own frames are boosts, not rotations.
concepts.label: Analogy

concepts.name: A polar family shrinks to the null point at infinity, in two gauges
concepts.plain: Move the interior point from h = (0:1:1) toward x_infinity by h_s = (0:1:s), with s from 1 down toward 0. On that homogeneous representative, Q = -4s, which tends to 0. The same projective point, normalized to affine height q = 1/s, has Q = -4/s, which tends to minus infinity. Both statements are right. They are different normalizations. The sign stays negative for s > 0, and the projective limit is the null point x_infinity either way.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Q(0, 1, s) = -4s. The affine representative (0, 1/s, 1) has Q = -4/s. The ratio of the two numbers is the square of the scaling factor 1/s. On the polar v_Z = -s v_Q the form is v_T^2 + 4 s v_Q^2. Its level set equal to 1 is an ellipse. As s tends to 0 that ellipse lengthens toward the pair of lines v_T = ±1. The filled sublevel, the set where the form is at most 1, lengthens toward the strip |v_T| <= 1. The level set does not become the strip. At s = 0 the polar of x_infinity is the line Z = 0, which does not meet the affine chart. The conic is smooth at x_infinity: in the chart Q = 1 it is the parabola T^2 = 4Z. That point is not a cusp of the modular curve.

numbers: At s = 1 the two gauges agree at -4. At s = 0.05 they read -0.2 and -80. Same point, same sign, different scale.

pitfalls: Do not treat -4s and -4/s as the same measurement.
Do not say the level set becomes a strip. The filled sublevel does.

concepts.name: Anticipation law: the past fluctuation of the primes predicts the present one inside the Krein disk
concepts.plain: Split the window sequence as r = A + D + Φ: archimedean part, D = pole minus the prime-number-theorem main term (a zero-free positive-definite kernel), and Φ = the prime fluctuation (atoms minus main-term density), which by the explicit formula is the zero sum. Positivity at each step holds exactly when the next value lies in the Krein disk (centre predicted from the past, radius E). For ζ the share of each fluctuation already predicted by the past fluctuation is about 1 (band medians 0.98–1.01 for ℓ ≥ 4), and dropping the past fluctuation from the predictor pushes k out of the disk for ℓ ≥ 11. Conjecture: for genuine L-functions the Euler data predict the next fluctuation inside the disk uniformly, with sup|k| bounded away from 1. Taken for all steps this is equivalent to positivity, so it is circular as a proof unless a mechanism from the Euler product is found; a bound on Φ relative to E is von Koch/RH-strength. For GL(2) forms anticipation is never needed up to ℓ = 12.

concepts.name: Ramanujan's 691 as a degeneration of the pole line
concepts.plain: tau(n) = sigma_11(n) mod 691 follows from Ramanujan's identity 691 + 65520 sum sigma_11(n) x^n = 441 Q^3 + 250 R^2, since 691 divides the numerator of B_12 and zeta(-11) = 691/32760. Over the complex numbers the Eisenstein (pole) line is orthogonal to the cusp forms; mod 691 its constant term, half of zeta(-11), vanishes and the Eisenstein line collides with the cuspidal line (Mazur's Eisenstein line meeting Spec T). So 691 is where the null-line quotient breaks down integrally, not an instance of it. An exploratory test found no irregular-prime signature in the real Weil-form model, as expected: primes enter only through smooth weights log p / p^(k/2). In the p-adic Stickelberger form on (Z/p)^x the pole is the unique eigenvalue of valuation -1, and the radical mod p sits exactly at the k with p | B_k (checked for 182 primes 5..1097, 66 irregular). At 691 the k = 12 radical line is the weight-12 Eisenstein constant term up to a unit; a second line sits at k = 200. What degenerates is a weight-k Eisenstein line in the p-adic family, not the pole of zeta; positivity has no p-adic analogue, only non-degeneracy.
concepts.label: Analogy

concepts.name: Integrality instead of positivity (45-degree direction)
concepts.plain: On the RM wedge, positivity is lost but a support property survives through integrality: the product of the two real central charges is a nonzero integer. The zeta analogue would be a discreteness or integrality constraint on lambda = rho(1 - rho) that a complex lambda cannot meet. No candidate is known; recorded as a direction, not a result.

concepts.name: Route: Jacobi/Finsler geometry of xp as a positivity source
concepts.plain: Downgraded route: one-degree-of-freedom Jacobi metrics are flat (length = reduced action), the two-degree-of-freedom geometry is Finsler with a gauge-dependent curvature sign, and positive Jacobi curvature does not mean stability (the coupled regularized xp is chaotic while its flag curvature is mostly positive). It supplies no positivity source.
